Penny to quarter size hail fell in Oxford Borough and Cochranville in West Fallowfield Township. In Cochranville, the hail accumulated one to two inches deep and caused some minor damage to vegetation as it removed some leaves.
A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs in Exton (West Whiteland Township).

A severe thunderstorm dropped large hail across Woolwich Township. Eight large farms in the township suffered hail damage. Nearly one hundred percent of the eggplants were damaged. There was also considerable damage done to tomato plants and cubanelle pepper plants.

Severe thunderstorms dropped marble to quarter size hail across central Gloucester County from South Harrison Township east through Harrison Township, Mantua Township, Pitman Borough and Washington Township.
A series of severe thunderstorms dropped penny to quarter size hail across Franklin Township.

Thunderstorms moving across the same areas caused flash flooding in Mannington, Carney's Point and Pennsville Townships. In Mannington Township, flooding washed away a small bridge over a tributary creek to the Salem River. U.S. Route 40 was flooded along the Pennsville and Carney's Point Township line. In Carney Point Township, the YMCA was partially closed after flood waters reached the fitness center, locker rooms and pool. Dunn's Park was also flooded. In Pennsville Township, flooding reached into a few homes. Adjusted for hail contamination, Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 3 and 4 inches in the area. A rainfall total of 5 inches was estimated in Mannington Township.

Thunderstorms moving over the same areas of Woolwich Township caused flooding of fields and small streams. One farm had 35 acres of sweet potato and butternut squash under water. Adjusted for hail Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 3 and 4 inches in the township. In neighboring Harrison Township, a storm total of 3.27 inches was measured in Mullica Hill.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flooding of small creeks and roadways in Pitman Borough. The worst reported flooding was near and along the railroad line where vehicles became stuck and water rescues were performed. No serious injuries were reported.

In addition to the damaging hail, severe thunderstorms produced wind gusts estimated to reach about 70 mph in sections of Harrison and South Harrison Townships. Storm chasers noted that corn fields were totally flattened.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Williamstown (Monroe Township).
A severe thunderstorm dropped nickel size hail from Bear northeast through New Castle. The large hail shredded leaves off of trees.

A severe thunderstorm tore down several large oak and sycamore trees at the Brandywine Zoo in Wilmington. The downed trees damaged several exhibits. The In Flight exhibit was destroyed. A downed tree also punctured a hole in the roof af the animal hospital and damaged a storage shed. No animals were injured. The zoo remained closed until the 13th.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding that entered a couple of basement apartments at the Dana Apartments on North Tatnall Street. About a dozen residents were evacuated from two basement apartments. Three apartments and families above the flooded apartments were also displaced because the electricity was turned off. The building sits lower than the street. Adjusted for hail Doppler Radar storm total estimates were between one inch and an inch and a quarter.
A lightning strike struck and damaged an outbuilding on Quilleytown Road in Carneys Point Township.
Penny size hail fell in Pennsville Township. This was the first of several severe thunderstorms with large hail to effect Salem County on the 10th.
Quarter size hail fell in the Eldora section of Dennis Township. Pea size hail also fell in Woodbine.
Penny size hail fell in the Mamora section of Upper Township.
A severe thunderstorm dropped penny size from Somers Point northeast through Linwood. The same thunderstorm dropped smaller, marble size hail in Estell Manor and Atlantic City.

The last severe thunderstorm of the day proved to be the most damaging  as large hail fell for the longest period of time. Areas of large hail occurred from Harrison Township southeast through Monroe Township. Ten peach orchards in Gloucester County were damaged by the large hail. About 40 percent of the peach crop was already harvested prior to the severe thunderstorms. The fourteen peach orchards affected by repeated  severe thunderstorms with large hail in Gloucester, Camden and Atlantic Counties normally harvest about 30 million pounds of peaches.

The last thunderstorm of the day was the most damaging as large hail fell for the longest period of time. Areas of large hail occurred across Winslow and Waterford Townships. About three peach orchards in Camden County were damaged by the large hail. About 40 percent of the peach crop was already harvested prior to the severe thunderstorms. The fourteen peach orchards affected by repeated severe thunderstorms with large hail in Gloucester, Camden and Atlantic Counties normally harvest about 30 million pounds of peaches.

A severe thunderstorm downed several trees along the 200 block of Rosenhayn Avenue in Upper Deerfield Township. The downed trees damaged four homes on the block. The left side of one home was destroyed. Another home was impaled twice by a downed tree. Another home had its awning torn away from its porch, outdoor furniture damaged and a tree on its pool. Elsewhere in Upper Deerfield Township, downed trees blocked Park Avenue. Several pine and oak trees were split and twisted. About 5,200 homes and businesses lost power in the county. Outages lasted into the 12th.

Penny to nickel size hail fell from Upper Deerfield Township east through Deerfield Township and Millville. In Millville, the large hail damaged about 75 vehicles at the Chrysler, Dodge and Jeep Dealership on North 2nd Street.
A mesonet site at Oswego Lake recorded a wind gust of 65 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Woodland Township.
A lightning strike amd ensuing fire damaged a townhouse on Rosemont Terrace in Upper Hanover Township. No injuries were reported.
A severe thunderstorm tore down trees at the intersection of Koerner Road and Pennsylvania State Route 390 in Paradise Township.

The squall line of severe thunderstorms tore down numerous trees and wires across Berks County. Muhlenberg Township, north of Reading was hardest hit. Dozens of trees were toppled in Riverview Park. The entire length of River Road was closed. The North 5th Street Highway was closed for more than three hours because of a toppled utility pole. A few other roads were closed late into the day. A house on George Street lost a piece of its roof. A building on Leiszs Bridge Road was damaged by a downed tree. Throughout the county, about 2,500 homes and businesses lost power.
The gust front associated with the squall line of severe thunderstorms tore down a few trees and wires in Delaware County, mainly in the northwestern part of the county.
Several trees and wires were knocked down in Mount Arlington Borough.
A severe thunderstorm tore down a few trees and wires in Mendham Borough and Township.
A severe thunderstorm tore down a few trees along Charlestown Road in Bethlehem Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down about a half dozen large trees in Hamilton Township. The trees were knocked down on and off of Jani Avenue, Kuser Road, Whitehorse-Hamilton Square Road and in Veteran's Park. The tree wind damage stopped in the Ravenscroft housing development. One home had its lawn furniture tossed and screens ripped away. Another home lost its mail box and party tent. Large tree limbs and wires were also knocked down in West Windsor Township.
A severe thunderstorm dropped nickel to quarter size hail in Millville and Vineland.
Lightning struck the Ocean City MUA pumping station.
Trees and wires were knocked down on the south side of Georgetown.
Penny size hail fell in Egg Harbor Township.

Heavy rain caused flooding along Frankford Creek. The creek was above its 7 foot flood stage from 613 p.m. EDT through 717 p.m. EDT on the 9th. It crested at 9.27 feet at 645 p.m. EDT. Storm totals included 2.27 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport and 1.97 inches at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport.

Heavy rain caused flooding along the Valley Creek. The Valley Creek at Valley Forge was above its 7 foot flood stage from 603 p.m. EDT through 1057 p.m. EDT on the 6th. It crested at 7.90 feet at 730 p.m. EDT. Storm totals in Chester County included 3.72 inches in Kenneth Square, 3.02 inches in Glenmoore and 2.47 inches in Honey Brook.

Heavy rain led to minor flash flooding of streams and roadways in and around Netcong Borough. In the central part of the county, several roads were flooded in Dover. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between two and two and a half inches around the borough.

Runoff from heavy rain led to roadway flooding as well as flooding of smaller streams across central Somerset County from Branchburg Township east through Bound Brook Borough. Several roads were closed. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached two inches.

Runoff from heavy rain caused flooding of smaller streams in northern Middlesex County. It also led to lane closures along the Garden State Parkway. Doppler Radar Storm Total estimates reached around 1.5 inches, most of which fell within an hour.

Heavy rain caused flooding of small river and roadway flooding in and around Somerdale Borough. Somerdale Road was closed near the White Horse Pike (U.S. Route 30). This is located close to the Cooper River. Doppler Radar storm total estimates were around 1.5 inches.

Showers and thunderstorms with heavy rain caused the flooding and washouts of a few roads in Durham and Nockamixon Townships. A large mudslide occurred across Pennsylvania State Route 611 in Durham Township and closed it. Other major roads closed in the area included Center Hill and Kintner Hill Roads. Water poured down the embankment of Pennsylvania State Route 212 overran a house on Old Furnace Road. The water broke windows, filled the basement with water and tore away the driveway. The rush of water also scattered boulders and smaller rocks that clogged Rodges Run under two bridges on Lehnenberg Road. Pennsylvania State Route 611 was closed in both directions until the 29th. Flooding along Gallows Run and rock slides caused the road to be closed from Pennsylvania State Route 212 to Centerhill Road. In Nockamixon Township, a 170-year-old stone wall collapsed under the weight of water cascading off the steep cliffs that hug the southbound side of River Road. The rain overflowed a culvert off the cliff side of the road, washed across the roadway, filled the canal and shattered the wall. Repairs were estimated at $500,000. A homeowner on River Road in the township saw hundreds of rocks carried onto his property by a flooding stream and then onto River Road. The stream knocked down 100 feet of fencing and carried away a propane tank. The precipitation total for the 28th from the Lehigh Valley International Airport was 3.83 inches.

Heavy rain during the day on the 28th led to poor drainage and roadway flooding in and around Bethlehem. The heavy rain also caused the Monocacy Creek in Bethlehem to reach flood stage during the afternoon. The Celtic Classic held in Johnston Park in Bethlehem was affected by its flooding. About six food vendors and twenty craft merchants were flooded. About 100 workers were forced to evacuate their location. That part of the park was covered by two feet of water. Performing acts were also moved to other stages. The Monocacy Creek at the gage site in Bethlehem was above its 4.5 foot flood stage from 305 p.m. EDT through 346 p.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 4.53 feet at 330 p.m. EDT. The precipitation total for the 28th from the Lehigh Valley International Airport was 3.83 inches.

Flooding was also reported along a small tributary to the creek along Horsehill Road in Hanover Township. The Whippany Creek in Morristown was above its 6 foot flood stage from 614 p.m. EDT through 1022 p.m. EDT on the 6th. It crested at 6.38 feet at 8 p.m. EDT. An EF1 tornado with maximum wind gusts of about 95 mph touched down in East Allentown. The tornado damaged about 50 homes and the Louis E. Dieruff High School which was closed until September 10th. About 100 trees were damaged or destroyed. The tornado touched down between North Ortt Street and East Cedar Street behind the Lehigh Valley Christian High School on Oswego Street. It proceeded to move west paralleling East Cedar Street and reached its maximum strength around North Kearney Street where EF1 damage started. The high school was within the path of the strongest part of the tornado. The tornado started to weaken just before it crossed North Irving Street and lifted around North Hart Street. ||Homes were hardest hit near the intersection of East Cedar and Kiowa Streets. Several roofs were damaged; shingles were pulled from other homes. Part of a roof was torn away from a home on North Irving Street. Along the path of the tornado siding was torn from a few other homes and power lines were pulled down in addition to the tree damage. The greatest destruction occurred on the grounds of the Louis E. Dieruff High School. The tornado peeled away a section of the high school's roof near the planetarium. This allowed the heavy rain to cause water damage to seventeen classrooms and a couple of hundred lockers. Ventilation units located on the roof were wrenched away. About twenty-five trees on the high school grounds were knocked down; the limbs damaged several school windows. Repairs to the high school were not expected to be completed until the middle of November.| |The tornado path length was about 0.6 of a mile and its maximum path width was about 30 yards. No injuries were reported.

The temperature bottomed out at 11 degrees during the early morning of the 16th at the New Castle County Airport in Wilmington. At this same location, the temperature bottomed out at 5 degrees during the early morning of the 17th. Some mesonet sites had very similar low temperature readings and the wind added in produced wind chill values to zero or just below for a time.

The temperature bottomed out at 13 degrees during the early morning of the 16th at Dover Air Force Base. At this same location, the temperature bottomed out at 6 degrees during the early morning of the 17th. Some mesonet sites had low temperature readings down to zero, especially on the morning of the 17th. These bitterly cold air temperatures combined with some wind, which produced wind chill values to zero or just below for a time.

The temperature bottomed out at 13 degrees during the early morning of the 16th at the Georgetown airport. At this same location, the temperature bottomed out at 5 degrees during the early morning of the 17th. Some mesonet sites had low temperature readings down to zero, especially on the morning of the 17th. These bitterly cold air temperatures combined with some wind, which produced wind chill values to zero or just below for a time.

A severe thunderstorm dropped nickel to quarter size hail in Vinemont (Spring Township), West Lawn and Shillington Boroughs and also within Reading. The Reading Regional Airport also reported a wind gust to 54 mph.
Nickel to quarter size fell from Blandon in Maiden Creek Township east through Fleetwood Borough.

A severe thunderstorm damaged a farm and several trees in Oley Township. The damaging winds tore off a portion of a slate roof of the farmhouse. It also ripped off siding and blew out several windows. Trees were snapped or uprooted in the area and two utility poles were snapped. About 130 of the 500 Metropolitan Edison homes and businesses that lost power in the county occurred in Oley Township. Other Metropolitan Edison outages were reported in Birdsboro, Fleetwood, Kutztown, Lenhartsville (the most), Mohrsville and Reading.
A severe thunderstorm dropped quarter size in Longswamp Township.

A severe thunderstorm dropped ping pong ball size hail in Nesquehoning and nickel size hail in Summit Hill. Travel on U.S. Route 209 became hazardous in Nesquehoning because of the hail. Large hail was also reported in Lehighton.
A second severe thunderstorm dropped nickel size hail in Jim Thorpe.

Ping pong to golf ball size hail fell in Upper Macungie and Lower Macungie Townships and Macungie Borough. The largest hail was reported in the Ancient Oaks area of Lower Macungie Township and it also covered the ground. Nickel size hail also covered the ground of Macungie Borough.
Quarter size hail fell in Catasauqua Borough.
Nickel size hail fell in East Texas (Lower Macungie Township) and in Allentown. The hail that fell in Allentown started to accumulate on the ground.
A Skywarn spotter reported nickel size hail in Quakertown.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell over the higher terrain of Williams Township. Nickel size hail also fell in Easton.
Quarter size hail fell in Pennsburg Borough and also accumulated to around an inch on the ground.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down about a dozen large trees in the Emmaus Community Park. Some of the trees were about 60 feet tall. Picnic tables in the park were also tossed. Buildings near Indian Creek Road suffered wind damage. The roof was ripped off from a barn, metal was pulled away from a shed and the slate from another roof was scattered.

Severe thunderstorms dropped large hail across several municipalities in Delaware County. The largest reported hail was golf ball size in Media Borough. Quarter size hail was reported in Lansdowne Borough. In Clifton Heights Borough, penny size hail covered the ground. Dime to penny size hail were reported in both Boothwyn (Upper Chichester Township) and Concord Township. Dime size hail fell in Drexel Hill (Upper Darby Township) and Parkside Borough.
A severe thunderstorm pulled down large tree limbs and wires in Upper Darby Township. Half inch hail also fell from the severe thunderstorm.
Nickel size hail fell in Wyncote (Cheltenham Township).

Golf ball size hail was reported by a Skywarn spotter in the northeast section of Philadelphia. Northeast Philadelphia airport also had a measured wind gust of 47 mph. Dime size hail was also reported in Center City Philadelphia.

A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage in Lansdale Borough and Montgomery Township in Montgomery County. No injuries were reported in spite of the damage. In Lansdale, wind damage occurred around West 8th Street. The roof was completely blown off the shipping building of the Village Handcrafted Cabinetry Company. The severe thunderstorm knocked down a chimney into the kitchen of a home near that building on West 7th Street and Maple Avenue. Water entered the home. Elsewhere in Lansdale, a utility pole was snapped at the West 5th Street Park and a large pine tree was knocked down on North Line Street. In Montgomery Township, about 25 homes suffered wind damage in the Weathersfield Development. Homes on Beacon Court, Essex Court and August Lane bore the brunt of the wind damage. The homes suffered siding and roof shingle damage. Whole trees were knocked down and damaged some vehicles. One home had its windows blown out.
A severe thunderstorm ripped the roof off a shed in Vinemont (Spring Township).

A severe thunderstorm tore down a pole in Lenhartsville (Greenwich Township). About 200 of the 500 Metropolitan Edison outages in Berks County occurred in this area. Power was totally restored at about 4 a.m. EDT on the 30th.
Penny size hail fell in Schooleys Mountain at an elevation of about 1,200 feet.
Quarter size hail fell in Hamilton Square (Hamilton Township).
Dime to nickel hail fell from Camden northeast through Pennsauken.

A severe thunderstorm dropped penny to quarter size hail from Mount Laurel Township east through Hainesport Township, Westampton Township, Southampton and Springfield Township. The nickel size hail in Jobstown (Springfield Township) partially covered the ground.
A lightning strike at a Public Service Electric and Gas substation caused power outages in Branchburg Township.
Quarter size hail fell in Hammonton.
Quarter size hail was reported in Tabernacle Township.
Nickel size hail fell outside of the Asbury Park Press building in Neptune.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in North East. One large pine tree fell onto and caused minor damage to one home.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Newark. About 300 homes and businesses lost power.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees on Talley Road in Brandywine Hundred north of Interstate 95 and east of United States Route 202.
Dime to nickel size hail fell in northeastern New Castle County in Wilmington and Brandywine Hundred.
Penny to quarter size hail fell from a severe thunderstorm in Bethlehem and Palmer Townships. Smaller hail was also reported in Bath and Nazareth.

A house was struck by lightning in Mertztown (Longswamp Township). The combination of the wind and lightning caused about 1,000 homes and businesses to lose power in thirteen municipalities in Berks County including Reading, Douglassville, Bernville and Kutztown.
Penny to quarter size hail fell in Phillipsburg and Alpha.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Perkasie.

Four hikers were struck and injured by lightning in the Delaware Water Gap National Recreational Area in Worthington State Forest about one mile south of Sunfish Pond in Pahaquarry Township. Lightning struck the ground first and then traveled to the hikers. Three men and one woman were injured. Two hikers initially were unable to talk after they were struck by lightning. Another hiker suffered a head wound. The injured hikers were taken to Pocono Medical Center in Pennsylvania.
A few trees and wires were knocked down by a severe thunderstorm in Belvidere. About 500 homes and businesses lost power in Warren and Hunterdon Counties.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires in Washington Township. About 500 homes and businesses lost power in Warren and Hunterdon Counties.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires across east central Hunterdon County in Franklin, Raritan and Readington Townships. About 500 homes and businesses lost power in Warren and Hunterdon Counties.
A severe thunderstorm snapped a pole on Delaware State Route 9 in East Dover Hundred south of Little Creek.
Lightning strikes caused several homes in Little Creek to lose power.
Nickel size hail fell in Vineland.
For the second time that morning, a severe thunderstorm dropped nickel size hail in Vineland.
Penny to nickel size hail fell in Voorhees Township.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a tree and a house.
Nickel size hail fell along City Avenue in Bala Cynwyd.
Lightning struck and caused minor damage to the bell tower of the Zion Methodist Church on County Route 382 in Baltimore Hundred.

A lightning strike and the ensuing fire destroyed an abandoned barn outside of Henderson along Bee Tree Road in Caroline County. A nearby tree was initially struck by the lightning. About twenty-seven fire fighters from four separate companies responded and took about thirty minutes to control the blaze. But, the two story barn was destroyed.

A lightning strike caused 31 homes to lose power in Preston. Power was restored to all homes by 11 p.m. EDT that evening.

A severe thunderstorm turned over a carport onto a swing set off of Dover Road in Easton. A large tree was also knocked down between two houses on Prospect Avenue. A mesonet site at Cook's Hope measured a wind gust to 50 mph.
Several residences were damaged by a lightning strike and then the ensuing fire in Honey Brook. No injuries were reported.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire badly damaged a garage in Woodbury Heights.
A trained spotter reported penny size hail in Southampton Township.

US Airways flight number 1036, a Boeing 757 jet, was struck by lightning as it was coming in for landing at Philadelphia International Airport. The jet landed safely without incident.
A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs and wires in and around Middletown. About 120 Delmarva Power and Light customers lost power.

A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs and wires in Hopewell Township. The thunderstorm also dropped pea to dime size hail in Mercer and Middlesex Counties as far northeast as Edison in Middlesex County.

The Valley Creek at Valley Forge exceeded its 7 foot flood stage from 256 a.m. EDT through 402 a.m. EDT on the 7th. It crested at 7.27 feet at 330 a.m. EDT. Chester County storm totals included 1.74 inches in Downingtown and 1.43 inches in West Chester.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused flooding across smaller creeks in central Montgomery County. The runoff and smaller stream flooding also led to flooding along the East Branch of the Perkiomen Creek. Montgomery County storm totals included 1.91 inches in Hatfield, 1.55 inches in Oreland, 1.51 inches in Kulpsville, 1.26 inches in Green Lane and 1.20 inches in Pottstown.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused flooding across smaller creeks in central and upper Bucks County. The runoff and smaller stream flooding also led to flooding along the East Branch of the Perkiomen Creek in  Montgomery County. Bucks County storm totals included 2.03 inches in Perkasie, 1.18 inches in Doylestown and 1.10 inches in Newtown.

The East Branch of the Perkiomen Creek at Schwenksville was above its 7 foot flood stage from 7 a.m. EDT through 1007 a.m. EDT on the 7th. It crested at 7.27 feet at 830 a.m. EDT. Runoff from the heavy rain that fell earlier that morning in upper Bucks County and central Montgomery County caused the flooding. Storm totals included 2.03 inches in Perkasie (Bucks County), 1.91 inches in Hatfield (Montgomery County) and 1.26 inches in Green Lane (Montgomery County).
A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs and wires in central Kent County. About 400 homes and businesses lost power.

events.event_narrative: The gust front from a thunderstorm produced a wind gust to 35 knots (40 mph) at Brandywine Shoal Light.
A severe thunderstorm tore down a few trees in Maurice River Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a line of trees along Eastern Neck Road south of Rock Hall. A travel trailer was destroyed by a downed tree.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Centreville.
A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs in Sadsbury Township.
A Skywarn spotter reported quarter size hail in Houston.
A severe thunderstorm dropped quarter size hail in Milford. In addition, some small tree branches were torn down.
A severe thunderstorm tore down a couple of trees in Aston Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flooding in and around Richmond Township in Berks County. Roads were flooded and closed in the area. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 2.5 and 3.0 inches, most of which fell within one hour.

A severe thunderstorm tore down seven utility poles in Kutztown. The same severe thunderstorm tore down several trees. The combination of the wind and lightning caused about 1,000 homes and businesses to lose power in thirteen municipalities in Berks County including Reading, Douglassville, Bernville and Kutztown.

Thunderstorms with frequent lightning struck several homes in Northampton County and caused a couple of fires. About one hundred cloud to ground lightning strikes occurred within a fifteen minute period in the Lehigh Valley. ||In Moore Township, a lightning strike and ensuing fire gutted a home on Countryview Lane. The shell of the house collapsed. Two adults that lived in the house were displaced and two cats died in the house. In Bushkill Township, a family was displaced after a lightning strike and ensuing fire badly damaged a home on Bushkill Center Road. The rear of the home around the kitchen was badly damaged. Two dogs were rescued. Other house fires were reported in Bath and Upper Nazareth Township. In East Allen Township, a family was trapped after a lightning strike downed wires around their home.
A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs and wires in Smithfield Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Upper Mount Bethel Township.

A lightning strike and ensuing fire sparked a garage and house fire on Oyster Shell Cove in Salt Pond in Baltimore Hundred. The garage was struck by lightning and the fire then spread to the home. Damage was estimated at $40,000. No injuries were reported.

A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust to 76 mph at the New Castle County Airport. The same severe thunderstorm caused a partial roof collapse at an industrial park near New Castle County Airport, knocked down large trees in New Castle, knocked down a tree onto a vehicle in Wilmington and capsized seven boats at Battery Park on the Delaware River. The worst reported wind damage was the partial collapse of the roof of an auto parts storage facility near the airport. About a 200 foot section of the roof was torn away, another piece collapsed into the building. Pieces of the roof landed in the back yards of homes on Bunker Hill Road. Two front doors were also blown away. Two homes in New Castle suffered roof damage after trees fell on them. There were about thirty weather related incidences (downed trees and wires and transformers) reported throughout New Castle County. No injuries were reported. About 15,000 homes and businesses lost power because of the severe thunderstorm. Power was fully restored by the 3rd.
The same severe thunderstorm dropped penny size hail in Wilmington.

A severe thunderstorm produced wind gusts to around 60 mph near the Delaware Memorial Bridge in Pennsville Township. Trees were also knocked down in the township. Wind damage from the severe thunderstorm extended east into Quinton Township where a couple of two foot diameter trees were knocked down. Atlantic City Electric reported about 5,300 homes and businesses lost power in Salem County.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and tree limbs in Vineland. There were ten major roadways with downed trees in the city. Most of the wind damage occurred south of Chestnut Avenue and east of the Boulevard.  Large fallen trees were reported on Garry Avenue and South Lincoln Street. A downed tree damaged the roof, garage and porch of a home on Blackberry Court. A vehicle was damaged by a downed tree. The gust front from the same severe thunderstorm produced estimated wind gusts of 60 mph in Millville. There were three reports of downed trees. Vineland Electric and Atlantic City Electric reported about 7,300 homes and businesses lost power in the county. Power was restored by midnight EDT that night.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust to 59 mph in Atlantic City.

events.event_narrative: A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust to 51 knots (59 mph) in Atlantic City.
A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs and wires in Pennsville Township.
A severe thunderstorm also knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Upper Pittsgrove Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires and caused power outages in Roxana (Baltimore Hundred).
Penny size hail fell south of Galena.
Nickel size hail was reported in Bath.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Upper Bern and Upper Tulpehocken Townships.
A severe thunderstorm tore down a large tree onto wires as well as several large tree limbs in Upper Pottsgrove Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down an eighty foot tree in West Rockhill Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Newtown Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a large tree in Kingwood Township onto County Route 519. A few other large tree limbs were torn down in the township.
Penny to nickel size hail fell from a severe thunderstorm near and along the borders of Salford, Lower Salford and Franconia Townships.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding as well as flooding of streams in the East Branch of the Perkiomen Creek basin in Franconia and Salford Townships. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 3.6 inches in this area, most of which fell within one hour.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding as well as flooding of streams in the East Branch of the Perkiomen Creek basin in West Rockhill Township. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 2.96 inches in the township, most of which fell within one hour.
A Skywarn spotter measured a wind gust to 60 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Dagsboro Hundred.

A Bay View couple was homeless after a lightning strike and ensuing fire badly damaged their home. Lightning struck a tree on the property and then jumped to the roof of the home. It took about sixty firefighters ninety minutes to extinguish the blaze. Motorists were detoured near Cecil College as the fire was being fought. No injuries were reported. Damage was estimated at $215,000.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding as well as flooding of Goose Creek in West Chester. Residents along the 300 block of East Union Street were evacuated until the flooding subsided that afternoon. No injuries or damage were reported. The morning event total in Downingtown was 1.90 inches.||The combination of thunderstorms with heavy rain during the morning and afternoon swelled all creeks in Chester County. Two male kayakers drowned in the swollen Brandywine Creek on the afternoon of the 9th in East Bradford Township. One man was pulled from the creek at 210 p.m. EDT that afternoon. They were last seen on the creek near a four foot high dam north of a bridge near Creek Route and Pennsylvania State Route 52 in the township.

A 53-year-old man collapsed and died while doing yard work in his backyard in Bethlehem Township. He was holding an electric trimmer when he was struck by lightning. Medical crews responded, administered CPR, then transported him to Lehigh Valley Hospital Muhlenberg Campus where he was pronounced dead.

In Rehoboth Beach, a lightning strike and ensuing fire caused about an estimated $250,000 in damage to a house on Coventry Lane in the Rehoboth Beach Yacht and Country Club development. Lightning apparently struck the attic of the home. Six fire companies fought the blaze.
In Dagsboro, an attic fire caused by a lightning strike to a home on Westchester Court caused an estimated $1,500 in damage to it before it was extinguished.
A lightning strike that hit a power line caused outages to about 300 customers in the Easton Utility service area in Easton. Traffic lights were also knocked out.

Lightning struck a home on Pleasant Avenue in Hanover Township. The ensuing fire was contained to the attic, but both the first and second floors of the home sustained smoke and water damage. The fire made the home uninhabitable. No injuries were reported.

A Fielding Drive man was hospitalized after he was shocked by a power surge caused by a lightning strike. Lightning struck the roof of a home on Rabbit Run Road in Willistown Township. It damaged some shingles on the roof as well as a nearby pine tree.

Lightning struck the peak of a roof of a home on North Limerick Road in Limerick Township and caught fire. Four fire companies assisted and fought the blaze and confined the fire to one bedroom and attic on one side of the house. The lightning strike also fried the electrical system and meter in the house.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees throughout Delaware County, mainly in the central part of the county. A downed tree blocked one road in Middletown Township. Another downed tree damaged a roadway shoulder in Marple Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a tree onto Sugartown Road in Devon (Easttown Township) as well as a few other large tree limbs in the township.
Penny to nickel size hail fell in Clayton. Hail covered the ground so extensively, that some of it was still around the next morning.

A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage between Smyrna and Blackiston Crossroads mainly in Kenton Hundred. There were nine calls for fallen trees and downed wires. In Smyrna shingles were torn from one home and a downed tree damaged a porch. Between Clayton and Blackiston, two mobile homes were damaged after trees fell on them. Another mobile home was moved off its foundation. A barn was destroyed by the thunderstorm winds and a camper within it was damaged.  One hundred pound propane tanks were toppled. Several homes in the Plantation Crossing development west of Clayton suffered minor structural damage.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage in eastern Morris County. Roadway flooding was reported on New Jersey State Route 10 in Hanover Township. A storm total from Hanover Township was 2.90 inches.
A squall line of strong to severe thunderstorms pulled down large tree limbs in central Berks County from Blandon (Maidencreek Township) south to West Reading.
Nickel size hail fell in Honey Brook Township.
Penny size hail fell in Exton (West Whiteland Township).
A severe thunderstorm dropped dime to nickel size hail in West Collingswood Borough. Pea size hail fell in nearby Mount Ephraim Borough.
A severe thunderstorm pulled down large tree limbs and wires in Evesham Township.
A house in Princeton was struck by lightning and damaged by the ensuing fire. No injuries were reported.
A building in Carteret was struck by lightning. The lightning strike left a small hole in the roof, but no fire developed.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged an Ocean Acres home in Stafford Township. No injuries were reported.
A severe thunderstorm knocked over large tree limbs, wires and eight poles in Fortescue (Downe Township). A wind gust to 51 mph was measured within Fortescue.
A severe thunderstorm dropped penny to nickel size hail in Womelsdorf Borough.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage as well as stream flooding in Caernarvon Township in cluding the Morgantown area. Doppler Radar storm total estimates for the day reached between 3 and 4 inches.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Oxford Borough.
Penny to nickel size hail also fell east of Hartley in Kenton Hundred.

A line of strong to severe thunderstorms tore down tree limbs and power lines mainly in central Queen Anne's County. The combination of the wind and lightning caused about 1,200 Delmarva Power and Light customers to lose power in the county, which was the hardest hit along the Maryland Eastern Shore.

A Skywarn spotter saw a funnel cloud northwest of Denton.
Penny size hail fell from a severe thunderstorm near Denton.
A Skywarn spotter estimated wind gusts of 60 mph in a severe thunderstorm near Denton.
A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs and wires between Agner and Federalsburg in Caroline County.

A severe thunderstorm produced a swath of straight-line wind damage up to one-half mile wide in spots from just west of Harrington in southwestern Kent County in Mispillion Hundred south to the town of Greenwood in northern Sussex County.  Damage began on High Stump Road west of Harrington where a few tree tops were snapped and a few other trees were uprooted. An old barn was blown down, with its roofing material blown up to one-half mile away.  Farther south, two trees were blown down along Burrsville Road. Wind damage continued into Sussex County. ||Corn was stripped to the stalk on many fields within the damage swath, resulting in a total loss in some cases.  Wheat and barely fields also suffered substantial damage.  Combined Kent and Sussex County crop losses could easily total several hundred thousand dollars.  Maximum wind speeds were estimated at 80 MPH.

A severe thunderstorm produced a swath of straight-line wind damage up to one-half mile wide in spots from southwestern Kent County into western Sussex County.  Most of the wind damage occurred in Northwest Fork Hundred. Maximum wind gusts were estimated at 80 mph and caused property as well as substantial crop damage.  One home sustained substantial damage.  There was widespread crop damage from large hail.||Wind damage in Sussex County started near County Route 16 near Blanchard. The most significant damage occurred parallel to McDowell Road east of Woodbridge Road.  A porch roof was ripped away from a wood-framed farm house, and a steel antenna tower next to the house was bent.  A tree near the house was blown down, and a large chicken barn near the house collapsed.  Farther east, another steel antenna tower was bent, and some shingles were torn off the roof of a nearby house. ||Corn was stripped to the stalk on many fields within the damage swath, resulting in a total loss in some cases.  Wheat and barely fields also suffered substantial damage.  Crop losses mainly from hail could easily total several hundred thousand dollars.  ||Tree damage was also noted in the town of Greenwood.  Small to medium sized limbs were torn away along Minor Street in downtown Greenwood.  Some lawn furniture was blown around, and streets and driveways were littered with leaves.  Some funnel clouds were reported, but they did not touch down.

A severe thunderstorm also produced large hail west of Greenwood in Sussex County.  There was widespread crop damage from large hail. The hail caused corn to be stripped to the stalk. Wheat and barely fields also suffered substantial damage.  Crop losses could easily total several hundred thousand dollars.  In the nearby garden, strawberry plants were pulverized by the hail. The most significant hail damage occurred parallel to McDowell Road east of Woodbridge Road. Hail size was estimated.

A funnel cloud was sighted during a severe thunderstorm in northwest Sussex County. A National Weather Service damage survey indicated that all of the wind damage was straight line and that the funnel did not touch the ground.
Quarter size hail fell in Broad Creek Hundred northeast of Laurel.
A large tree was uprooted near the Bethel Wesleyan Church in Goldsboro.
Nickel size hail fell in Franklin Township.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Walnutport.
Nickel size hail fell just west of Slatington.
A severe thunderstorm dropped penny to quarter size hail in Allentown.
In addition to large hail, a severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Allentown.
A severe thunderstorm dropped nickel size hail that brusied apples and peaches on farms in Lower Mildford Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Quakertown Borough.
Golf ball size hail fell in Milford Township.
Penny size hail fell in Souderton Borough.
A severe thunderstorm dropped quarter size hail in Lansdale Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a large tree onto Nixon Avenue in the Roxborough section of Philadelphia and also produced pea size hail.
Nickel size hail fell in Byram Township.
A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs in Woodbury.
A severe thunderstorm tore down power lines and large tree limbs in Stanton in Mill Creek Hundred.
A severe thunderstorm tore a couple of trees in Millville (Baltimore Hundred).

The gust front from a severe thunderstorm flattened a corn field (was year old corn) off of Auckland Road near Love Point on Kent Island. This was the same parent thunderstorm that produced waterspouts on Chesapeake Bay.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires throughout Cecil County. The combination of damaging winds and lightning caused about 2,000 homes and businesses in the county to lose power. Power was not fully restored until the afternoon of the 21st. Heavy rain from the thunderstorm also flooded Delaware Avenue in Elkton.
A downed tree pulled down wires onto a pick-up truck on Bradford Avenue in West Chester. The driver and two passengers were stuck inside until the power was shut down.
Farther southwest in Chester County, a severe thunderstorm tore down a few trees in Nottingham Township.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 68 mph at High Point in Sussex County.

A severe thunderstorm tore down a couple of trees and wires in Coolbaugh and Tobyhanna Townships in northwestern Monroe County. The same thunderstorm dropped small hail (dime size) in Jackson and Pocono Townships. The dime size hail covered the ground in Scotrun (Pocono Township).
A home was struck by lightning in Lehighton. A pole was also struck and knocked down in the borough.
A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees in Kidder Township.
A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees in southeastern Monroe County mainly in Polk and Hamilton Townships.
A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs and wires in Mansfield Township.
A severe thunderstorm tore down numerous trees and wires across the northern half of Middlesex County. Hardest hit municipalities included East Brunswick, Old Bridge and Woodbridge.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a home in South River.
Quarter size hail fell in Upper Pottsgrove Township and penny size hail fell in Lower Pottsgrove Township.

A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees in Pottstown. Trees were knocked down on Center Avenue, Rosedale Drive and Henry Street. Another tree was struck by lightning and fell down on King Street. A large maple tree fell down onto and damaged the porch of a home on Rosedale Drive. In Stowe (Upper Pottsgrove Township), a tree fell onto a roof of a home. About 740 homes and businesses lost power.

events.event_narrative: A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 56 knots (65 mph) at the Sandy Hook Coast Guard Station. The gust front from the same thunderstorm produced wind damage in Long Branch.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 62 mph at the Keansburg Coast Guard Station. Wires were knocked down in nearby Union Beach and ignited a small fire.

A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 65 mph at the Sandy Hook Coast Guard Station. The gust front from the same severe thunderstorm tore down a few trees and large tree limbs in Long Branch and West Long Branch. The New Jersey Transit Coast Line between New York City and Long Branch suspended service because of a downed tree on wires near Red Bank.
Nickel size hail fell in Delran Township.
A severe thunderstorm dropped penny size hail in Moorestown Township.
Peal to nickel size hail fell from a severe thunderstorm in Laureldale Borough. Nickel size hail also fell in Ruscombmanor Township.
Nickel size hail fell from a severe thunderstorm in Trappe Township.
Nickel size hail fell in Worcester Township.
Quarter size hail fell in Royersford.
Nickel size hail fell within Philadelphia.
A severe thunderstorm dropped penny size hail in Toms River.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous poles and wires in Point Pleasant and Bay Head. A primary electrical wire was knocked down in Bay Head and forced the closure of one street until it was removed.

events.cz_name: MANASQUAN INLET TO LITTLE EGG INLET NJ OUT 20NM
events.event_narrative: A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage in both Point Pleasant and Bay Head.
A severe thunderstorm tore down a few trees in Birdsboro Borough. The combination of a few severe thunderstorms caused about 2,800 homes and businesses to lose power in Berks County.

A severe thunderstorm tore down a few trees in Wernersville Borough. The combination of a few severe thunderstorms that passed through Berks County caused about 2,800 homes and businesses to lose power.

The first severe thunderstorm of the evening to affect Berks County caused widespread tree damage in the southeast part of the county. Scores of trees were knocked down. The worst reported damage was in Amity Township. About thirty homes were damaged, two were destroyed by fallen trees and resulted in the displacement of those two families. About 80 other people were displaced temporarily. Many trees were knocked down along Levengood Road and County Routes 562 and 662 in the township. Downed trees and poles blocked and closed County Route 562. In Douglas Township, the Manatawny Winery was damaged. A pheasant farm near Yellow House was damaged. Wires were knocked down throughout the township. In Boyertown, a tent was overturned. Numerous trees were also knocked down in Oley and Earl Townships. About 2,800 homes and businesses lost power in the county because of the series of severe thunderstorms. No injuries were reported.

Slow moving thunderstorms with torrential rain caused poor drainage and stream flooding in Medford Township. Several roads were closed. Hardest hit roadways were the intersection of New Jersey State Route 70 and Hartford Road in the township. One car was stranded in the flood waters. The intersection was reopened at 5 p.m. EDT. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 3 and 4 inches in parts of Medford and Southampton Townships; most fell within one hour.
Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage flooding and flooding of smaller creeks in and around the Mahoning Creek Basin.

Runoff from heavy rain in southern Somerset County and northern Mercer County caused flooding along the Millstone River in Griggstown. The Giriggstown Causeway was closed. The Millstone River at Giriggstown was above its 10 foot flood stage from 1203 a.m. EDT on the 14th through 157 a.m. EDT on the 15th. It crested at 10.75 feet at 245 p.m. EDT on the 14th. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 1.5 and 2.0 inches. While not the heaviest rain, the first half of June and the month of June as a whole was wetter than normal and made it easier for streams and creeks to potentially flood.||The heavier than normal rain that fell throughout the month of June made it the sixth wettest June on record (6.61 statewide average) for New Jersey since 1895. The heavy rain made it difficult to make hay, for farmers to get into wet fields, caused fruits to swell, drowned some crops and increased the number of slugs, mosquitoes, mold and mushrooms. It also cut down on the number of visitors to pick your own stands and wreaked havoc on the schedules of youth leagues and other outdoor events. ||For individual stations, it was the third wettest June on record for Atlantic City (7.05 inches). June also established a new record for the most number of days with measurable precipitation (17 days). In Trenton, it was the ninth wettest June on record (6.96 inches) and also set a record for the most number of days with measurable precipitation (21 days).

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused roadway flooding and flooding of creeks in and around Exton in West Whiteland Township. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached three inches in the area and a measured storm total of 2.47 inches was reported from nearby Downingtown.

Slow moving thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage as well as flash flooding of smaller streams and creeks including the headwaters of the Neshaminy Creek in and around Doylestown, Warwick, Warrington and Westminster Townships in central Bucks County. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 5 and 6 inches in the area.  In Warwick Township, two water rescues were performed by emergency responders. A man became stranded in his vehicle after the Neshaminy overflowed on Creek Road and a woman was rescued from her vehicle on Stover Street after a retention basin overflowed. In Doylestown, both Pine Run and Chapman Road were closed. The Little Neshaminy Creek at Neshaminy was above its 8 foot flood stage from 337 p.m. EDT through 939 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 9.21 feet at 445 p.m. EDT. Event storm totals included 4.61 inches in Richboro (Northampton Township).

Runoff from heavy rain upstream caused flooding along lower parts of the Neshaminy Creek. The Neshaminy Creek at Langhorne was above its 9 foot flood stage from 717 p.m. EDT on the 13th through 259 a.m. EDT on the 14th. It crested at 11.9 feet at 1230 a.m. EDT on the 14th. Storm totals included 4.61 inches in Richboro and 2.21 inches in Langhorne.

Runoff from the heavy rain upstream caused flooding to continue into the night of the 13th along lower stretches of the Neshaminy Creek. The Neshaminy Creek at Langhorne was above its 9 foot flood stage from 717 p.m. EDT on the 13th through 259 a.m. EDT on the 14th. It crested at 11.9 feet at 1230 a.m. EDT on the 14th. Storm totals included 4.61 inches in Richboro and 2.21 inches in Langhorne.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours dropped a Doppler Radar estimated 3 to 6 inches across southern Montgomery County from Whitpain Township northeast through Horsham Township. This caused poor drainage flooding as well as flooding along the Wissahickon and Pennypack Creeks. Several roads were closed due to the flooding and marine rescues from stranded vehicles. The worst reported flooding occurred along the Pennypack Creek at the Robert Bruce Apartments along the Hatboro and Upper Moreland Township line. The creek flooded into the parking lot and submerged a few vehicles. Residents moved from some lower lying apartments to higher ones as a precaution. Event precipitation totals included 3.78 inches in Willow Grove and 3.50 inches in Ambler.

Runoff from the heavy rain across southern Montgomery County led to flooding along the Wissahickon Creek. The Wissahickon Creek at Fort Washington was above its 9 foot flood stage from 505 p.m. EDT through 1049 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 11.78 feet at 730 p.m. EDT. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 5 and 6 inches in the county. Actual reported amounts included 3.78 inches in Willow Grove and 3.50 inches in Ambler.

Runoff from the heavy rain across southern Montgomery County caused flooding along the Wissahickon Creek to occur deep into the evening on the 13th. The Wissahickon Creek at Fort Washington was above its 9 foot flood stage from 505 p.m. EDT through 1049 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 11.78 feet at 730 p.m. EDT. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 5 and 6 inches in the county. Actual reported amounts included 3.78 inches in Willow Grove and 3.50 inches in Ambler.

Runoff from the heavy rain in Montgomery County caused flooding along the Pennypack Creek within Philadelphia. The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge was above its 7 foot flood stage from 941 p.m. EDT on the 13th through 1239 a.m. EDT on the 14th. It crested at 7.8 feet at 1130 p.m. EDT on the 13th.

Runoff from the heavy rain in Montgomery County caused flooding along the Wissahickon Creek within Philadelphia. The Wissahickon Creek at its mouth was above its 5 foot flood stage from 815 p.m. EDT on the 13th through 337 a.m. EDT on the 14th. It crested at 6.65 feet at 1145 p.m. EDT on the 13th.

Heavy rain fell from about 730 a.m. EDT and 900 a.m. EDT on the morning of the 18th in and around Kent Island. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached about one inch. But, the heavy rain coincided with the high tide which was higher than normal because of the approaching new moon and an up the bay wind flow. This caused roadway and field flooding around the region. On Kent Island, Thompson Creek Road flooded as did the Thompson Creek Public Landing. At the Kent Narrows, Wharf Drive flooded as did the parking lot of a seafood market. On the Eastern Shore, Winchester Creek flooded some front yards in Grasonville. Standing water was on Main Street in Queenstown. The high tide that morning at Tolchester Beach (Kent County) and Cambridge (Dorchester County) reached 3.50 feet above mean lower low water. That is the level at which minor tidal flooding begins.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding of the Beaver Brook in downtown Clinton during the early morning of the 2nd. Leigh and Main Streets flooded around 4 a.m. EDT. The back of five buildings were flooded on Leigh Street. A restaurant on East Main Street suffered minimal flood damage. Two police vehicles were also flooded and damaged. The flood waters receded by 6 a.m. EDT and all roads were reopened. Storm totals from northern Hunterdon County included 4.78 inches in Califon, 3.27 inches in Annandale and 3.11 inches in High Bridge.

The runoff from the heavy rain earlier on the morning of the 2nd across northern Hunterdon County led to minor flooding along the South Branch of the Raritan River. The South Branch of the Raritan River at Stanton was above its 8 foot flood stage from 918 a.m. EDT through 1151 a.m. EDT on the 2nd. It crested at 8.19 feet at 1015 a.m. EDT. Farther upstream, the South Branch of the Raritan River at High Bridge crested just below (9.94 feet) its 10 foot flood stage at 4 a.m. EDT. Storm totals included 4.78 inches in Califon, 3.27 inches in Annandale and 3.11 inches in High Bridge.

A downburst from a severe thunderstorm caused wind damage centered around Long Branch and Oceanport. About 13,000 homes and businesses lost power in a dozen municipalities in that part of Monmouth County. Numerous wires and tree limbs were knocked down. The combination of roadway debris and traffic lights that were out made driving difficult.

Lightning struck a pine tree in the front yard of a Katherine Drive home in Rockaway Township and caused it to explode about 4 a.m. EDT. The tree shrapnel impaled a nearby home's roof and damaged the back window of a car. The cable connection within the home was fried by the lightning strike. All power was restored that afternoon.

A lightning strike caused a townhouse fire on Creekside Court in the Christine Hollow Development in Bear. The fire burned the roof of the townhouse and adjacent townhouses also suffered minor damage. The townhome residents were displaced. Damage was estimated at $125,000.
Heavy rain caused flooding along Pennsylvania State Route 61 between Hamburg and Leesport. A couple of vehicles were stranded in the high water. A couple of basements were also flooded.
The Oyster Creek Nuclear Generating Station was forced to shut power generation down after lightning strikes in the Lacey Township area caused outages.

A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage in Newtown, Lower Makefield, Northampton and Upper Makefield Townships. Trees and wires were knocked down. In Washington Crossing (Upper Makefield Township), downed trees damaged vehicles and fences. Some shingles were also peeled back from homes.

A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a three-story Victorian home on East Ridley Avenue in Ridley Park Borough. The fire was confined to the roof, but smoke damage occurred throughout the home.
A severe thunderstorm downed trees in Chester Township and Chester Borough. A section of County Route 510 (also known as State Route 24) was closed because of downed trees.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees in several additional municipalities in central Morris County. Downed trees were reported in Dover, Hanover, Montville, Morris Plains, Parsippany and Wharton. There were still 180 people without power in the county on the afternoon of the 18th.
A lightning strike caused a house fire in Hanover Township. No injuries were reported.
Dime to quarter size hail was reported by a Skywarn Spotter in Juniata Park.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees within Philadelphia from the West Mount Airy section east to the Wissinoming section. A Skywarn Spotter in Juniata Park estimated wind gusts of between 60 and 65 mph.
A severe thunderstorm dropped penny size hail in Levittown and quarter size hail in Morrisville Village. The thunderstorm also produced wind gusts of about 40 mph in Levittown.
A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs in Maple Shade Township. The same thunderstorm dropped pea to dime size hail.
A severe thunderstorm dropped hail up to the size of quarters in Hamilton Township.
The gust front from a severe thunderstorm tore down several trees and tree limbs in Voorhees Township.

A severe thunderstorm tore down a large tree across Forked Neck Road in Shamong Township. A vehicle veered to miss the falling the tree and ended in a ditch. No injuries were reported. A couple of other large tree limbs were pulled down in the township.
Quarter size hail fell in Forks Township.
A severe thunderstorm produced a measured wind gust of 62 mph in Forks Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Media, Upper Darby and Springfield.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Salford Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Lansdale Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few utility wires within the city of Chester.
A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees and tree limbs in Readington Township.
A severe thunderstorm tore down a couple of trees and wires in Branchburg Township.
A severe thunderstorm tore down a few trees in Bernards Township.
Penny size hail fell from a severe thunderstorm in Colora.
Quarter size hail fell from a severe thunderstorm in Hockessin (Mill Creek Hundred).
A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs and wires in the northern part of East Greenwich Township.
Nickel size hail fell from a severe thunderstorm in both Brookhaven and Upland.
A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees and wires across roadways west of Dover.
A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees, wires and telephone poles in Easton.
A severe thunderstorm dropped penny to nickel size hail in Centreville.
A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees in Preston. A downed tree also tore down a transformer.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Andover Township. The roof of an apartment building was also damaged.
A tree was knocked down onto the roof of a house during a thunderstorm.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in East Brunswick Township.
