A severe thunderstorm produced a swath of wind damage from downed trees, tree limbs to downed wires across the northeast half of Chester County. Many roadways were blocked and vehicles damaged by fallen trees. Trees also fell onto the Pennsylvania Turnpike. Hardest hit were Uwchlan, Wallace, West Vincent and Willistown Townships, but wind damage was also reported in North Coventry, Phoenixville, Charlestown, Downingtown, West Whiteland, West Goshen, East Goshen, West Chester, Westtown, Pocopson. Kenneth and Kenneth Square. Nearly 80,000 homes and businesses lost power and it took until June 28th for power to be fully restored. In West Chester, downed trees blocked the entrance to a hospital. Downed trees also damaged a home and garage and crushed a barn. In North Coventry, a downed tree punched a hole in the roof of a home.

Severe thunderstorms produced a swath of wind damage across the northeast half of Delaware County. Numerous trees and wires were knocked down. There were four times the normal number of calls into the county's 911 center. Because of the nearly 100,000 power outages in the county, dry ice was distributed in Havertown, Newtown Square and Springfield. A woman and her daughter were injured when a tree fell onto their vehicle in Lansdowne. A 300-year-old tree was knocked down onto Greenwood Avenue in the borough. Most of the borough lost power. In Upper Darby Township, the roof from the Today's Child Learning Center blew onto the SEPTA Regional Rail lines tracks near the Primos Station. The roof of another home was nearly torn away.  In all several homes and a park were damaged by fallen trees along Windermere Avenue. Another downed tree fell onto a moving vehicle, but the five occupants were not hurt. Firefighters rescued a 10-year-old boy with an iron lung. A Skywarn Spotter measured a wind gust of 76 mph. Because 15,000 residents lost power, an air conditioned comfort center was available at the Upper Darby High School Cafeteria.  In Haverford Township, a 30,000 volt transmission wire was knocked down and create a crater on a roadway. In Marple Township, windows were shattered and siding was stripped around the Lawrence Park Industrial Center. A large sign above the Five Guys Shopping Center was cracked. In Springfield Township around Dutton Circle and Valley View Road, windows and sidings were also damaged, roof shingles were also torn and at least one porch and vehicle were damaged by downed trees. The SEPTA Media/Elwyn line did not resume regional rail service until the evening of the 25th.

The same severe thunderstorm produced a swath of large hail (quarter to golf ball size) across eastern Delaware County from Haverford Township south through Yeadon Borough. The largest hail (golf ball size) was reported in Yeadon and ping pong ball size hail (1.5 inches in diameter) was reported in Drexel Hill in Upper Darby Township.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 65 knots or 75 mph at Philadelphia International Airport. This was the third highest gust ever recorded at the airport.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in the southern half of Philadelphia. There were 184 calls of downed trees with the Southwest Philadelphia and Cobbs Creek areas hit the hardest. A few streets were blocked by downed trees. Downed trees also blocked some of the lanes on the Schuylkill Expressway. Part of the roof was torn from the New Light Beulah Baptist Church on Bainbridge Street and crushed two vehicles.  Downed trees crushed a fence at Saint John Neumann Place in South Philadelphia. The awning of a banquet hall on West Oxford Street collapsed. The severe thunderstorm also lifted the tarp at Citizen Bank Baseball Park into the air. Trolley Wires were knocked down in the University City area.

A series of severe thunderstorms produced wind damage across Camden County from Haddon Heights Borough southeast into eastern sections of Winslow Township. Numerous trees and tree limbs were knocked down. About 40,000 Atlantic City Electric customers were still without power as of 1201 a.m. EDT on the 25th. Wind damage was reported in Haddon Heights Borough, Pine Hill Borough, Gloucester Township, Voorhees Township, Hi-Nella Borough, Stratford Borough and along the borders of Waterford and Winslow Townships. A shed was destroyed by a downed tree in Pine Hill Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees along U.S. Route 206 in Hammonton Township. About 2,300 homes and businesses lost power in the township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and tree limbs in Shamong Township. A 47-year-old woman died while camping at the Atsion Recreation Area within the township. A tree snapped and fell on top of a tent she as well as a 51-year-old man and 31-year-old woman were taking shelter within. The latter two suffered minor injuries. Another downed tree damaged a vehicle within the town.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees, tree limbs and wires in Salem County centered around Alloway Township.
A severe thunderstorm dropped quarter size hail in Mays Landing (Hamilton Township).
A severe thunderstorm dropped quarter to half dollar size hail within Atlantic City.

A severe thunderstorm dropped quarter size hail in a swath across southeastern Atlantic County from the William J. Hughes Technical Center and Pomona in Galloway Township southeast into the city of Absecon.

The same severe thunderstorm that dropped large hail in Galloway Township produced damaging winds. Dozens of trees were knocked down. On Tulip Avenue, a downed tree crashed through the roof of one house into the bedroom. Other downed trees in the township damaged fences and a deck.

A series of three severe thunderstorms affected Gloucester County and knocked down numerous trees, tree limbs and wires and caused some structural damage within the county. Emergency responders were dispatched to about 125 weather related incidents throughout the county. Except for Swedesboro and Elk Township, every municipality within the county had at least one weather related incident. The first severe thunderstorm affected the northeast quarter of the county the hardest. A structural collapse occurred at Bagelicious on Delsea Drive in Deptford Township. Three trees fell into one house on North Brentwood Avenue in Pitman Borough. The house was rendered uninhabitable. No serious injuries were reported.

The second in a series of three severe thunderstorms affected southwestern Gloucester County and in particular Franklin Township the hardest. There were about a dozen weather related incidents in the county. No serious injuries were reported.
The last in a series of three severe thunderstorms affected southeastern Gloucester County from Pitman Borough southeast into Monroe Township.
A second severe thunderstorm knocked over some additional trees in Winslow Township. One downed tree fell onto and damaged the roof of a house on Willard Way.
A lightning strike caused an apartment fire at the Campus Crossings Apartments in Glassboro.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Commercial and Maurice River Townships.
The second severe thunderstorm of the day to affect Chester County downed additional trees, tree limbs and wires in the southwestern part of the county.

A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage across central Sussex County in and to the north of Georgetown. The cab cover of one vehicle was torn off one truck and damaged a nearby car's windows. Downed wires were reported on Delaware State Route 113 in Georgetown. A mesonet site five miles north of Georgetown measured a wind gust to 61 mph.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in the southwestern part of Queen Anne's County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several large tree limbs and wires in Denton.

A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage across parts of the southern half of Cape May County. Trees and large tree limbs were knocked down in Middle Township. Wind gusts of 63 mph and 58 mph were measured in North Cape May and a wind gust of 57 mph was measured in Villas.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few large tree limbs onto roadways in Manahawkin (Stafford Township).
A lightning strike set a pole on fire in Ship Bottom. The combination of lightning strikes and stroke winds caused numerous outages on Long Beach Island.
A lightning strike damaged a chimney in Lavallette.

Lightning struck a building in a row of stores at the intersection of Main Street and Delilah Road in Pleasantville. It blew out an electric meter at one store. About 2,300 homes and businesses lost power in the city. Lightning strikes and wind also combined to cause about 1,500 homes and businesses to lose power in Brigantine and 1,200 in Absecon.
A severe thunderstorm tore down trees along Montgomery Avenue in Lower Merion Township.
Lightning struck a famous Yellowwood tree from the 1790s within Bartram's Garden. The Garden was closed on the 25th because of the damage.

A lightning strike created a foot wide hole in the roof of a house on Jasmine Road  in Lower Southampton Township. It ignited a wire within the attic and started a fire. Six different municipal responders assisted with the fire which was contained within 20 minutes.
A lightning strike set a barn on fire in Honey Brook.
A lightning strike and the ensuing fire destroyed two homes on Gramercy Lane in Uwchlan Township. No injuries were reported.
Quarter size hail fell in South Philadelphia.

Lightning struck a power line in Jefferson Township and caused about 2,000 homes and businesses to lose power at around 9 a.m. EDT on the 10th. Power was not restored until 7 p.m. EDT that evening.

A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs and wires in southern Hunterdon County. The combination of the winds and lightning caused about 1,000 Jersey Central Power and Light homes and businesses to lose power in Hunterdon and Warren Counties.

A severe thunderstorm tore down trees on Riverside Drive in Lower Saucon Township. Pennsylvania Power and Light reported about 2,400 homes and businesses lost power in the Lehigh Valley because of the lightning and winds.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding of the Monocacy Creek at the Colonial Industrial Quarter in Bethlehem around 8 a.m. EDT on the 10th. The creek flooded four structures in the area near the intersection of Main and West Church Streets. Tree branches slammed against the buildings and a couple of windows were broken. Rainfall reached 5.67 inches at the Lehigh Valley International Airport. The flooding in the area was described as the worst since the remnants of Hurricane Ivan in 2004. Up to about 5 feet of water accumulated within the 1761 Tannery, 1762 Waterworks and 1869 Luckenbach Mill. In the 1762 Waterworks, the 18 foot water wheel was clogged and damaged. In the 1761 Tannery, wooden vats were destroyed, the heating system was damaged and the wooden floor buckled.  There was concern about the 1762 Waterworks and the 1761 Tannery structural integrity. The two buildings took on water for the longest period of time. A few feet of water still occupied the buildings during the afternoon of the 10th. The rushing water also damaged the Springhouse and the ground floor of the 1869 Luckenbach Mill. Elsewhere in the Lehigh Valley, the Schoenersville exit to U.S. Route 22 was closed. Roads were closed due to floodng in Allentown and Bethlehem and basements were flooded in Catasauqua and Lower Nazareth Township. The Monocacy Creek at Bethlehem was above its 5 foot flood stage from 815 a.m. EDT through 1038 a.m. EDT on the 10th. It crested at 5.44 feet at 9 a.m. EDT.

A lightning strike destroyed a home in New Hope and killed the family's dog. It was believed that lightning initially struck the home's chimney before spreading. Four fire companies responded to the blaze. No injuries were reported.

An EF0 tornado touched down on the Lynn Acres Farm on Kistler Valley Road around 400 a.m. EDT.  Numerous trees were uprooted or snapped. Three homes, one significantly, were damaged by the fallen trees.    On the farm, a small barn had half its roof completely removed and other structures sustained roof damage. This included portions of a metal roof. Parts of the metal roof were found along the two mile damage path. There were numerous trees toppled or sheared off around the farm and along a ravine that runs through the farmland. Some of the corn in two separate fields was partially flattened. The tornado then traveled north near Sechler Road with several trees uprooted or sheared off along the way. The most widespread damage occurred near the intersection of Sechler Road and Wedge Drive where numerous large trees were completely uprooted or sheared off about 20 feet above the ground. Two homes were damaged on Sechler Road by the downed trees. The tornado then appeared to have lifted at times as the damage was more sporadic. The tornado continued on a northward track and dissipated near the intersection of Decatur Street, Pennsylvania State Route 143 and Madison Street. Two large trees were completely uprooted and damaged the chimney and roof of the back of one home at that intersection. The tornado's path length was about 2.2 miles. Its maximum path length was 150 yards and its estimated maximum wind speed was 80 mph. No injuries were reported.

A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 69 mph at the Lehigh Valley International Airport and knocked down trees within Allentown. The combination of damaging wind and lightning caused about 15,000 homes and businesses to lose power, in the Lehigh Valley, 10,000 of the outages were in Lehigh County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Lower Macungie Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a fence and tossed a trampoline in Northampton Borough. The combination of damaging winds and lightning caused about 5,000 homes and businesses to lose power in Northampton County, most in Northampton Borough and Lehigh Township.
Golf ball size hail fell in New Garden Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in East Marlborough Township, one fallen tree damaged a home.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous large trees in Kenneth Square and Kenneth Township. Many homes within Kennett Square sustained water damage after the fallen trees created holes in the roofs. The combination of the damaging winds and lightning across southern Chester County caused power outages that lasted up to twenty-four hours. Of the 45,000 homes and businesses that lost power in the PECO energy service area, Chester County was hardest hit.

A lightning strike and a subsequent fire damaged several trailers in Shaner's Trailer Park on East Main Street in Lower Pottsgrove Township. Lightning was believed to hit either a water or electrical line and then started a fire under one trailer. One woman was injured and hospitalized. Two other trailers were also damaged by the fire. The lightning strike also shorted the phone and cable lines. Two families were displaced.
A severe thunderstorm tore down several large tree limbs in Whitpain and Plymouth Townships.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in northeastern and eastern Bucks County. Trees were knocked down in both directions on Pennsylvania State Route 32 in Yardley Borough and in Lower Makefield Township. The roadway was blocked into the 26th in Lower Makefield Township. Two downed trees also crushed two vehicles. No injuries were reported. Both Bucks and Chester Counties took the brunt of the power outages (45,000) in PECO Energy's service area.

A severe thunderstorm tore down trees and signs in Philadelphia. In the Torresdale section, a home was damaged by a downed tree. A large maple tree was blown down onto Roxborough Avenue between Houghton Street and Ridge Road.
A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees and wires across the northern tier of New Castle County. One tree fell onto a home in Talleysville.
A severe thunderstorm knocked a few trees down in Bear.
A severe thunderstorm split a large tree in half and also tore down several large tree limbs in Frankford.
A mesonet site measured a wind gust of 58 mph in Lewes.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and tree limbs in Georgetown. One downed large tree knocked down a fence and a screened in porch of one home in the Cinderberry section of the town.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Perryville.  Some poor drainage flooding also occurred during the thunderstorm.

A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage in and near Kent Island in Queen Anne's County. The Kent Island Volunteer Fire Department had their tents blown down. A greater than 100-year-old linden tree fell onto the Kent Island Federation of Art Building in Stevensville. Elsewhere in Stevensville, a grill was tossed into a pool. A motorcyclist was not injured after he rode into a downed tree.  Wind damage extended into Grasonville where some large tree limbs were pulled down. Scattered outages on Kent Island lasted up to six hours. A Skywarn spotter measured a wind gust of 62 mph on Kent Island. Also 0.70 inches of rain fell in ten minutes and caused poor drainage flooding.
A Skywarn spotter measured a wind gust of 71 mph at Knapps Narrows on Tilghman Island during a severe thunderstorm.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Easton. A Skywarn spotter estimated wind gusts of 60 to 65 mph.

A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage across several municipalities in Caroline County. Numerous trees and wires were knocked down, some were greater than 100 years old. Choptank Electric and Delmarva Power and Light reported about 3,000 homes and businesses lost power in the county. Power was not fully restored until 5 a.m. EDT on the 26th. In Denton, the porch railings were ripped away from one home and porch furniture was tossed two hundred feet. Numerous trees were knocked down from Asbury off of Maryland State Route 328 southeast through the Caroline Country Club. In Federalsburg, the damaging winds caused roof damage to one home and Henry's Furniture Store. Dover Doppler Radar was measuring winds of around 85 mph at 1,300 feet above Denton.
The gust front from a severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Morris Plains. One downed tree damaged a vehicle.

A squall line of severe thunderstorms knocked down trees in several townships throughout Hunterdon County. Downed trees were reported in Clinton, Delaware, Franklin and West Amwell Townships. Some fell across roadways. In West Amwell Township, a downed tree completely closed Gulick Road.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in Trenton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in and around Clayton. At least one downed tree damaged a home.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Franklin Township. At least one downed tree damaged a home.
The gust front from a severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees as well as fifty feet of fencing at one property on Hinchman Avenue in Cherry Hill.
The gust front from a severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Mount Laurel Township.
A Skywarn spotter estimated wind gusts of 70 mph in Buena Vista Township.
The Millville Municipal Airport reported a measured wind gust of 51 knots or 59 mph during the severe thunderstorm in Cumberland County.

Severe thunderstorms produced a swath of wind damage across central Cumberland County. Numerous trees, wires and poles were damaged. Atlantic City Electric, reported about 30 percent of its customers, 12,000, lost power in the county. A microburst occurred around the Pleasant Drive area of Millville and produced about a half mile of intense tree damage. Wind gusts were estimated around 70 mph.|Wind damage was reported in Bridgeton, Commerical, Port Elizabeth and Vineland, but the worst wind damage occurred within Millville. Within Millville, three major roadways were closed. A sedan on Fulton Street was totaled by a downed tree. There were still about 5,100 homes and businesses without power the following evening, the 26th.
A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs and wires in Woodbine. Power outages were reported.
A severe thunderstorm tore down trees and wires in Northfield. Power outages were reported.
A trained spotter estimated wind gusts of 60 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Egg Harbor Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees in North Cape May.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees along the Garden State Parkway at mile marker 21.8.
A funnel cloud was sited over Atlantic City, but did not reach the ground.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused small stream and considerable urban and poor drainage flash flooding in and around Wilmington. A couple of major roadways were flooded and closed including Old Airport Road and Lancaster Avenue. A woman's vehicle stalled while trying to pass through a parking lot lake in Edgemoor off the Governor Prinz Boulevard.  Storm totals included 2.78 inches in Wilmington and 2.45 inches at the New Castle County Airport.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding along the Frankford Creek as well as poor drainage flooding in central Philadelphia. The heavy rain also caused the tracks for the Market-Frankford el to be underwater. Service was suspended between 9 a.m. EDT and 2 p.m. EDT. The Frankford Creek at Castor Avenue was above its 7 foot flood stage from 859 a.m. EDT through 1258 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 11.28 feet at 10 a.m. EDT.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding along the Pennypack Creek as well as poor drainage flooding in northeast Philadelphia. A 20-year-old man drowned while rafting on the swollen Pennypack Creek. During the morning, fire officials rescued a man stuck next to the pillar of a rail bridge near the intersection of Ashburner Street and Frankford Avenue on the creek. Later that day, two men fell into the water after their raft overturned near Winchester Avenue and Roosevelt Boulevard, but only one man survived. The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge was above its 7 foot flood stage from 1018 a.m. EDT through 617 p.m. EDT EDT on the 13th. It crested at 9.1 feet at 4 p.m. EDT.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding along the Wissahickon Creek as well as in northern Philadelphia. Lincoln Drive along the creek was flooded. The Wissahickon Creek at its mouth was above its 5 foot flood stage from 910 a.m. EDT through 1031 a.m. EDT EDT on the 13th. It crested at 5.64 feet at 10 a.m. EDT.

Runoff from the morning heavy rain caused flooding along the East Branch of the Brandywine Creek during the afternoon of the 10th. The East Branch of the Brandywine Creek at Downingtown was above its 7 foot flood stage from 1225 p.m. EDT through 146 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 7.16 feet at 1 p.m. EDT.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding along roadways and small creeks that surround the Cooper River in Camden. Both the Admiral Wilson Boulevard and U.S. Route 130 were closed due to flooding between 10 a.m. and Noon EDT. A Skywarn Spotter in Camden recorded 2.40 inches in 80 minutes.
Flash flooding caused the closure of the Schuylkill Expressway along the Conshohocken Curve from Belmont to City Avenues between 930 a.m. EDT and 1130 a.m. EDT.

A man was rescued from the roof of his car along the intersection of Tookany Creek Parkway and Central Avenue in Cheltenham. The Tookany Creek flooded after a Doppler Radar estimated three to four inches of rain fell during the morning of the 13th in lower Montgomery County.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in and around Wilmington. The flooding forced the safe evacuation of nearly three dozen infant and toddlers at an Elsmere day care center on Kirkwood Highway. The highway had up to four feet of water on it and was closed between Maple Avenue and Saunders Road. A bakery was also damaged by the flooding as were about 14 vehicles at the Veterans Affair Medical Center. In Wilmington, fire fighters made three water rescues. A man in his 50s was injured trying to rescue a woman stuck in flood waters. Three major roadways were closed including Governor Printz Boulevard. Elsewhere flooding along the Noneguch Creek near New Castle flooded Airport Road and several vehicles were stuck in high water in New Castle. The two day Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 6 to 8 inches in the area.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller creeks as well as considerable highway and poor drainage flooding. In Trainer Borough, the Stoney Brook Creek flooded. Cars became stuck in three feet of water at the intersection of Main and Pennsylvania Streets in the borough. Interstates 476 and 95 as well as McDade Boulevard (within Darby) were flooded. Poor drainage flooding was also reported in Norwood, Prospect Park, Ridley and Tinicum Townships. Two day Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 5 to 6 inches in Delaware County. The actual two day precipitation total at the Philadelphia International Airport was 4.31 inches.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding as well as considerable highway and poor drainage flooding in south Philadelphia. The ramps to Interstate 95 were closed at Broad Street. The heavy rain also caused incoming flight delays of 90 minutes at Philadelphia International Airport. Two day Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 6 to 8 inches in southwestern Philadelphia. The actual two day precipitation total at the Philadelphia International Airport was 4.31 inches.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding of smaller creeks as well as considerable highway and poor drainage flooding in northwest Gloucester County. In Paulsboro, New Jersey State Route 44 was closed at Berkeley Road near the Mantua Creek. Two day Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 5 to 6 inches in Gloucester County. The actual two day precipitation total at the Philadelphia International Airport was 4.31 inches.
Torrential downpours and flooding forced the closure of the on and off ramps of Interstate 676 at Atlantic Avenue in Camden. The Ferry Avenue PATCO High Speed Line stop was also flooded.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours also caused stream and urban flooding in other parts of Camden, Collingswood, Pennsauken, Haddon Township, Mount Ephraim and Gloucester City. Considerable flooding was reported along U.S. Route 130 from Gloucester City north into Pennsauken.  Along the Cooper River in Camden, Baird Boulevard was flooded near U.S. Route 30. Two day Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 4 to 5 inches in Camden County. In Pennsauken, 3.65 inches of rain fell in two and a half hours on the afternoon of the 14th.

All lanes of New Jersey State Route 70 near Kings Highway in Cherry Hill Township were closed for about an hour because of flash flooding. Flooding along the South Branch of the Pennsauken Creek flooded Cornwall Road in Cherry Hill Township also.

Torrential downpours caused the closure of Northbound State Route 73 near Greentree Road in Evesham Township. Two day Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 5 to 6 inches in Burlington County. At South Jersey Regional Airport in Lumberton Township, 3.72 inches of rain fell during the afternoon of the 14th.
Thunderstorms with torrential downpours dropped 2.34 inches of rain in 40 minutes in Hammonton Township and caused small stream and roadway flooding in the township.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 60 mph in Ewing Township.
A wind gust to 56 knots (64 mph) was measured in Florence Township during a severe thunderstorm. Several large tree limbs were knocked down in the township.
A tree was snapped by a severe thunderstorm in Mount Laurel Township just off of Union Mill Road. A few other large tree limbs were knocked down in and around the township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a tree and several large tree limbs in the Middleport area of Seaford.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a tree and several large tree limbs in Federalsburg.

A squall line of severe thunderstorms knocked down trees and wires in multiple areas across the southwestern half of Talbot County from Saint Michaels through Royal Oak and Trappe. A wind gust of 55 mph was measured in Royal Oak.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and caused cosmetic and isolated roof damage to homes on Tilghman Island.

Lightning struck a home on Bay Front Drive on Tilghman Island and started a fire on the morning of the 12th. It took firefighters about 20 minutes to extinguish the blaze. Damage was estimated at $5,300. The thunderstorm complex was a prolific lightning producer through Maryland. Lightning rates as it moved across the Eastern Shore were around 1,000 cloud-to-ground strokes per hour. About 800 homes and businesses lost power in Talbot County. Outages were reported on Tilghman Island in Tilghman, Sherwood and Wittman. Other outages in Talbot County were reported in Saint Michaels, Neavitt, Bozman and Trappe. All power was restored by 4 pm EDT on the afternoon of the 12th.

A positive cloud-to-ground lightning strike caused a barn fire just north of the Pole Tavern Traffic Circle on New Jersey State Route 77 in Upper Pittsgrove Township. Lightning struck the peak of the barn and traveled down through the silo. Sparks flew onto hay stored in the barn and started the fire. All 326 bales of hay along with heavy equipment were destroyed. No injuries were reported.
A severe thunderstorm tore down a few trees and wires in Honey Brook Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Manalapan Township. One tree fell onto a home.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several large tree limbs in Monroe Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs in Cranbury Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Plainsboro Township.

A lightning strike and the ensuing fire destroyed a vacant one story barn at the intersection of Friendship and New Roads in South Brunswick Township. It took about thirty firefighters forty-five minutes to extinguish the blaze.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Hopewell Township, a couple of which blocked roadways.

A severe thunderstorm caused extensive tree damage on and to the east of Princeton University in Princeton Borough. Wind damage was reported from Nassau Street to Carnegie Lake. Several homes and vehicles were damaged by fallen trees along Harrison Street, Sycamore Road and Cedar Lane. Four homes were badly damaged as were vehicles on the Butler Tract off of Harrison Street. This included graduate student housing. Some students and families were evacuated to the Frist Campus Center. On the university grounds itself, trees were knocked down around Palmer Stadium, along the intersection of Faculty Road and Broadmead Street, Ivy Lane and along Washington Road. In Princeton Township,  wind damage occurred on the opposite side of Carnegie Lake along Plainsboro Road as far east as Connector Road. Some roadways remained closed due to the fallen trees into the 17th. Power was fully restored on the 18th. No injuries were reported.

Thunderstorms dropped a Doppler Radar estimated up to four inches of rain across extreme southeast Sussex County. This caused stream, field and poor drainage flooding.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding on Brigantine Island including Atlantic City. Flooding was reported on many side streets and roadways toward Lakes and Absecon Bays in Atlantic City. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 3.73 inches just west of Atlantic City. An actual storm total of 3.58 inches was measured in Margate City.

An EF-0 tornado touched down in Chester City on the afternoon of the 22nd. The first wind damage occurred near the intersection of 4th and Engle Streets where a couple of trees and a garage was blown down.  A nearly continuous path of tree damage then occurred to the 2000 block of Third Street where several trees were blown down and structural damage occurred to a building and its roof.  Additional damage occurred in a continuous path to the intersection of Pennsylvania State Route 291 and Reaney Street where a house incurred siding and roof damage. The tornado then lifted as it approached the Commodore Barry Bridge where planks were ripped off the new Interstate 95 ramp being constructed. The path length of the tornado was approximately 0.33 miles and its maximum path width was 80 yards. The estimated maximum wind speed was 75 mph. No injuries were reported.
A severe thunderstorm downed large tree limbs and wires in Mantua Township and Woodbury City.
A severe thunderstorm downed large tree limbs and wires in Pitman Borough.
A severe thunderstorm downed large tree limbs and wires in Monroe Township.
Quarter size hail fell in Montague.
Nickel size hail fell in Sparta.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust to 70 mph in Keansburg and knocked down a few trees.
Penny size hail fell in Nazareth.
A funnel cloud was sighted passing over New Castle County Airport.  It did not touch down.
A severe thunderstorm caused roof damage to a New Castle County Government Center building on Reads Way in Wilmington. Several trees and tree limbs were also knocked down and damaged one vehicle.

An EF-0 tornado moved through New London Township during the afternoon of the 27th. The tornado touched down south of the intersection of Pennsylvania State Route 896 and Saginaw Road and just to the north of  State Road. The tornado moved north and crossed West Avondale Road before it lifted. The tornado touched down one more time in a wooded area behind the Avon Grove Intermediate School. Numerous trees were snapped and a few homes suffered siding and roof damage. A car was also tossed by the tornado. No injuries were reported. The tornado's path length was approximately 1.4 miles and its maximum path width was 100 yards. The estimated maximum wind speed was 70 mph.

An EF-1 tornado touched down in Plumsted Township in Ocean County at about 605 p.m. EDT on the 16th. The tornado remained on the ground for about 2.2 miles. The tornado touched down  just north of the intersection of Long Swamp Road and Archertown Road in the township.  The tornado traveled eastnortheast crossing Ocean County Route 539 and lifted near Hawkins Road or Prospertown-Colliers Mills Road near Colliers Lake. The worst damage occurred along East Colliers Mills Road where a house suffered serious roof damage and a dormer was blown off. A neighboring house also suffered roof damage. One small barn was destroyed and another was blown over. A few vehicles were damaged by fallen trees. Numerous small trees and a few large ones were snapped along the tornado's path.  An estimated 300 trees were knocked down. The tornado's path length was about 2.2 miles, its maximum path width 250 yards and the estimated maximum wind speeds were 90 mph.
Lightning struck a house and a tree in Elkton and caused a house fire. No injuries were reported.
A Skywarn Spotter measured a wind gust of 59 mph in Bear.

A wet microburst associated with a severe thunderstorm caused considerable tree and some wind damage in Perth Amboy. The estimated maximum wind speed was about 80 mph and struck the historic district in the southeast part of Perth Amboy the hardest. About 15 to 20 homes and buildings were damaged. One family on Paterson Street had to be relocated because the roof over the front door of their home became detached. A state of emergency was declared and only emergency responders were permitted to travel through the southeast part of the city. It was lifted on the 18th when most streets were passable again. There was a measured wind gust of 73 mph within Perth Amboy.  A funnel cloud also passed across the city, but did not touch down.  Damage from the microburst occurred in an area bounded by 2nd Street to the west, Smith Street to the north, and the waterfront on the east and south. The most concentrated damage occurred on Water, Market and High Streets. Snapped trees and tree branches were the prevalent damage type, but roof and chimney damage also occurred in several locations. A couple of cars were also damaged by downed trees. No homes experienced significant structural damage, but several garages were badly damaged by either the winds themselves or collaterally from flying and/or falling debris. One minor injury due to flying debris occurred along First Street. The worst damage was located in a two-block area bounded by Second Street, Gordon Street, Madison Avenue and Lewis Street. Several large trees and numerous power lines were blown down, and structural damage occurred to several garages. Numerous houses in this area suffered roof damage, mainly in the form of lost shingles and damaged or destroyed chimneys. Several homes had sections of roofs torn away. A roof was also torn from one industrial building along Second Street, portions of which were transported several blocks away. Extensive tree damage also occurred in and near Bayview Park. Personnel from the city of Perth Amboy and the city of Woodbridge worked through the night to clean up the storm debris.
A funnel cloud was sighted along U.S. Route 9 in Old Bridge.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Woodbridge.

A squall line of severe thunderstorms knocked down trees and wires in numerous locations throughout Monmouth County. Hardest hit within the county was in the Freehold area. About 3,500 of the 10,000 outages reported by Jersey Central Power and Light occurred in and around Freehold. An additional 1,000 outages occurred in Brielle. The outbound New Jersey Transit North Coast Rail Commuter Line between Hazlet and Long Branch experienced up to 30 minute delays because of downed trees.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires in the northwest half of Gloucester County including Sewell and Glassboro.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees in Voorhees Township. In Gloucester Township, the same line of thunderstorms produced a measured wind gust of 54 mph in Blackwood.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a telephone pole in Southampton Township. A Skywarn spotter's anemometer was broken by the damaging winds. At nearby South Jersey Regional Airport in Lumberton Township, a measured wind gust of 55 mph occurred.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 61 mph at the Lakehurst NAS.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Lakewood Township and damaged a few cars. Downed trees and wires were reported on Bradshaw Road, Caronetta Drive, Cross Street, Oak Street, Ocean Avenue, South Lake Drive and U.S. Route 9.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Jackson Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees onto vehicles in Hamilton Township. No injuries were reported.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down about a dozen trees across Carbon County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires in Upper Mount Bethel Township.
Penny size hail fell in Allentown.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in and around Allentown. A Skywarn Spotter estimated wind gusts at 60 mph.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Greenwich Township.
Penny size hail fell in Bernville.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees in Washington Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in Bushkill Township and also in Tatamy.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in Mansfield and Independence Townships as well as Hackettstown.

The gust front from a severe thunderstorm caused wind damage in Mercer County mainly in Ewing and Hopewell Townships. A meteorologist measured a wind gust of 60 mph in Ewing. New Jersey State Route 29 along the Hopewell and Ewing border was shut down because of downed trees. One lane of New Jersey State Route 31 was also closed because of downed trees. Elsewhere in the county, stands were knocked over and equipment knocked down at an Italian-American festival in Hamilton Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in and around Flemington.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires across the southern tier of Somerset County in Hillsborough, Montgomery and Franklin Townships. In Montgomery Township, uprooted saplings were thrown into and damaged two moving vehicles. The drivers were not injured. Four roadways were closed because of debris. In Franklin Township, the Griggstown Causeway was closed because of a snapped utility pole. There were two dozen reports of downed trees in the township.
A lightning strike caused a transformer fire on Easton Avenue in Montgomery Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Sayreville, Old Bridge and South Amboy. The combination of lightning and damaging winds caused about 1,500 homes and businesses to lose power in Middlesex County. Power was full restored early on the 23rd.

Penny size hail fell in Newark.

A line of severe thunderstorms caused wind damage mainly along the western tier hundreds of New Castle County, especially along the border with Maryland. In Blackbird Hundred, trees were knocked down along Green Giant Road and Blackbird Station Road. In Stanton (Mill Creek Hundred), a 200-year-old oak tree took down cable and phone lines. The combination of lightning and damaging wind caused about 4,500 homes and businesses to lose power in New Castle County. Outages were concentrated from Middletown southward to Smyrna in Kent County and from the Saint Georges area east through New Castle. All power was restored by the evening of the 23rd.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees on properties located near the Cecil County border with Delaware. The combination of damaging winds and lightning caused about 5,800 homes and businesses to lose power in Cecil County. Power was not fully restored until the evening of the 23rd.
A severe thunderstorm produced a 51 knot wind gust (59 mph) as it moved across Sandy Hook.
A severe thunderstorm produced a 62 mph wind gust as it moved across Keansburg.

The East Ditch at Beaver Brook Road was above its 2.5 foot flood stage from 829 a.m. EDT on the 30th through 1140 a.m. EDT on the 30th. It crested at 2.69 feet at 925 a.m. EDT. The event precipitation total (including October 1st) was 4.79 inches in Parsippany-Troy Hills.

Heavy rain during the morning of the 30th caused flooding along the Big Elk Creek in Elkton. Delaware Avenue was closed due to flooding. Event precipitation totals (including October 1st) included 7.74 inches in Elkton.

The Lehigh River at Stoddartsville (along the Monroe and Luzerne County line) was above its 7 foot flood stage from 1118 p.m. EDT on September 30th through 733 p.m. EDT on October 1st. It crested at 11.74 feet at 515 a.m. EDT on October 1st. The event precipitation total (through October 1st) was 7.19 inches in Mount Pocono.

The Valley Creek near Valley Forge was above its 7 foot flood stage from 1236 a.m. EDT through 937 a.m. EDT on October 1st. It crested at 12.83 feet at 445 a.m. EDT on October 1st. The event precipitation total (through October 1st) was 8.25 inches in West Chester..

Lightning struck the roof of one apartment building in the Mill Pond development in Eatontown. The ensuing fire spread into the attic of the building. About three apartments sustained fire damage and all units below them suffered water and smoke damage, Tenants from all twenty-four units were evacuated for at least one night. Five municipalities assisted in extinguishing the fire. No injuries were reported.
Lightning struck a home on Clayton Drive in Millstone. The strike caused electrical damage to the home.

A lightning strike sparked a large fire on a farm in Douglass Township. Lightning struck in the middle of bales of hay on the farm and quickly spread. Between 300 and 375 bales of hay were consumed by the fire. The fire was not totally extinguished until 3 p.m. EDT the next day. About 200,000 tons of hay burned. Twenty-one separate fire companies assisted in fighting the fire. No injuries were reported.

The first round of heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding and small stream flooding during the day on the 30th mainly in the western half of Chester County. In Honeybrook Township, westbound Beaver Dam Road near South Birdell Road flooded. A vehicle stalled in the flood waters and the driver had to be rescued. In Caln Township, the 11th Avenue Bridge was inaccessible. In West Vincent Township, Horseshoe Trail was closed because of flooding between Pennsylvania State Route 113 and Chantilly Road. The Octorara School district dismissed children early because of flooded roads. Two day (including October 1st) storm totals included 9.79 inches in Kennett Square, 8.25 inches in West Chester, 7.49 inches in Nottingham, 7.36 inches in Unionville and 7.27 inches in Spring City.
Penny size hail fell in White House Station.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees near Boonton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires across the northern portion of Camden County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a tree, tore down several tree limbs and tossed a trampoline into a neighbor's yard over an eight foot fence.

Lightning struck the electrical box in the front of a log cabin home in Hopatcong and ignited a fire that engulfed the unoccupied dwelling. The fire was under control within a hour, but the interior of the cabin was gutted with extensive smoke and fire damage on both floors.

Flooding started early in the morning on October 1st. Governor Jack Markell declared a limited state of emergency in Delaware because of the flooding in Edgemoor.. The worst flood damage occurred in Edgemoor when the Shellpot Creek flooded and tore away a small bridge and gas lines on Colony Boulevard between 2 a.m. EDT and 3 a.m. EDT on the 1st and trapped about 1000 residents in their homes at the Summit Chase Colony North and Las Casas Apartments. In Christina, flooding along the Christina River forced the evacuation of about 25 families along East Main Street. Nineteen families were evacuated from the Kingsmill Mobile Home Park in Kirkwood after a small creek flooded. In Hockessin, houses near Mill Creek had basement flooding. The basement wall of a home on Halcon Drive near New Castle collapsed. Dozens of roads throughout the county flooded and there were numerous water rescues that included ones in Stanton, Newport and Wilmington. A mudslide closed Delaware State Route 141 near Newport. Two school districts closed for the day.| |The Brandywine Creek at Wilmington was above its 16.5 foot flood stage from 335 a.m. EDT through 1122 p.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 17.69 feet at 6 p.m. EDT.  The Christina River at Coochs Bridge had major flooding, had its fourth highest crest on record and was the highest crest since September of 2004 with the remnants of Hurricane Jeanne. The river was above its 10.5 foot flood stage from 112 a.m. EDT through 1002 a.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 13.06 feet at 615 a.m. EDT.  The Red Clay Creek at Wooddale had major flooding and tied the fourth highest crest on record. It was the highest crest since June of 2006. The creek was above its 7 foot flood stage from 210 a.m. EDT through 1057 a.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 10.91 feet at 745 a.m. EDT.  Farther downstream,  the Red Clay Creek at Stanton had moderate flooding and its fourth highest crest on record. It was its highest crest since September of 2004 with the remnants of Hurricane Jeanne. The creek was above its 15 foot flood stage from 123 a.m. EDT through 1252 p.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 19.84 feet at 845 a.m. EDT. The White Clay Creek at Newark was above its 13 foot flood stage from 133 a.m. EDT through 136 p.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 16.0 feet at 445  a.m. EDT. ||Event precipitation totals included 9.32 inches in Claymont, 7.89 inches in Newport, 7.83 inches in Middletown and 7.58 inches at the New Castle County Airport.

The Big Elk Creek flooded in Elkton during the morning of the 1st. A shopping center at Bridge Street was flooded as was Howard Street. Elsewhere in Cecil County, Winding Brook Village northeast of Elkton flooded. There was flooding in downtown Perryville. In Charlestown, flooding occurred along Maryland State Route 7 and Broad Street. School buses were detoured around flooded roads. Event precipitation totals were 8.00 inches in Conowingo, 6.74 inches in Elkton and 6.60 inches in Colora.

The Aquashicola Creek at Palmerton was above its 7 foot flood stage from 1040 a.m. EDT through 142 p.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 7.26 feet at 1230 p.m. EDT.   The Tobyhanna Creek at Blakeslee along the Carbon and Monroe County line was above its 10 foot flood stage from 425 a.m. EDT through 930 a.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 10.33 feet at 615 a.m. EDT.||Precipitation totals included 9.44 inches in Jim Thorpe, 7.96 inches in Lehighton and 7.42 inches in Palmerton.

The Lehigh River at Stoddartsville had moderate flooding, its fourth highest crest on record and its highest crest since June of 2006. The river was above its 7 foot flood stage from 1118 p.m. EDT on September 30th through 733 p.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 11.74 feet at 515 a.m. EDT on October 1st. The Tobyhanna Creek at|Blakeslee along the Carbon and Monroe County line was above its 10 foot flood stage from 425 a.m. EDT through 930 a.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 10.33 feet at 615 a.m. EDT.||Precipitation totals included 10.45 inches in Blakeslee, 7.26 inches in Mount Pocono and 5.29 inches in East Stroudsburg.

The Little Lehigh Creek at Allentown was above its 6 foot flood  stage from 432 a.m. EDT through 954 a.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested  at 6.92 feet at 745 a.m. EDT.  The Lehigh River at Walnutport along the Lehigh and Northampton County line was above its 8 foot flood  stage from 446 a.m. EDT through 218 p.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested| at 9.11 feet at 1015 a.m. EDT. ||Precipitation totals included 8.08 inches at the Lehigh Valley International Airport. 7.26 inches in Chapman and 5.59 inches in Schnecksville.

Four homes were evacuated along Norwood Street in Bethlehem because of flooding along the Saucon Creek. Basement flooding occurred. The Lehigh River at Walnutport along the Lehigh and Northampton County line was above its 8 foot flood stage from 446 a.m. EDT through 218 p.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 9.11 feet at 1015 a.m. EDT. Farther downstream, the Lehigh River at Glendon was above its 19 foot flood stage from 857 a.m. EDT through 315 p.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 19.34 feet at 11 a.m. EDT. The Monocacy Creek at Bethlehem was above its 4.5 foot flood stage from 203 a.m. EDT through 835 a.m. EDT on the 1st and again from 1037 a.m. EDT through 426 p.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 5.94 feet at 415 a.m. EDT.||Event precipitation totals included 8.85 inches in Bath, 8.58 inches in Easton and 6.71 inches in Walnutport.

The Manatawny Creek at Spangville was above its 6 foot flood stage from 320 a.m. EDT through 1243 p.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 7.42 feet at 8 a.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 7.25 inches at the Blue Marsh Dam, 6.46 inches in Reading and 5.40 inches in Hamburg.

While the Delaware River did not reach the established flood stage at Trenton, New Jersey, a significant rise occurred in the river. A breakaway barge had to be guided under the New Hope-Lambertville Bridge which was closed until that occurred. Both Yardley and Lower Makefield closed River Road as waters from the Delaware River crept a few inches onto the roadway. Roadway flooding and closures including Erie Road were reported in Quakertown as the Tohickon Creek flooded.||The East Branch of the Perkiomen Creek at Dublin was above its 5 foot flood stage from 318 a.m. EDT through 602 a.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 6.30 feet at 415 a.m. EDT. The Little Neshaminy Creek at Neshaminy was above its 8 foot flood stage from 630 a.m. EDT through 843 a.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 8.36 feet at 745 a.m. EDT. The Neshaminy Creek at Langhorne was above its 9 foot flood stage from 751 a.m. EDT through 701 p.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 10.48 feet at 245 p.m. EDT.||Event precipitation totals included 7.50 inches in Sellersville, 5.53 inches in Doylestown and 4.01 inches in Bensalem.

The Perkiomen Valley was hit the hardest by flooding in Montgomery County. A 55-year-old woman drowned after she drove into flood waters of the Skippack Creek on the morning of October 1st off Stump Hall road just north of Anders Road near Evansburg State Park near Skippack. Near Schwenksville, two men were swept into the East Branch of the Perkiomen Creek as they tried to drive over the Park Avenue Bridge. They were rescued from the creek about eight hours later. The sewage treatment plant was flooded in Schwenksville.  In Collegeville, there were eight rescues. Homes along the Skippack Pike near the Skippack Creek were flooded. In Lower Salford Township, a vehicle rescue occurred near the intersection of Quarry and Store Roads. Several roads were closed in Towamencin Township, many along the Skippack Creek. An ambulance became stuck on the bridge over the Skippack Creek on Old Forty Foot Road. In Teleford, there were five rescues. Along the Schuylkill River, Riverfront Park flooded in Pottstown and two homeless people were rescued. In West Norriton, about 200 people were evacuated from the Jefferson Villa Apartment after its basement flooded with Schuylkill River water. The King of Prussia Mall flooded and forced the closure of one store and the food court. In all one home was destroyed and another suffered major damage. One business suffered major flood damage. There was moderate damage at the King of Prussia mall complex in the food court area and ninety-three other homes suffered minor damage. Major flooding occurred in eastern Morris County and started on the 7th. Sections of the Pompton and Passaic Rivers never had a chance to recede before the next round of heavy rain arrived on the 10th. The worst flooding and damaged occurred after the second round of heavy rain.  Nevertheless, about twenty homes were evacuated in Lincoln Park when the Pompton River crested the first time. During the second and more serious round of flooding, over 1,000 homes were affected by flood waters in Pequannock and Lincoln Park. The American Red Cross and Salvation Army distributed nearly 4,000 meals and 4,500 snacks. The American Red Cross also distributed nearly 700 clean-up kits and 200 bulk items. Pumps, fans, wet vacs and dehumidifiers were in demand. In Pequannock, 1,300 homes were affected by flood waters and around 100 homes were damaged. About 1,500 people were evacuated and 2,000 residents affected by the flood waters. The hardest hit area was the lower village south of Jackson Avenue, by Madison Avenue and east of the Newark-Pompton Turnpike. New Jersey State Route 23 was closed and was flooded at its intersection with Jackson Avenue.  The National Guard dispatched five high water rescue vehicles. Barricades and bagging helped minimize flood damage to a shopping center off of New Jersey State Route 23. In Lincoln Park, twelve homes were evacuated and 200 homes were affected by flood waters. A shelter was opened in the borough. Riveredge Road was under three feet of water. U.S. Route 202 was closed. Firefighters needed a boat to fight one fire.||The Passaic River at Pine Brook had major flooding with its second crest and was above its 19 foot flood stage from 430 p.m. EST on the 7th through 1245 a.m. EDT on the 18th. The first crest was 20.09 feet at 9 p.m. EST on the 8th. The next crest was 22.04 feet at 1130 p.m.EST on the 12th and that was the sixth highest crest on record. events.event_narrative: A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 54 knots (62 mph) at Ship John Shoal Light.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and power lines in western Salem County in and around Carney's Point Township.

A line of severe showers and thunderstorms tore down tree limbs and a few trees mainly in the northwest part of Cecil County. The combination of the thunderstorm and synoptic scale winds caused about 4,500 homes and businesses to lose power in Cecil County on the 5th.
The gust front from a severe thunderstorm knocked down several large tree limbs in Millington.

Lightning during a thunderstorm ignited a barn fire on Huckleberry Road in Orefield in South Whitehall Township. The barn filled with smoke, but the fire was extinguished quickly and the damage was minimized.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees within Jim Thorpe.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and power lines in East Stroudsburg.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees and power lines in Easton.

A lightning strike and subsequent fire engulfed a home on Merion Lane in Jackson Township. The house suffered extensive structural damage and a Honda Pilot was also badly damaged. Seven fire companies battled the blaze. No serious injuries were reported.

A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees, tree limbs and wires as it moved across eastern Sussex County. In Stillwater Township, a downed pole blocked and closed Dove Island Road into the 16th. About 500 homes and businesses lost power in the area.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees on and around Curly Hill, Silo Hill and Gayman Roads in Plumstead Township. Two properties on Curly Hill Road had extensive tree damage and one had a broken gazebo. On Silo Hill Road, the siding and corner roof of a pole barn were torn away. In Pipersville in Tinicum Township, a few large tree limbs were knocked down. Around 550 homes and businesses lost power in the township. Power was fully restored by 715 a.m. EDT on the 16th.
Quarter size hail fell in Plumstead Township.

An EF-0 tornado with an estimated maximum wind speed of 75 mph briefly touched down in the northeast part of Philadelphia and damaged a couple of businesses and an apartment building in the area and caused two injuries. The tornado touched down near the intersection of Red Lion Road and Northeast Avenue. The roof of a car repair shop on Northeast Avenue caved in and injured two workers. One had to be hospitalized. An apartment complex near the garage was damaged and the Red Cross assisted four people in finding temporary quarters.  The roof of a beer distributor on Northeast Avenue collapsed. Torn shingles, signs and debris littered the grass around the distributor. A seafood restaurant on Bustelton Avenue then lost part of its roof.  The tornado then lifted. The path length was approximately two tenths of a mile and the maximum path width about 33 yards. The estimated maximum wind speed was 75 mph. This was the first tornado to touch down within Philadelphia since January 18, 1999.
A funnel cloud was spotted over Island Creek south of Oxford. It did not touch down and no damage was reported.

An EF-0 tornado touched down in Queen Anne's County northwest of Church Hill around 1215 p.m. EDT. The tornado started on the Chester River and came onshore near Ralph's Wharf. It moved in a northeast direction, crossed Maryland State Route 213 at Union Church Road and crossed Maryland State Route 544, McGinnes Road, before lifting near the Thomas Cemetery. Damage was minor and intermittent as the tornado did not stay on the ground the entire time. The worst reported property damage occurred around Union Church Road where shingles were blown off a house and a play station was also damaged.  The tornado's path length was 3.69 miles and maximum path width about 17 yards or 50 feet. The maximum estimated wind speed was 65 mph.

Penny size hail fell in Smyrna.
A funnel cloud was sighted near Oyster Cove off of Quaker Neck Road. It did not touch down and no damage was reported.

An EF-0 tornado touched down in Franklin Township, badly damaged one home and caused minor damage to about a dozen others, a church and a baseball field. The tornado touched down to the rear of a few homes on Church Street and moved through Penn Street before lifting. On Church Street, a trampoline was blown thirty feet and trees were knocked down on one property. A neighboring trampoline was tossed into the sign of Saint Matthews Evangelical Lutheran Church. The church also suffered additional wind damage. The worst tornado damage occurred as it crossed Penn Street. A recently renovated home had its roof torn away. The dry walls fell onto a woman. A tree also fell on top of the house. A metal shed was also twisted, aluminum window awnings were mangled and a swing set was toppled. Numerous trees were either snapped or uprooted along the tornado's path. The estimated maximum winds were 75 mph. The estimated path length was about 0.4 miles and path width about 50 yards.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a tree onto a three story dwelling in Philadelphia.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees around the intersection of Catharine and South 60th Streets in Philadelphia.

The Doppler Radar from Fort Dix had measured wind speeds of 76 mph at two thousand feet above sea level as the severe thunderstorm moved through the county.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust to 58 mph at the Philadelphia International Airport.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Smyrna.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few additional trees around Centreville.

A severe thunderstorm near Seaford knocked down a few trees, caused roof damage to a couple of homes and damaged a produce stand.
A severe thunderstorm dropped hail as large as quarters in Clayton.
Nickel size hail fell from a thunderstorm in Clayton.

A thunderstorm produced heavy rain in Clayton and caused a retention pond to overflow and flood two homes on Costill Avenue in Clayton. A few other homes on the block also had basement flooding. A Skywarn Spotter measured 3.63 inches of rain. most of which fell within an hour.
A severe thunderstorm toppled a few trees in Cumru Township. The combination of the wind and lightning strikes caused power to be out in parts of the township for most of the 11th.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees near Galena. One blocked a roadway.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Church Hill. A Skywarn spotter near Church Hill had a measured wind gust of 57 mph.
A Skywarn spotter estimated wind gusts of 60 mph in Ridgely during a severe thunderstorm. A couple of trees and several tree limbs were knocked down between Ridgely and Greensboro.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and utility poles in and around Denton. Choptank Electric reported about 2,600 of its Caroline County customers lost power. Delmarva Power and Light reported additional outages. It took until around 4 a.m. EDT on the 13th to fully restore power in Caroline County.
A lightning strike damaged a home in Somerset in Franklin Township.
Lightning strikes from thunderstorms damaged a couple of homes in Highland Park and Edison.
Nickel size hail fell in Belmar.

A severe thunderstorm on Tilghman Island, knocked down several very large trees, poles and electrical wires at the entrance to Black Walnut Point. Another half dozen large trees were knocked over on Bar Neck Road and also damaged the power lines and power meters to several homes. In addition, sheds and patio furniture was overturned. One boat was also damaged as was the screened porch of another home. The same severe thunderstorm knocked down a very large tree that blocked Elston Shore Road in Neavitt.

A severe thunderstorm caused pockets of property damage throughout Oxford. A boat was blown off its lift at Campbell���s Boatyard at Jack���s Point. The masthead at the Pier Street Marina was pulled off and rooftop air conditioning units were overturned. Flying debris shattered the glass of four cars. A home���s chimney at South Morris and Pier Street was blown away and debris fell through the window of a neighbor���s home   Fencing around the town���s tennis courts and temporary construction fencing were destroyed. A tree fell onto a garage on Holly Harbor Road.
A severe thunderstorm in Trappe knocked down trees on Trappe Landing Road, White Marsh Road, Southside and Island Creek Road.

A severe thunderstorm uprooted several trees, snapped others and tore down tree limbs along Marsh Creeek Road and Sunset Boulevard in Preston. Power lines were also knocked down and outages in the area lasted into the afternoon of the 22nd.

A severe thunderstorm caused pockets of wind damage (downed trees) across central Morris County mainly from around Budd Lake east through Morristown. About 2,000 homes and businesses lost power in Morris County.
Golf ball size hail fell from a severe thunderstorm in the Whiting section of Manchester Township.

A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage that was concentrated in the Crestwood Village development in Whiting in Manchester Township. About a dozen large trees were uprooted and damaged two homes. A number of large tree limbs were also knocked down. It was estimated that about eighty properties were affected by downed trees. One person was trapped within their home until the tree was removed. Trees and tree limbs were knocked down on Columbus Boulevard, Crockett Lane, Ironside Drive, Constitution Boulevard and Chestnut Avenue. A firefighter was injured while removing a downed tree. About 500 homes and businesses lost power in Ocean County.
Quarter size hail also fell from a severe thunderstorm in Whiting (Manchester Township).

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in the northeast part of Manchester Township and resulted in a fatality. A 69-year-old man was killed on County Route 571 in front of the Ridgeway Elementary School when two trees fell onto his vehicle. A police officer was injured trying to extricate the man from the vehicle.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs in New Lisbon (Pemberton Township).
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees across mainly central Gloucester County.

A severe thunderstorm knocked numerous trees across the northern part of Warren County in Blairstown, Hackettstown and Independence Township. About 3,000 homes and businesses lost power in Warren County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down five poles in East Windsor Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees at the Six Flags Theme Park.

A police officer filmed a funnel cloud that passed over the Colliers Mills Wildlife Management Area in Jackson Township. The area it moved through was inaccessible and it apparently did not touch down.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Lansdale.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Horsham Township.

A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage in a couple of pockets of Warrington Township. Trees were knocked down along County Line Road near Falls Road. A downed wire caused a power surge at the Hampton Inn along Pennsylvania State Route 611 and Kelly Road. The surge caused an electrical fire and the inn was evacuated for about an hour. The top of a large tree was sheared off on Pennsylvania State Route 611 near Bristol Road. Other large tree limbs were also knocked down in the area and damaged a couple of vehicles. One downed limb broke the window of a gift shop. The severe thunderstorm also knocked down some bricks from an abandoned dwelling.

A severe thunderstorm tore down numerous trees and tree limbs across the central and southern tier of Sussex County. Nearly 1000 JCP&L customers lost power. In Stillwater Township, one property owner alone lost fifteen trees. Wind gusts were estimated at 65 mph.
A severe thunderstorm also dropped quarter size hail in Stillwater Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Stroud Township. The intersection of Pennsylvania State Routes 447 and 191 was closed because of a tree that was hanging onto wires.

A severe thunderstorm snapped and uprooted trees in Middle Smithfield Township. There was a two mile length of wind damage in the township that extended from Lower Lakeview Drive to U.S. Route 209 border with Pike County. Several trees were knocked down across roadways. U.S. Route 209, Winona Falls Road and River Road were all closed because of downed trees.

Thunderstorms produced flash flooding across southeastern sections of Sussex County. In Andover Borough, U.S. Route 206 was closed near Stickle Pond Road. High Street was closed in Newton and parking lots off of U.S. Route 206 were flooded in Hampton Township. Precipitation totals included 4.47 inches in Sparta and 2.93 inches in Andover.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller creeks in the Pequannock Basin mainly in Jefferson Township. Event precipitation totals included 2.80 inches in Charlotteburg (Passaic County).

A lightning strike killed eleven sheep on a farm in East Coventry Township near Sawmill and Harley Roads. They were found lying in a circle the ensuing morning and the bark from a nearby tree was shattered.

A lightning strike near Big Daddy���s Family Barbecue in Bartonsville (Stroud Township) that set a pole ablaze resulted in about 1,000 people losing power in the township.

A lightning strike of a power pole on East Broad Street in East Stroudsburg caused about 600 people to lose power.  Lightning also struck a couple of homes within Monroe County during the afternoon of the 24th, but no serious damage was reported.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a large sign and a 100-year-old tree on a diner property on New Jersey State Route 70 in Brick Township.
Another severe thunderstorm in Brick Township dropped quarter size hail.
A funnel cloud was observed just to the northwest of West Creek. It did not touch down.

Two people were struck and injured by lightning in Plainsboro Township.
One person was struck and injured by lightning in Ocean Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of large tree limbs and wires in East Penn Township. One tree was set on fire on Dinkers Road because of the downed wires.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a large tree and wires on Glenbrook Road in Jackson Township..The combination of lightning and wind caused about 400 homes and businesses to lose power in Jackson and Pocono Townships.
A severe thunderstorm downed trees and blocked Warner Road near Long Woods Drive in Chestnuthill Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Barrett Township. A downed tree blocked Pennsylvania State Route 191 near Pocono Plateau Road.
Lightning Struck a transformer near the East Stroudsburg High School on North Courtlandt Street.

Lightning struck a Harrington home in the Farmington area on Staytonsville Road near Wolf���s Trail End Drive. The ensuing fire caused about $200,000 in damage. Four fire companies battled the blaze and the residents were evacuated without injury. One firefighter was injured battling the blaze.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees, tree limbs and wires in Princeton Township. Cherry Valley Road was blocked between The Great Road and Province Line Road. Trees and wires were also knocked down on U.S. Route 206, Mercer Street, Crestview Road, Dempsey Avenue, Riverside Drive, Stuart Road, Terhune Road, Quaker Road and Cherry Hill Road. U.S. Route 206, Mercer Street, Cherry Valley and Stuart Roads were still closed the next morning.  In Princeton Borough, about a dozen trees were knocked down. One vehicle in the Borough Hall parking lot was damaged by a fallen tree. About 500 homes and businesses lost power in Mercer County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Montgomery Township. Cherry Valley Road was closed as well as Opossum Road between Red Fox Court and Orchard Road because of downed trees.

A 54-year-old male was struck and killed by lightning while ducking under a tree during a thunderstorm to light a cigar in Hammonton. In 1963, the man's father was also struck and killed by lightning. A 38 year-old male cousin was seriously injured by the same lightning strike. The man felt a blast and remembered being thrown back a few feet before losing consciousness. He regained consciousness in the ambulance and was expected to recover.
Penny size hail fell in Franklin Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Sparta Township on and around West Mountain Road, Grandview Terrace and Sterling Hill Road. One property lost between fifteen and twenty trees and also suffered roof damage to its home. About 150 homes lost power. Power was fully restored by 3 p.m. EDT that afternoon.
Quarter size hail also fell from the severe thunderstorm in Sparta Township.

Lightning struck and started a barn fire on Lamington Road in Bedminster Township. Seven fire companies responded to the fire and it took about forty minutes to extinguish. Much of the hay in the barn was destroyed.

A lightning strike caused a communications failure that affected the police, fire and rescue services in East Brunswick Township. The municipal building also suffered some structural damage by the lightning strike.

A lightning strike knocked out a transformer on the roof of the JFK Medical Center. It also caused a small smoky fire in a pipe in the wall of the hospital. Sixteen patients were moved off the pediatrics specialty care unit until the blaze was extinguished.

A lightning strike and ensuing fire destroyed a shed and its contents in Alexandria Township. Lightning struck a branch of a tree and then traveled to the roof of the shed where it ignited the fire. It took two fire companies about twenty minutes to extinguish the blaze. A snow blower, go cart and tools within the shed were all destroyed.

A lightning strike to Lucy the Elephant in Margate caused significant damage to the tourist attraction's electrical and climate control system. The computer printers, air conditioning controllers, lighting and fire alarm controllers all suffered electrical damage.
Lightning struck four homes in Toms River Township, but caused little structural damage. The lighting caused about 2,000 JCP&L customers to lose power in ten municipalities within Ocean County.

Lightning struck and started a roof fire in an unoccupied home on Fathom Avenue in the Ocean Acres section of Stafford Township. Four fire companies responded and confined the fire to the west side of the home's roof.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding within Toms River Township. The worst flooding was reported at the intersection of New Jersey State Route 37 and Mule Road. About thirty motorists were stranded within their vehicles throughout the township and several had to be rescued. Many jughandles were also impassable. The Doppler Radar storm total estimate over the township was between 2 and 3 inches, most of which fell within one hour.
Quarter size hail fell in Manalapan Township.
Hail up to the size of quarters fell from a severe thunderstorm in Jackson Township.
In addition to the large hail, the severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires within Jackson Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a tree in Washington Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Forks Township, including one onto a home that suffered structural damage.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of poles and wires in Lower Mount Bethel Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of poles and wires in Perkasie.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and power lines in lower Bucks County.

A lightning strike took down two wires on the property of the Crystal Springs Aquatic Center in East Brunswick Township. One downed wire energized a fence. The facility closed for the rest of the day. No injuries were reported.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires near the Interstate 295 corridor in Hamilton Township. A Skywarn Spotter estimated wind gusts of 60 mph in the area.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Wall Township and caused road closures. Ocean Road was closed near Bailey Corner Road. Allaire Road was closed near South Manor Court. A transformer fire closed Eighteenth Avenue.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Millstone Township, one onto County Route 571 just south of Stagecoach Road.
A corn field was leveled by a severe thunderstorm in Upper Nazareth Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires in East Windsor Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires in Upper Freehold Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees and wires in Eatontown.  This severe thunderstorm was responsible for dozens of calls of downed trees in the southern half of the county.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs in Bordentown Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs along State Route 68 in Mansfield Township.  County Route 677 was closed within the township because of downed trees.
A trained spotter measured a wind gust of 62 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Florence Township. A few trees were also knocked down within the township.
Penny size hail fell in Florence Township.
Numerous medium to large limbs were knocked down by a severe thunderstorm in the Yorkshire Terrace area of North Hanover Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and several tree limbs in Springfield Township. Mount Pleasant Road was closed as was County Route 537 between State Route 68 and Wrightstown-Georgetown Road. There were also downed tree limbs along State Route 68 within the township.
A severe thunderstorm uprooted a very large pine tree onto and damaged a fence in Wrightstown. Neighboring McGuire Air Force Base recorded a wind gust of 54 mph.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several large tree limbs in and around the New Hanover Township Municipal Complex.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Plumsted Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding along the U.S. Route 206 corridor in Bordentown Township. A couple of water rescues occurred and no injuries were reported.  Adjusted Doppler Radar storm total estimates were 3 to 4 inches in parts of Bordentown Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused small stream and roadway flash flooding in Florence Township. Adjusted Doppler Radar storm total estimates were 3 to 4 inches in parts of Florence Township. A Cocorahs observer in neighboring Chesterfield Township measured 2.49 inches of rain.
