A gust front outrunning a cluster of severe thunderstorms entered near Seaford in western Sussex County at approximately 11:57 pm EDT on the 29th. This gust front produced damaging wind gusts estimated between 65 mph to 70 mph as it traversed eastward across the county. Within approximately 20 minutes of the gust front passage, a potent line of severe thunderstorms tracked eastward through Sussex county, producing another round of destructive wind gusts, estimated from 65 mph to 70 mph. Large tree limbs were reported down across the county, including in Seaford, Lincoln, Lewes, and Millsboro. In addition, multiple downed trees were reported in Selbyville, and a wind gust to 70 mph was estimated in Bridgeville. Severe thunderstorms exited eastern Sussex County, including the town of Lewes, at approximately 1:10 am EDT on the 30th. Measured wind gusts included 69 mph in Dewey Beach and 63 mph in Lewes.

A gust front outrunning a cluster of severe thunderstorms entered near Sandtown in western Kent County at approximately 11:57 pm EDT on the 29th. This gust front produced damaging wind gusts estimated between 65 mph to 70 mph as it traversed eastward across the county. Within approximately 20 minutes of the gust front passage, a potent line of severe thunderstorms tracked eastward through Kent County, producing another round of destructive wind gusts, estimated from 65 mph to 70 mph. Large tree limbs were reported down across the county, including in Felton and Dover. In addition, several downed trees and an estimated wind gust to 70 mph were reported in Harrington. Severe thunderstorms exited eastern Kent County, including the town of Bowers, at approximately 1:10 am EDT on the 30th.

A gust front outrunning a cluster of severe thunderstorms entered near Pennsville in western Salem County at approximately 12:19 am EDT on the 30th. This gust front produced damaging wind gusts estimated from 65 to 70 mph as it traversed eastward across the county. Within approximately 20 minutes of the gust front passage, a potent line of severe thunderstorms tracked eastward into Salem county. One thunderstorm cell in particular experienced rapid intensification and expansion as it tracked into southern New Jersey. Destructive wind gusts, estimated at 75 mph, resulted in significant tree and power line damage county-wide. Severe thunderstorms exited eastern Salem County, including the town of Elmer, at approximately 1:06 am EDT on the 30th. ||Widespread damage occurred across Salem County as a result of the strong wind gusts associated with the gust front and cluster of severe thunderstorms. One home was destroyed, another suffered major damage. Three other homes suffered minor damage and one other was also affected. Numerous large tree limbs blew down in the town of Elmer. The Little Acres Farm in Pittsgrove Township had about four dozen 80-foot trees completely uprooted. Approximately 70 trees were knocked down onto roadways across the county, resulting in numerous road closures. Several hundred large trees were knocked down or damaged in Parvin State Park (Pittsgrove Township) in eastern Salem County, and two fatalities resulted. Two young boys, ages 2 and 7, were killed when the top half of a 40 to 50 foot pine tree snapped off due to high wind gusts and landed on the camping tent where they and other family members were taking shelter. The two boys were cousins, one from nearby Franklin Township (Gloucester County) and the other from Millville (Cumberland County). An intense cluster of thunderstorms tracked over eastern Salem County at 12:50 am EDT on the 30th, producing wind gusts estimated between 70 to 75 mph.  ||Thousands of customers lost power across the county as a result of extensive tree and wire damage, with many areas experiencing power outages for up to one week. Some customers did not have their power restored until after the 4th of July. As a result, Salem County Emergency Services and the American Red Cross established air-conditioned cooling centers in Woodstown and at the Pittsgrove Township Municipal Building as temperatures soared into the 90s during the week following the derecho.||Damage estimates for Parvin State Park alone are approximately $500,000 as several buildings were damaged and hundreds of trees were either knocked down or damaged. More than a month following the derecho, the majority of the park remained closed to the public as clean-up efforts continued. The swimming beach and concession stand at the park did not reopen until the weekend of July 21st - 22nd. Through early August 2012, some 938 trees have been removed from the park, and damaged large limbs from another 989 trees have been hauled away. Park officials anticipate that much of the park will remain closed to the public for months.

A gust front outrunning a cluster of severe thunderstorms entered near Greenwich in western Cumberland County at approximately 12:23 am EDT on the 30th. This gust front produced damaging wind gusts ranging from 65 to 70 mph as it traversed eastward across the county. Within approximately 10 to 20 minutes of the gust front passage, a potent line of severe thunderstorms tracked eastward into Cumberland County. One thunderstorm cell in particular experienced rapid intensification and expansion as it tracked through southern New Jersey. Destructive wind gusts, estimated as high as 75 mph, resulted in significant tree and power line damage county-wide. Eight homes in the county were destroyed, forty others suffered major damage. In addition, one hundred thirty one other homes suffered minor damage and fifty others were affected.||Several wind gusts in association with the gust front passage or cluster of intense thunderstorms were measured across the county by trained spotters, mesonet sites, and ASOS equipment. A 59 mph wind gust associated with the gust front was measured in Newport by a trained spotter at 12:40 am EDT on the 30th. Soon after, severe thunderstorms tracked through the Newport area, producing winds measured at 59 mph by a trained spotter. The strong winds associated with the cluster of thunderstorms occurred at 12:50 am EDT on the 30th and lasted for a duration of 10 minutes. ||Intense thunderstorms produced several other measured wind gusts as they progressed from west to east across the county. A 62 mph gust was measured by a mesonet station in Upper Deerfield Township at 12:45 am EDT. Two locations recorded the highest measured gust of 67 mph in Cumberland County. A mesonet station in Bivalve measured a 67 mph gust at 12:50 am EDT, and the ASOS equipment at the Millville Municipal Airport (KMIV) measured a 67 mph gust at 12:57 am EDT. In addition, the KMIV Airport ASOS also measured a 63 mph gust at 12:52 am EDT. The final measured gust in Cumberland County of 64 mph was recorded in Vineland by a trained spotter at 1:00am EDT on the 30th. Severe thunderstorms exited eastern Cumberland County, including the town of Port Elizabeth, at approximately 1:19 am EDT on the 30th.  ||Widespread damage occurred across Cumberland County as a result of the strong wind gusts associated with the gust front and cluster of severe thunderstorms. Numerous trees were knocked down in Vineland and Bridgeton, and damage to some buildings was also reported in Vineland. Trees were reported down along Glade Road in Maurice River Township. Electric wires were knocked down in Delmont, and multiple large tree limbs blew down in Port Norris.||Thousands of customers lost power across the county as a result of the extensive tree and wire damage, with many areas experiencing power outages for about one week. According to Vineland Electric, about 1,800 customers did not have their power restored until the week of July 9th. As a result, the city of Vineland, as well as other surrounding communities, provided air-conditioned cooling centers as temperatures soared into the 90s during the week following the derecho. Vineland also postponed its Independence Day fireworks twice.

A gust front outrunning a cluster of severe thunderstorms entered near Buena in western Atlantic County at approximately 12:49 am EDT on the 30th. This gust front produced damaging wind gusts estimated from 65 to 70 mph as it traversed eastward across the county. Within approximately 20 minutes of the gust front passage, a potent line of severe thunderstorms tracked eastward into Atlantic County. One thunderstorm cell in particular experienced rapid intensification and expansion as it tracked across the eastern part of the county. Destructive wind gusts, measured around 75 mph, resulted in significant tree and power line damage county-wide. Based on the extensive damage, winds were estimated to be as high as 90 mph in areas across the county. There were seven homes that were destroyed, forty-nine that suffered major damage, fifty-two that suffered minor damage and forty-two that were affected.||Several wind gusts in association with the gust front passage or cluster of intense thunderstorms were measured across the county by trained spotters, mesonet sites, and ASOS equipment. The strongest measured wind gust across Atlantic County was recorded in Absecon at 74 mph by a retired NWS employee at 1:05 am EDT on the 30th. Several locations in nearby Atlantic City also recorded significant wind gusts. A 66 mph gust was measured at a mesonet station in Atlantic City at 1:11 am EDT on the 30th. At the Atlantic City Marina, a 64 mph gust was measured by the NOS platform at 2:00 am EDT. The ASOS equipment at the Atlantic City International Airport (KACY) recorded a wind gust of 58 mph at 1:13 am EDT. Elsewhere, a 64 mph gust was measured at a mesonet station in Mullica Township at 1:15 am EDT, and a 60 mph gust was recorded in Estell Manor by a NWS cooperative observer at 1:00 am EDT. Finally, a 50 mph gust was measured by a resident in Somers Point at 1:00 am EDT. Severe thunderstorms exited eastern Atlantic County, including Atlantic City, at approximately 2:02 am EDT on the 30th.||Extensive damage occurred across Atlantic county as a result of the strong wind gusts associated with the gust front and cluster of severe thunderstorms, and a State of Emergency was declared in the county. An idle 727 aircraft was moved and damaged by the derecho at the Atlantic City International Airport. Numerous large trees and electric wires were knocked down in many communities, including Estell Manor, Northfield, Mays Landing, Egg Harbor City, Hamilton Township, Galloway Township, Linwood, Margate City, Egg Harbor Township, Ventnor City, Longport, and Atlantic City. As a result, much of the county was affected by long-term power outages, and numerous roads were impassable. Atlantic City Electric reported approximately 105,000 of its customers lost power. In addition to the widespread tree and power line damage, structural damage was also significant across the county, with trees blown down onto houses in Buena and Absecon and shingles blown off of homes in Somers Point. Thousands of customers experienced power outages for about one week. Approximately 1,400 Atlantic City Electric customers that had lost power during the early morning of June 30th did not have their electricity restored until July 8th. Several communities, including Linwood, Egg Harbor Township, Galloway Township, and Brigantine, provided air-conditioned cooling centers as temperatures soared into the 90s during the week following the derecho.

A gust front outrunning a cluster of severe thunderstorms entered near Eldora in western Cape May County at approximately 12:33 am EDT on the 30th. This gust front produced damaging wind gusts estimated from 65 to 70 mph as it traversed eastward across the county. Within approximately 20 minutes of the gust front passage, a potent line of severe thunderstorms tracked eastward into Cape May County. Strong wind gusts, estimated between 65 to 70 mph, resulted in significant tree and power line damage across the county. ||Several wind gusts in association with the gust front passage or cluster of intense thunderstorms were measured or estimated across the county by trained spotters and residents. The strongest measured wind gust across Cape May County was recorded in Eldora at 65 mph by a county official at 1:10 am EDT on the 30th. Elsewhere in Ocean City, a resident estimated wind gusts to be greater than 60 mph at 1:00 am EDT, causing several trees to be blown down. Wind gusts were also estimated to be greater than 60 mph by a resident in Sea Isle City at 12:50 am EDT. Finally, a 55 mph wind gust was estimated by a trained spotter in Wildwood at 1:15 am EDT. Trees, large tree limbs, and electric wires were blown down in Goshen, Ocean City, Woodbine, Marmora, and Avalon. As a result, thousands of customers across the county experienced multi-day power outages, and many roads were impassable. Some areas experienced power outages for up to one week. events.cz_name: LITTLE EGG INLET TO GREAT EGG INLET NJ OUT 20NM
events.event_narrative: The derecho produced damaging wind gusts along the entire shore of Atlantic County and claimed the life of a 48-year-old man. The man drowned on Absecon Bay after the 20-foot skiff he was in capsized. The body was recovered at 5 a.m. EDT early that morning. Two other men who were in the boat survived. The capsized vessel washed ashore in a marsh.  Peak wind gusts along marine areas included 67 knots (77 mph) at Point Point, 64 knots (74 mph) in Absecon, 57 knots (66 mph) at the Atlantic City Marina and 56 knots (64 mph) on the Absecon Channel.

A lightning strike and the ensuing fire gutted the 104-year-old Episcopal Church of the Redeemer in Longport. It was believed that the lightning strike ignited the tower. The church's roof was nearly completely burned, the stucco exterior severely charred and the stained-glass windows were gone. Firefighters had a difficult time battling the blaze as strong to damaging wind gusts were occurring with the derecho at the time of the blaze. No serious injuries were reported.

A family of 4 people suffered minor injuries from a lightning strike on the beach in Wildwood off of East Cedar Avenue. They were under a beach umbrella when lightning struck nearby and traveled up the umbrella. A man, two women (one pregnant) and one child were injured. All were hospitalized due to tingling in their hands and arms.

Flash flooding from torrential downpours flooded Stanton-Grange Road in Lebanon and Stanton-Station Road in Readington Township.  Doppler Radar storm total estimates were 2 to 4 inches.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in Ocean City, Sea Isle City and Middle and Lower Townships. Widespread roadway flooding was reported, especially in Ocean City. The heavy rain coincided with the afternoon high tide. Event precipitation totals included 1.78 inches in Dennis Township and 1.70 inches in Middle Township.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding on Absecon Island in both Atlantic City and Margate City. Numerous streets were flooded in Atlantic City and vehicles were getting stuck in the high water. In Margate, flooding spread into some buidlings.  Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 2.0 to 2.5 inches on the island. The Marina within Atlantic City measured 1.60 inches of rain.

Thunderstorms which back built over Galloway Township caused flash flooding during the late afternoon of the 14th. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 3 to 5 inches in the township. The Garden State Parkway was flooded in the township as were numerous other smaller roadways including Kensington Drive. Vehicles were partially submerged and flood waters reached up to the entrances of homes.

events.event_narrative: A nearly stationary waterspout formed on the Great Bay for about ten minutes. Several eyewitnesses saw and photoed the waterspout including a meteorologist from ION Weather and aircraft flying in the region. No damage to boats or injuries were reported.

A funnel cloud was sighted over a farm field in Eastern Queen Anne's County near Hope east of U.S. Route 301 and south of Price Station Road. Because of excellent visibility, it was seen from Caroline County as well as motorists traveling on U.S. Route 301.
A severe thunderstorm dropped quarter size hail in Middletown Township.
A severe thunderstorm dropped quarter to half dollar size hail in Sparta Township and also caused wind damage within the township.
A severe thunderstorm dropped quarter size hail in Rockaway Township.
A thunderstorm dropped nickel size hail in Atlantic Highlands.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires in Sparta Township (it also dropped large hail). One downed tree damaged a vehicle. No injuries were reported.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Millstone Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees within the city of Vineland.
A 41-year-old male was struck and died the next day from a lightning strike while fishing with his 10-year-old son on Takanassee Lake Beach in Long Branch. His son was not injured.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires near Tunis Mills.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in western parts of Lower Township, North Cape May, Cape May and West Cape May. Vehicles were stuck in flood waters in Cape May. Event precipitation totals included 5.05 inches in Cape May.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused additional flash flooding in lower Cape May County, in particular North Wildwood and Wildwood Crest where streets were flooded. Some businesses in Wildwood were flooded. Event precipitation totals included 4.46 inches in Wildwood Crest.
Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused additional flash flooding in Avalon and Stone Harbor. In Avalon, one vehicle was totally submerged in flood waters. No injuries were reported.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in Eastern Sussex County. The hardest hit area was in and around Long Neck. Many roadways were flooded and closed. One road collapsed in Oak Orchard. In Oak Orchard, River Road was under water and the bulkhead of one home was damaged at the Riverwinds Development. Holly Lake Road was also closed  Flooding was also reported along Beaver Dam Road and Delaware State Ropute 5. Along the coast, Delaware State Route 1 in Dewey Beach and Delaware State Route 26 leading into Bethany Beach were flooded. Event precipitation totals included 7.21 in Rehoboth Beach, 6.83 inches in Harbeson,  6.39 inches in Bethany Beach and 5.76 inches in Indian River Inlet.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused roadway flash flooding in Rehoboth Beach. First Street was under two feet of water and at least one resort garage was flooded. Over two dozen vehicles were damaged. Event precipitation total was 7.21 inches.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in and around Easton. About 16 roadways in and out of Easton were flooded and closed including U.S. Route 50. Water rescues were performed on Washington Street and Elliot Road. Most roadways were able to reopen by 10 p.m. EDT that evening. The Talbot Town Shopping Center suffered flood damage as some businesses had two feet of water within them.  The Talbot County Visual Arts Center in Easton was closed because of flood damage. In Cordova, vehicles were abandoned and rescues were performed. Maryland State Route 333 was flooded in Oxford. There were 70 flood related calls in Talbot County. Two roadways were washed out and two small bridges were also flooded. Rainfall totals included 7.37 inches in Easton.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in and around Saint Michaels.  Vehicles were abandoned and rescues were performed. Event precipitation totals included 6.10 inches in Saint Michaels.
Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in southern Queen Anne's County. Doppler Radar storm total estimates were around 6 inches.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding in central Queen Anne's County. Doppler Radar storm total estimates were around 5 inches. Storm total rainfall included 5.46 inches in Queenstown.
Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in western Caroline County. Doppler Radar storm total estimates were around 8 inches.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused small stream and drainage flash flooding in northern Caroline County. Doppler Radar storm total estimates were around 7 inches. Event precipitation totals included 5.30 inches in Denton.

A thunderstorm produced a measured wind gust of 56 mph at the Trenton Mercer County Airport at 5:13 pm EDT. The strong wind gusts associated with this thunderstorm damaged a window in the Control Tower of the Mercer County Airport.

Strong wind gusts from a  severe thunderstorm knocked down trees in the city of Trenton. A tree and a pole were knocked down on Cadwalader Drive. In addition, trees were also reported down across the train tracks in Trenton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires throughout Tulpehocken Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a large tree in Upper Bern Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a large tree in Maiden Creek.
Strong wind gusts produced by a severe thunderstorm knocked down electric wires in Rockland Township.
Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage flash flooding on roadways in Hopewell Township. Doppler Radar storm total estimates were around 3 inches throughout most of the township.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage flash flooding that resulted in several water rescues and stranded vehicles in Woodbridge. Three vehicles were trapped on Woodbridge Center Drive. Several other vehicles were caught in flood waters on U.S. Route 9 under the New Jersey State Route 440 Bridge and also on Leesville Avenue. Doppler Radar storm total estimates were around 3 inches in the Woodbridge area.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged an attic of a home under construction on Jefferson Road in Princeton.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged the attic of a home on Henderson Avenue in Princeton. The homeowner was displaced from her home, but no injuries were reported.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several large trees into homes in the Lake Riviera area of Brick Township.  No injuries were reported.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in and around Easton. Easton Utilities and Choptank Electric reported scattered outages caused by the damaging winds and lightning throughout the county.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in and around Cordova.

A lightning strike and ensuing fire caused about $25,000 in damage to a home on Armiger Drive in the Hill-N-Dale Development south of Blades.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire caused extensive damage to a home on Eagle Run Lane in Delmar. No injuries were reported.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire caused extensive damage to a home on Inlet View Court in Bethany Beach. No injuries were reported.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a home on Waterford Lane in Selbyville.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a home on Martins Farm Road in Milton.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a home on Hollis Road in Georgetown.

A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage in the Pot Nets Bayside Community in Long Neck. Three homes had rooftop damage as the wind blew off shingles. Up to seven boats were also damaged and numerous trees were knocked down.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a home in the Harts Landing section of Lewes.

Flash flooding submerged eight vehicles to their windows at city hall police headquarters in Long Branch. Doppler Radar storm total estimates were 2.0 to 2.5 inches, most of which fell within 45 minutes.
A lightning strike damaged a home on Chapel Farm Drive in Easton.
A lightning strike damaged a home in Cordova.
A lightning strike and subsequent three alarm fire badly damaged a home in Salisbury Township. No injuries were reported.
Lightning struck and injured one person at the Drivers License Center In Hanover Township.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged the roof of a two story home on Log College Drive in Warminster Township. The homeowner escaped without any injuries.
A lightning strike caused a brief shed fire on Markham Road in Edison.
Lightning struck a home in Rock Hall. No injuries were reported. Lightning also caused about 170 Delmarva Power customers to lose power in Kent County.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding of fields, yards, poor drainage locations and small streams centered around Dagsboro Hundred. Actual rainfall amounts included 3.54 inches in Stockley and 2.95 inches in Jones Crossroads.
Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in Federalsburg. A few roadways were flooded and closed.

An EF0 tornado touched down in the Barclay Farms Subdivision in Camden with an estimated maximum wind speed of 85 mph. The tornado damaged approximately ten homes, six of them seriously and caused two injuries. Six homes were considered uninhabitable and gas lines were turned off in the development.  The tornado touched down on Dawson Lane and paralleled the train tracks from south to north.  Structural damage to homes occurred from Dalby Lane north through Carey Lane.  The tornado lifted after it passed Carey Lane. At one home, the wind tore the roof off a garage, damaging the two cars inside and the side of the home. The owner of the house was hospitalized after he cut his hand on a piece of broken glass. A firefighter was also injured assisting another resident. About 1,200 customers of the Delaware Electric Co-Operative lost power after the tornado moved through. All service was restored by 630 p.m. EDT that evening.  The tornado's path length was approximately 0.2 miles and its maximum path width was 35 yards.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours affected Blackbird Hundred and caused flash flooding of smaller streams as well as poor drainage and field flooding.  Storm totals included 4.17 inches within the hundred.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller creeks as well as poor drainage and roadway flooding in West Chester and West Goshen Township. A couple of roads were closed in West Chester. Doppler Radar rainfall estimates were around three inches.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller creeks as well as poor drainage and roadway flooding in Concord and Thornbury Townships. Doppler Radar rainfall estimates were around four inches within the townships..

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding along the Valley Creek.  The Valley Creek near Valley Forge exceeded its 7 foot flood stage from 549 a.m. EDT through 716 a.m. EDT on the 3rd. It crested at 7.78 feet at 645 a.m. EDT.

For the second time within the same day, thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding along the Valley Creek.  The Valley Creek near Valley Forge exceeded its 7 foot flood stage from 1118 a.m. EDT through 1230 p.m. EDT on the 3rd. It crested at 7.29 feet at Noon EDT.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding along the Chester Creek.  The Chester Creek near Chester exceeded its 8 foot flood stage from 618 p.m. EDT through 824 p.m. EDT on the 3rd. It crested at 8.92 feet at 7 p.m. EDT.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused small stream and poor drainage flooding in sections of Stafford, Barnegat and Little Egg Township. The torrential downpours led to the closing of New Jersey State Route 72 in western Barnegat Township.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused small stream and poor drainage flooding in sections of Bass River and Woodland Township. Event precipitation totals included 5.19 inches in Chatsworth (Woodland Township).

Runoff from the torrential downpours that started the night of the 3rd led to flooding along the Wading and Oswego Rivers in southeastern Burlington County. Additional thunderstorms during the next couple of days slowed the recession of the flooding along those rivers. Flooding affected Burlington County Routes 563 and 679. Burlington County Route 563 was closed and barricaded at the Evans Bridge. The bridge was expected to remain closed at least into the 7th until it could be evaluated for damage. The roadway itself was closed between Greenbank-Chatsworth Road in Washington Township and Leektown Road in Bass River Township.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding along the Southampton Creek in Upper Moreland Township.  Flooding from the creek was reported around Byberry and Pioneer Roads.  Storm totals included 2.22 in Williow Grove and 2.12 inches in Jenkintown.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding in the Spruce Hill section of Philadelphia, in particular around 43rd and Baltimore Streets. The precipitation total at the Philadelphia International Airport for September 4th was 3.12 inches.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding of small creeks as well as poor drainage and low lying area flooding in and around Stroudsburg. A precipitation event total of 5.75 inches was measured in East Stroudsburg.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding of small creeks and roadways in sections of Chestnut Hill, Hamilton, Jackson, Middle Smithfield and Stroud Townships. Doppler Radar storm total estimates exceeded 6 inches within the core of the heaviest rain.  Pennsylvania State Route 191 near the former Penn Hills Resort in Stroud Township flooded. Flooding was also reported along sections of the Brodhead Creek that reached onto other roadways.

Runoff from heavy rain that fell in Montgomery County earlier in the day caused flooding along the Pennypack Creek.  The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge was above its 7 foot flood stage from 1138 a.m. EDT through 1202 p.m. EDT on the 4th. It crested at 7.40 feet at 1145 a.m. EDT.

For the third time in the same day, flooding occurred along the Pennypack Creek.    The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge was again above its 7 foot flood stage from 639 p.m. EDT through 713 p.m. EDT on the 4th. It crested at 7.50 feet at 645 p.m. EDT.

A thunderstorm with heavy rain caused flash flooding along the Pennypack Creek as well as poor drainage flooding in northeastern Philadelphia. The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge was above its 7 foot flood stage from 203 p.m. EDT through 239 p.m. EDT on the 4th. It crested at 7.78 feet at 215 p.m. EDT. Of the three times the Pennypack Creek flooded on the 4th, this was its highest crest of the day.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding of streams and poor drainage flooding in Montague, Sandyston, Walpack and Wantage Townships in western Sussex County. In Sandyston, several driveways were washed away. County Route 560 was closed for debris clean-up. Firefighters pumped water from basements on Bevans Road and County Route 560.  Flooded roadways were reported in Montague. New Jersey State Route 23 was flooded and closed in Wantage. Event precipitation totals included 3.47 inches in Montague and 3.44 inches in Wantage. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 6 inches in parts of Sandyston and Walpack Townships.

A weak EFO tornado touched down in Mount Ephraim at 631 p.m. EDT on the 4th. The tornado initially touched down  on the west side of Cleveland Avenue. It then moved eastnortheast, crossed Jefferson Avenue and lifted as it approached Kings Highway. (County Route 551). Several homes in the area experienced roof damage, mainly from fallen tree limbs. A couple of large trees were uprooted. One badly damaged a concrete sidewalk.  The maximum wind speeds were estimated at 70 mph. The path length was about 0.15 miles and the maximum path width was 25 yards.

A lightning strike downed a pole and wires on West Main Boulevard or Pheasant Drive (Pennsylvania State Route 248) in Moore Township. The roadway was closed between Grouse Drive and East Dannersville Road until 930 a.m. EDT on the 5th.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding along McKinley Avenue in Stafford Township. A couple of basements were also flooded on Perry Lane. Event precipitation totals included 3.49 inches in Berkeley Township and 3.01 inches in Stafford Township, all of which fell within two hours.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Newton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Parsippany.
A trained spotter estimated wind gusts at 60 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Chester.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees in Marion and Jefferson Townships.  In Marion Township, trees were knocked down on Main Street, Forge Road and Water Street. In Jefferson Township, trees were knocked down on Christmas Village Road. Schaefferstown Road and Pennsylvania State Route 183.  Christmas Village Road was closed between Stone Road and Cross Key Road.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in south central Berks County.  Wind damage  (trees and wires down) was reported on Tulpehocken Road in Spring Township, Yorkshire and Vermont Roads in Cumru Township, Kenhorst Boulevard, Logan Street, Peach Street and Franklin Street in Reading, Penn Avenue in Wyomissing and along Kurtz Mill and Gunhart Roads in Robeson Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Oxford.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires across Eastern Berks County.  Trees and or wires were knocked down on Smoketown Road in Rockland Township, West State Street in Longswamp Township and Manatawny Road in Earl Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Pottstown, including one across Pennsylvania State Route 100.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Bangor Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs in Easton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Glen Mills (Thornbury Township).
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in the city of Chester, Two firefighters were injured responding to the downed trees.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Norwood.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees onto wires in North East.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several large tree limbs and wires throughout New Castle County.
A line of severe thunderstorms knocked down several large tree limbs and a few wires throughout Salem County.
A line of severe thunderstorms knocked down several trees and wires throughout Sussex County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few large tree limbs as well as trees in Deptford Township. One downed tree damaged a garage.
A severe thunderstorm knocked a few trees and wires throughout Morris County.
A severe thunderstorm generated a wind gust of 59 mph at Point Point.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Barnegat Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires in the Waretown section of Ocean Township. Power outages were reported along the U.S. Route 9 corridor.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires in the Forked River section of Lacey Township.  One downed tree damaged the roof of one home on Spruce Street and crushed the shed of another home. Ten roadways were blocked by fallen wires and three roadways were blocked by downed trees. Wind damage was centered around Lakeside Drive in the township.

events.event_narrative: A severe thunderstorm generated a wind gust of 51 knots (59 mph) at Point Point.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding across several locations in Carbon County. In Lehighton, the exit ramps to U.S. Route 209 from the Northeast Extension of the Pennsylvania Turnpike were closed due to flash flooding. A couple of water rescues were performed. In Kidder Township, Pennsylvania State Route 903 was closed between Pennsylvania State Route 534 and Johnathan Point Drive. The Mud Run Bridge on Pennsylvania State Route 903 was closed due to flooding. The latter roadway was not expected to be open until it was inspected the next day (the 19th).  In Franklin Township, driveways were swept into the street. Tons of debris had to be hauled away. Floodwaters ripped a pipe from the ground. In Mahoning Township, Country Club Road was closed between Pennsylvania State Routes 443 and 902. The Pohopoco Creek below Beltzville Lake at Parryville was above its 5.5 foot flood stage from 343 p.m. EDT through 425 p.m. EDT on the 18th. It crested at 5.62 feet at 4 p.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 5.75 inches in Lehighton, 5.66 inches in Beltzville, 5.41 inches in Jim Thorpe, 5.28 inches in Bowmanstown and 4.99 inches in Palmerton.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding and road closures, particularly in central and northern Monroe County. Road closures were reported in Lehman, Tobyhanna and Pocono Townships. Event precipitation totals included 5.78 inches in Blakeslee,  5.75 inches in Pocono Summit and 5.67 inches in Mount Pocono.
Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller streams and poor drainage flooding in northern Lehigh County. Event precipitation totals included 2.76 inches in Schnecksville.

Heavy rain caused poor drainage roadway flooding in Netcong, Randolph and Roxbury. The Netcong Circle (U.S. Route 46) was closed due to flooding.  Event precipitation totals included 2.81 inches in Mount Olive Township,  2.40 inches in Lake Hopatcong, 2.36 inches in Rockaway Township, 2.31 inches in Dover and 2.26 inches in Randolph Township.
A funnel cloud was sighted over Maple Shade, but did not touch down. It was associated with the same thunderstorm that did produce a tornado in Mount Ephraim in Camden County.
A lightning strike and ensuing smoky conditions forced the evacuation of a 117 room hotel in Mount Laurel Township. No injuries were reported.
A lightning strike caused 700 homes to lose power in Parsippany.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Wantage Township. Trees and wires were knocked down on New Jersey State Route 23 just north of Lewisburg Road. The roadway was closed for several hours. The damaging winds collapsed a tent at the Green Valley Farm stand on that roadway. Elsewhere in the township, several trees were knocked down in yards near the intersection of Unionville Road and County Route 561.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees in Nazareth. Pennsylvania State Route 191 was closed between Whitfield Street and East North Street because of downed trees and wires.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Sandyston and Walpack Townships.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Sparta Township including one on Sparta Avenue.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and tree limbs onto the SEPTA Paoli-Thorndale Regional Rail Line tracks. Service was suspended during the evening.
A line of severe thunderstorms knocked down a few trees and wires along Allentown Pike in Maidencreek Township, and Boy Scout and Ebling Roads in Greenwich Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires along West Douglass and Douglass Streets in Reading and Hill Road and Chestnut Street in Lenhartsville Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires along Mountain Road in Tilden Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires on Legion Drive in Bethel Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires along Interstate 78 in Upper Bern Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires along Beagle Road,  North End Road and Schuylkill Hill Road in Centre Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires along Evans Hill and State Hill Roads in Lower Heidelberg Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires on Heidelberg Avenue|in Exeter Township.

The main stem of the Perkiomen Creek at East Greenville was above its 4 foot flood stage from 451 p.m. EDT on the 29th through 1237 a.m. EDT on the 30th  It crested at 5.43 feet at 9 p.m. EDT on the 29th.  Elsewhere in the county, urban and poor drainage flooding occurred.  Pennsylvania State Route 309 near the Fort Washington Interchange was flooded. In the Pennypack Basin, Byberry Road was closed in Lower Moreland Township. Event precipitation totals included 4.00 inches in Ambler, 3.30 inches in West Norriton, 2.95 inches in Conshohocken, 2.83 inches in Pottstown, 2.63 inches in Perkiomenville and 2.58 inches in Green Lane.

Many gaged streams in Chester County had moderate flooding. In addition, there was poor drainage flooding. Two roadways were closed along the main stem of the Brandywine Creek due to flooding. The West Branch of the Brandywine Creek at Honey Brook had moderate flooding and was above its 7 foot flood stage from 554 p.m. EDT on the 29th through 343 a.m. EDT on the 30th.  It crested at 9.43 feet at 915 p.m. EDT on the 29th. The East Branch of the Brandywine Creek at Downingtown had major flooding and was above its 7 foot flood stage from 430 p.m. EDT on the 29th through 647 a.m. EDT on the 30th.  It crested at 11.11 feet at 943 p.m. EDT on the 29th. The main stem of the Brandywine Creek at Chadds Ford had moderate flooding and was above its 9 foot flood stage from 6 p.m. EDT on the 29th through 631 a.m. EDT on the 30th  It crested at 12.20 feet at 421 a.m. EDT on the 30th. The Valley Creek at Valley Forge had moderate flooding and was above its 7 foot flood stage from 326 p.m. EDT through 1050 p.m. EDT on the 29th.  It crested at 8.55 feet at 715 p.m. EDT.  The French Creek at Phoenixville was above its 8 foot flood stage from 454 p.m. EDT on the 29th through 742 a.m. EDT on the 30th.  It crested at 8.62 feet at 615 p.m. EDT on the 29th.||Event precipitation totals included 5.90 inches in Landenburg, 5.78 inches in West Chester, 5.59 inches in Exton, 4.75 inches in Glenmoore, 4.61 inches in Honey Brook and 3.15 inches in Phoenixville.

Many gaged streams in Delaware County had moderate flooding. In addition, there was poor drainage flooding as well tidal flooding along and near the Delaware River.  The Darby Creek flooded Darby Borough. Flooding was also reported in Malvern. Pennsylvania State Route 1 in Chadds Ford was closed due to Brandywine Creek flooding. The main stem of the Brandywine Creek at Chadds Ford had moderate flooding and was above its 9 foot flood stage from 6 p.m. EDT on the 29th through 631 a.m. EDT on the 30th  It crested at 12.20 feet at 421 a.m. EDT on the 30th.  The Chester Creek near Chester had moderate flooding and was above its 8 foot flood stage from 355 p.m. EDT on the 29th through 426 a.m. EDT on the 30th . It crested at 10.54 feet at 830 p.m. EDT on the 29th.  The Crum Creek at Newtown Square was above its 6 foot flood stage from 306 p.m. EDT through 1125 p.m. EDT on the 29th  It crested at 7.87 feet at 615 p.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 5.02 inches in Media, 4.20 inches in Garnet Valley, 3.06 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport and 2.43 inches in Aston Township.

The heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding as well tidal flooding along and near the Delaware River in Philadelphia.  Event precipitation totals included 3.06 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport, 2.17 inches in Rockledge and 1.62 inches at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport.

Heavy rain, creek and poor drainage flooding affected the southeastern part of Berks County the hardest. Monocacy Creek Road at U.S. Route 422 in Amity Township, Mertztown Road in Longswamp Township, Bertolet Mill Road in Oley Township and Lobachsville Road in Pike Township were all closed due to flooding. Evacuations occurred along the Manatawny Creek Basin. The Manatawny Creek at Spangsville was above its 6 foot flood stage from 616 p.m. EDT on the 29th through 535 a.m. EDT on the 30th.  It crested at 7.56 feet at 1015 p.m. EDT on the 29th.  Event precipitation totals included 5.12 inches at Unionville, 3.82 inches in Alburtis, 3.72 inches in Oley and 2.32 inches in Reading.

The heavy rain that fell across central and southern Ocean County not only caused poor drainage flooding, but exacerbated the tidal flooding along Barnegat Bay and on the barrier islands. Event precipitation totals included 6.14 inches in Barnegat, 4.67 inches in Little Egg Harbor and 3.50 inches in Brick Township.

Heavy rain caused urban and poor drainage flooding and exacerbated the tidal flooding along the Delaware River and near the Atlantic coast in Burlington County. In Mount Laurel Township, Union Mill Road was closed because Parkers Creek flooded.  The North Branch of the Rancocas Creek at Pemberton was above its 2.5 foot flood stage from 430 p.m. EDT on the 30th through 6 p.m. EDT on the 31st   It crested at 2.58 feet at 130 a.m. EDT on the 31st.  Event precipitation totals included 4.10 inches in Medford, 3.51 inches in Chatsworth, 3.15 inches in Medford Lakes, 2.92 inches in Mount Laurel, 2.82 inches in Morrestown and 2.42  inches in Westampton.

Heavy rain caused urban and poor drainage flooding and exacerbated the tidal flooding along the Delaware River. Event precipitation totals included 4.66 inches in Winslow Township, 3.94 inches in Lindenwold, 3.84 inches in Mount Ephraim, 2.94 inches in Pennsauken and 2.93 inches in Gloucester Township.

Heavy rain caused urban and poor drainage flooding and exacerbated the tidal flooding along the Delaware River in Gloucester County.  The Raccoon Creek at Swedesboro just touched its 13.0 foot flood stage at 100 a.m. EDT on the 30th.  Farther downstream, flooding occurred near and along the creek in Logan Township along U.S. Routes 130 and 322 and also on High Hill Road.  Roadway flooding was also reported in Franklin Township, South Harrison Township and National Park. Event precipitation totals included 5.31 inches in Pitman, 5.23 inches in Franklin, 5.22 inches in Malaga, 4.90 inches in Washington Township, 4.41 inches in Monroe Township and 3.96 inches in Glassboro.

Heavy rain caused urban and poor drainage flooding and exacerbated the tidal flooding along the Delaware River in Salem County.  Event precipitation totals included 5.56 inches in Pittsgrove Township.

Heavy rain caused urban and poor drainage flooding and exacerbated the tidal flooding along the Delaware Bay in Cumberland County.  Event precipitation totals included 7.30 inches in Newport, 7.07 inches in Vineland, 6.20 inches in Upper Deerfield, 5.93 inches in Bivalve and 5.77 inches at the Millville Airport.

Heavy rain caused urban and poor drainage flooding and exacerbated the tidal flooding along both the Delaware Bay and the ocean side in Cape May County.   Event precipitation totals included 11.91 inches in Wildwood Crest, 11.40 inches in Green Creek, 10.24 inches in North Wildwood, 10.06 inches in Seaville, 9.51 inches in Rio Grande, 9.37 inches in West Cape May, 8.60 inches in Dennisville, 8.41 inches in Lower Township, 8.10 inches in Cape May, 7.82 inches in Woodbine and 7.57 inches in Dennis Township.

Heavy rain caused urban and poor drainage flooding and exacerbated the tidal flooding along the ocean in Atlantic County.  Flooding was reported along the Atlantic City Expressway near U.S. Route 9 in Pleasantville. Event precipitation totals included 8.15 inches, 7.06 inches in Estell Manor, 6.83 inches in Egg Harbor Township, 5.80 inches at the Atlantic City International Airport, 5.74 inches in Folsom and 5.46 inches in Hammonton.

The heavy rain that fell across Talbot County not only caused poor drainage flooding, but exacerbated the tidal flooding along the Chesapeake Bay. Nearly two dozen roadways were flooded and closed. Event precipitation totals included 12.49 inches in Easton, 9.60 inches in Trappe and 5.00 inches in Cordova.

The heavy rain that fell across Caroline County not only caused poor drainage flooding, but exacerbated the tidal flooding along the Chesapeake Bay. Event precipitation totals included 10.55 inches in American Corner, 9.93 inches in Greensboro and 8.93 inches in Denton.

Heavy rain that was exacerbated by ongoing construction caused the closure of the New Jersey Turnpike in Mercer County because of flooding between exits 7A (Interstate 195) and 8 (Hightstown). Event precipitation totals included 2.43 inches in Hightstown and 1.75 inches in Trenton.

The heavy rain that fell across Cecil County not only caused poor drainage flooding, but exacerbated the tidal flooding along the Chesapeake Bay. Event precipitation totals of around just under 6 inches were reported near Elkton.

The heavy rain that fell across Kent County not only caused poor drainage flooding, but exacerbated the tidal flooding along the Chesapeake Bay. Event precipitation totals of around 6 to 8 inches were reported, including 6.93 inches in Worton.

The heavy rain that fell across Queen Anne's County not only caused poor drainage flooding, but exacerbated the tidal flooding along the Chesapeake Bay. Event precipitation totals included 9.89 inches in Queenstown, 6.77 inches in Stevensville and 4.50 inches in Centreville.

The heavy rain that fell across New Castle County not only caused poor drainage and creek flooding, but exacerbated the tidal flooding along the Delaware River and Bay. Thirty-four roadways were closed because of either flooding or high winds. Water rescues occurred in Odessa. The Christina River at Cooch's Bridge had moderate flooding and was above its 10.5 foot flood stage from 1042 a.m. EDT on the 29th through 408 a.m. EDT on the 30th. It crested at 12.35 feet at 730 p.m. EDT on the 29th. The White Clay Creek at Delaware Park had moderate flooding and was above its 13 foot flood stage from 410 p.m EDT on the 29th through 341 a.m. EDT on the 30th. It crested at 15.28 feet at 815 p.m. EDT on the 29th. The Red Clay Creek at Stanton had moderate flooding and was above its 15 foot flood stage from 239 p.m. EDT on the 29th through 245 a.m. EDT on the 30th. It crested at 17.02 feet at 700 p.m. EDT on the 29th. The Brandywine Creek at Wilmington was above its 16.5 foot flood stage from 747 a.m. EDT through 1143 a.m. EDT on the 30th. It crested at 16.69 feet at 800 a.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 8.33 inches in Delaney Corner, 7.65 inches in Newark, 6.88 inches in Bear and 5.01 inches at the New Castle County Airport.

The heavy rain that fell across Sussex County not only caused poor drainage and creek flooding, but exacerbated the tidal flooding along the Delaware Bay. Three roadways were flooded in Selbyville. The culvert over the Bunting Branch is expected to be closed until 2013. Evacuations occurred along the Nanticoke and Broad Creeks. Forty roadways were closed because of either flooding or high winds. The Nanticoke Creek at Bridgeville was above its 8 foot flood stage from 203 a.m. EDT through 422 p.m. EDT on the 30th. It crested at 8.25 feet at 915 a.m. EDT on the 30th. Event precipitation totals included 10.20 inches in Georgetown, 9.55 inches in Milford and 9.49 inches in Indian River Acres.

The heavy rain that fell across Kent County not only caused poor drainage and creek flooding, but exacerbated the tidal flooding along the Delaware Bay. The Saint Jones River flooded in Dover, but no homes were damaged. Forty roadways were closed either due to flooding or high winds. A couple of vehicles were submerged. Event precipitation totals included 9.14 inches in Dover, 8.47 inches at the Dover Air Force Base and 7.96 inches in Smyrna.

The Perkiomen Creek at East Greenville briefly reached its flood stage of 4.0 feet at 530 p.m. EDT on the 2nd. Event precipitation totals included 1.12 inches in Gilbertsville and 1.03 inches in Pottstown.

Elsewhere in the city, East 12th Street and Interstate 495 were also flooded. It crested at 15.19 feet at 945 a.m. EST.||Event precipitation totals included 2.45 inches in Newark, 1.64 inches in Newport, 1.44 inches at the Wilmington Airport and 1.43 inches in Middletown.

The Neshaminy Creek at Langhorne had moderate flooding and was above its 9 foot flood stage from 945 a.m. EST through 655 p.m. EST on the 21st. It crested at 10.08 feet at 315 p.m. EST.  Event precipitation totals included 2.33 inches in Doylestown, 2.09 inches in Springtown, 1.98 inches in Sellersville and 1.32 inches in Penndel.

The Wissahickon Creek at its mouth was above its 5 foot flood stage from 637 a.m. EST through 452 p.m. EST on the 21st. It crested at 6.39 feet at 2 p.m. EST on the 21st. The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge was above its 7 foot flood stage from 652 a.m. EST through 118 p.m. EST on the 21st. Event precipitation totals included 2.10 inches in Alburtis, 1.70 inches in Hamburg, 1.62 inches in Fleetwood, 1.45 inches at the Blue Marsh Dam, 1.34 inches in Wyomissing and 1.23 inches at the Reading Airport.

A 46 mph wind gust was recorded in Pittstown at 600 am EST on the morning of the 21st.  Elsewhere in the county, a large tree was reported down across Route 31 near mile-marker 36 just north of Clinton.

The Millstone River in Griggstown was above its 10 foot flood stage from 533 a.m. EST on the 27th through 207 a.m. EST on the 29th. It crested at 11.68 feet at 8 p.m. EST on the 27th.  The Griggstown Causeway was closed. Event precipitation totals included 1.49 inches in Peapack,  1.41 inches in Montgomery Township and 1.35 inches in Hillsborough Township.

Heavy rain caused flooding along many major roadways in northeastern Middlesex County and exacerbated the tidal flooding along Raritan Bay and the Arthur Kill. Flooding caused jughandle closures on U.S. Route 1 in South Brunswick Township and lane closures of New Jersey State Route 18 in East Brunswick Township. Roadway flooding also occurred in Woodbridge Township .Event precipitation totals included 2.24 inches in Woodbridge,  1.83 inches in East Brunswick, 1.80 inches in South Brunswick and 1.78 inches in New Brunswick.

In addition to river flooding, the heavy rain caused flooding of many major roadways in Monmouth County. It crested at 6.67 feet at 445 a.m. EST.  The Swimming River in Red Bank was above its 6 foot flood stage from 136 a.m. EST through 307 p.m. EST on the 27th. It crested at 7.11 feet at 6 a.m. EST. Farther downstream,  the Manasquan River at Allenwood was above its 14.5 foot flood stage from 448 a.m. EST on the 27th through Midnight EST on the 28th. It crested at 16.43 feet at 215 p.m. EST on the 27th.||Event precipitation totals included 5.90 inches in Howell, 4.12 inches in Eatontown,  3.94 inches in Belmar, 3.81 inches in Red Bank, 3.48 inches in Freehold and Fair Haven, 3.45 inches in Sea Girt and 3.33 inches in Manalapan.

The North Branch of the Rancocas Creek at Pemberton was above its 2.5 foot flood stage from 845 p.m. EST on the 27th through 945 a.m. EST on the 29th. In Lakewood Township, both directions of New Jersey State Route 70 near Union Avenue were flooded and closed.  In Toms River Township, both North Bay and New Hampshire Avenues were  flooded and closed. The North Branch of the Metedeconk River at Lakewood had moderate flooding and was above its 8 foot flood stage from 516 a.m. EST through 11 p.m. EST on the 27th. It crested at 9.37 feet at 415 p.m. EST on the 28th.  Event precipitation totals included  5.42 inches in Berkeley Township, 3.98 inches in Stafford Township, 3.83 inches in Brick Township, 2.56 inches in Point Pleasant and 2.55 inches in Jackson Township.

Heavy rain caused the flooding of the Bushkill Creek along the Forks and Palmer Township border on the morning of the 21st. Bushkill Drive was flooded and closed. A vehicle became trapped in the flood waters near the intersection of Zucksville Road and Bushkill Drive. The woman was able to get out of the car and walk away.  The northbound side of Bushkill Drive was reopened at 830 a.m. EST, the southbound side later that day. Event precipitation totals included 2.08 inches in Bethlehem, 2.06 inches in Hellertown, 2.00 inches in Glendon and 1.93 inches in Nazareth.

Heavy rain caused flooding along the Hackery Brook in Hackettstown. Both Manor Drive and East Baldwin Street were flooded and closed around the waterway.  Event precipitation totals included 2.33 inches in White Township, 2.30 inches in Hackettstown,  2.26 inches in Stewartsville, 2.16 inches in Broadway, 2.15 inches in Allamuchy Township, 2.05 inches in Phillipsburg, 1.91 inches in Belvidere and 1.78 inches in Blairstown.

Event precipitation totals included 2.17 inches in Holland Township, 2.12 inches in Alexandria Township, 1.57 inches in Frenchtown, 1.37 inches in Clinton and 1.19 inches in Flemington.

The Manatawny Creek near Spangsville had moderate flooding and was above its 6 foot flood stage from 318 a.m. EST through 1225 p.m. EST on the 31st. It crested at 7.43 feet at 715 a.m. EST. Event precipitation totals included 2.93 inches in Mohnton, 2.79 inches in Reading, 2.62 inches in Boyertown, 2.26 inches in Kutzville and 2.12 inches in Berne.

The Wissahickon Creek at its mouth was above its 5 foot flood stage from 945 a.m. EST through 1219 p.m. EST on the 31st. It crested at 5.23 feet at 1115 a.m. EST. Event precipitation totals included 1.28 inches in Wyndmoor, 1.18 inches in Rockledge and 0.94 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport. Heavier rain fell in upstream areas of the Wissahickon Basin in Montgomery County.

The Schuylkill River at Norristown was above its 13 foot flood stage from 820 a.m. EST through 628 p.m. EST on the 31st. It crested at 13.99 feet at 130 p.m. EST. The East Branch of the Perkiomen Creek at Schwenksville had moderate flooding and was above its 7 foot flood stage from 440 a.m. EST through 103 p.m. EST on the 31st. Event precipitation totals included 2.75 inches in Perkiomenville, 2.64 inches in Green Lane, 2.44 inches in Pottstown, 2.43 inches in Frederick, 2.37 inches in East Greenville, 2.09 inches in Gilbertsville, 1.62 inches in West Norriton, 1.60 inches in Blue Bell and 1.56 inches in Collegeville.

In Sellersville, flooding along the East Branch of the Perkiomen Creek forced the closure of the intersection of Main and Walnut Streets. In Quakertown, creek flooding affected Ninth and Main Streets and West End Boulevard. The East Branch of the Perkiomen Creek at Dublin was above its 5 foot flood stage from 421 a.m. EST through 549 a.m. EST on the 31st. It crested at 5.23 feet at 445 a.m. EST. Event precipitation totals included 2.64 inches in Pennsburg, 2.33 inches in Springtown, 1.79 inches in Perkasie, 1.53 inches in Doylestown and 1.14 inches in Langhorne.

The Brandywine Creek at Chadds Ford was above its 9 foot flood stage from 1231 p.m. EST through 515 p.m. EST on the 31st. It crested at 9.20 feet at 219 p.m. EST. The Crum Creek at Newtown Square was above its 6 foot flood stage from 616 a.m. EST through 745 a.m. EST on the 31st. It crested at 6.28 feet at 700 a.m. EST. Event precipitation totals included 1.37 inches in Aston.

The Neshanic River at Reaville was above its 5 foot flood stage from 450 p.m. EDT through 750 p.m. EDT on the12th. It crested at 5.37 feet at 6 p.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 1.64 inches in Holland Township, 1.39 inches in Bethlehem Township, 1.23 inches in Clinton, 1.20 inches in Stockton and 1.14 inches in Flemington.

The Main Stem of the Perkiomen Creek at East Greenville was above its 4 foot flood stage from 256 p.m. EDT through 714 p.m. EDT on the12th. It crested at 4.56 feet at 6 p.m. EDT. A lightning strike and ensuing fire destroyed a home and left a family homeless on Brahma Avenue in Bridgewater Township. Lightning struck the home's electrical system and sparked a fire. There was heavy fire damage on the second floor and smoke and water damage throughout the house. Three fire companies took about thirty minutes to extinguish the blaze. No serious injuries were reported.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and power lines in Washington Township in and around Old Post Road.  One man's head was injured when part of a tree fell on him. Chainsaws were needed to remove the downed trees from the roadway.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees onto wires on Gilbert Road in Chestnuthill Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in East Stroudsburg. One fell across Burson Street.

Lightning from a line of thunderstorms caused about 600 homes and businesses to lose power in Atlantic County with a few dozen additional outages in Cape May and Cumberland Counties. Traffic lights were out along the Black Horse Pike (U.S. Routes 40 and 322) in Egg Harbor Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding in the eastern part of Morris County. A few roadways were covered with water and the East Ditch overflowed its banks. Elsewhere in Morris County, some poor drainage flooding occurred. Event precipitation totals included 2.91 inches in Parsippany, 2.75 inches in Randolph,  2.63 inches in Roxbury,  2.62 inches in Denville, 2.58 inches in Boonton and 2.46 inches in Hanover Township.

The heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding and affected westbound U.S. Route 22 east of Potterstown Road in Readington Township. In addition, flooding was reported along Rockafellows Mill Road near the Rockafellows Mill Bridge. Event precipitation totals included 3.20 inches in Franklin Township, 2.71 inches in Lebanon, 2.66 inches in Clinton, 2.58 inches in Flemington and 2.46 inches in Readington Township.

The heavy rain caused roadway and poor drainage flooding in Mercer County. Event precipitation totals included 3.34 inches in Lawrence Township, 3.10 inches in Hamilton Township, 2.85 inches in Robbinsville Township and 2.10 inches in Princeton.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding in west central New Castle County from Glasgow north to near Newark. Event precipitation totals included 2.15 inches in Glasgow and 1.69 inches in Newark.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain also caused flash flooding of smaller streams and poor drainage areas in and around New Castle. Several vehicles became trapped in flood waters. No injuries were reported.  Event precipitation totals included 1.75 inches at the New Castle County Airport.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding as well as flash flooding of smaller streams in central Cecil County from Elkton southwest to Elk Neck State Park. The majority of flooded roadways occurred in the Elkton area. Event precipitation totals included 2.92 inches in Elkton.

Runoff from the heavy rain during the afternoon of the 30th continued flooding along the Raccoon Creek.  The Raccoon Creek above Swedesboro was above its 13 foot flood stage from 449 p.m. EDT through 1142 p.m. EDT on the 30th. It crested at 13.93 feet at 730 p.m. EDT.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding along roadways and small creeks near Mullica Hill in Harrison Township. Roadway flooding included the intersection of Walters Road and U.S. Route 322. The flooding also spread to the Raccoon Creek within Harrison Township. Event precipitation totals included 2.59 inches in Mullica Hill, 2.50 inches in Woolwich Township and 2.01 inches in South Harrison Township.
Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding along roadways and small creeks in Glassboro. Roadway flooding included East High Street (U.S. Route 322).

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding along roadways and smaller creeks in the southern part of Evesham Township.  Event precipitation totals included 2.10 inches in nearby Medford Lakes and 1.80 inches in Medford Township.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding along numerous roadways and smaller creeks in and around Atco in Waterford Township. The White Horse Pike (U.S. Route 30) and many yards were also flooded.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding along numerous roadways and smaller creeks in and around Woodstown and Pilesgrove Township in Salem County.  Event precipitation totals included 3.27 inches within Woodstown.
Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding of small creeks as well as roadway flooding in Muhlenberg and Ruscombmanor Townships.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding of small creeks (including Willow Creek) as well as roadway flooding (including Main Street) in Fleetwood. Event precipitation total in Fleetwood was 2.96 inches.
Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding of small creeks as well as roadway flooding in and around Bethel Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Hockessin (Mill Creek Hundred).
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees along Brackenville Road in Mill Creek Hundred.
A series of funnel clouds were spotted as a thunderstorm crossed northern New Castle County from Newark to Bear. None of them touched the ground or caused any damage.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Gibbstown and East Greenwich Township. A 61 mph wind gust was measured in Gibbstown.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and power lines along Harvard Avenue and at the intersection of Union and Atlantis Avenue in Stratford Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and power lines in Medford and Medford Lakes.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees and wires in Tabernacle Township.
A thunderstorm dropped up to penny size hail in West Creek (Eagleswood Township).
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires in and around Christina.
A funnel cloud was sighted over Port Deposit. It did not touch down or cause any damage.
A man was struck and injured by lightning where he was standing on Doctor Jack Road in Conowingo. He was taken to Christiana Hospital.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding in southern Delaware County. The Garnet Valley area of Bethel Township. Thunderstorms dropped 2.25 inches of rain in the area within 45 minutes.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding along the southern tier of Chester County.  Doppler Radar storm total estimates averaged 2 to 3 inches in this area. The White Clay Creek at Strickersville was above its 9.5 foot flood stage from 757 p.m. EDT through 910 p.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 9.75 feet at 845 p.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 2.47 inches in Landenburg.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding in Carbon County from Lansford and Summit Hill Township east through Jim Thorpe. Doppler Radar storm total estimates averaged 2 to 3 inches in this area.  Event precipitation totals included 1.75 inches in Coaldale and 1.58 inches in Jim Thorpe.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller creeks as well as poor drainage flooding in Salem County affecting Carneys Point and Oldman Township to the west of the New Jersey Turnpike. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached around two inches, most of which fell within one hour.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller creeks as well as poor drainage flooding in Gloucester County affecting the municipalities along the Delaware River.  Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached around two inches, most of which fell within one hour. Event precipitation totals included 1.83 inches in East Greenwich Township.

The thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding across the northern tier of New Castle County from Newark east through New Castle and northward to the Pennsylvania border. In Newark, Paper Mill Road was flooded from a tributary of the White Clay Creek. At least one vehicle was stuck in flood waters along the White Clay Creek itself.  Several vehicles were stuck in high water along South Chapel Street. Near Newark, flooding occurred on Delaware State Routes 2 and 7 and water rescues were performed. The Persimmon Creek flooded over a roadway and the Christina River flooded parkland. Flooding also occurred along Delaware State Route 1 and Interstate 95 in Christina Hundred. The Christina River at Coochs Bridge had major flooding and was above its 10.5 foot flood stage from 653 p.m. EDT on the 28th through 251 a.m. EDT on the 29th. It crested at 12.89 feet at 1115 p.m. EDT on the 28th. The White Clay Creek at Delaware Park had moderate flooding and was above its 13 foot flood stage from 649 p.m. EDT on the 28th through 154 a.m. EDT on the 29th. It crested at 15.25 feet at 945 p.m. EDT on the 28th.  Event precipitation totals included 3.55 inches in Newark, 2.49 inches in Newport, 2.37 inches in Wilmington and 2.13 inches in Hockessin.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding across northern Cecil County. More than a dozen roadways were closed, mostly in Elkton and North East. The Northeast Creek in North East exceeded its banks and flooded West Cecil Avenue, Washington Street and Russell Street. Washington and Russell Streets were closed through the night. Some water rescues were performed as flooding reached into properties near the creek. Also the rising water forced the evacuation of a Washington Street resident and six residents of an apartment building were evacuated after flood waters knocked over a gas can. In Elkton, Delaware Avenue and parts of Appleton Road and Elkton Road remained flooded and closed through most of the night of the 28th. In Rising Sun, the Stone Run Creek flooded playground equipment at Veterans Memorial Park on Wilson Avenue.  Portions of Barnes Corner Road, Jacob Tome Highway (Maryland State Route 276)  and Maryland State Route 274 were also flooded in Rising Sun and Old Elm and Warburton Roads flooded in North East. The Big Elk Creek at Elk Mills was above its 9 foot flood stage from 723 p.m. EDT through 848 p.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 9.28 feet at 730 p.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 2.84 inches in Elkton.

Heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding mainly in the western half of Chester County. It also led to flooding along sections of the East and West Branches of the Brandywine Creek.  The West Branch of the Brandywine Creek at Honey Brook had moderate flooding and was above its 7 foot flood stage from 707 p.m. EDT on the 27th through 218 a.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 9.01 feet at 1015 p.m. EDT on the 27th. Farther downstream, the West Branch of the Brandywine Creek at Coatesville was briefly above its 7 foot flood stage from 818 p.m. EDt through 904 p.m. EDT on the 27th. It crested at 7.04 feet at 845 p.m. EDT. The East Branch of the Brandywine Creek below Downingtown had moderate flooding and was above its 7 foot flood stage from 945 p.m. EDT on the 27th through 129 a.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 8.40 feet at 1145 p.m. EDT on the 27th.  Event precipitation totals included 2.36 inches in Modena, 2.27 inches in West Grove and 2.01 inches in Glenmoore.

Heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding in Warwick, Warrington and Warminster Townships. Mearns Road north of Bristol Road was closed due to flooding as was Creek Road near the Little Neshaminy Creek. Doppler Radar storm total estimates in the area were between 1.0 and 1.5 inches.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding and flash flooding of smaller creeks in the northwest half of Mercer County from Ewing Township northeast through Hopewell and Princeton Townships. In Pennington Borough, West Delaware Avenue and New Jersey State Route 31 were flooded. Yards and driveways were also flooded in Pennington and also in Lawrence Township.  Event precipitation totals included 3.31 inches in Lawrence Township, 3.22 inches in Pennington Borough, 2.97 inches in Ewing Township, 2.50 inches in Trenton and 2.36 inches at the Mercer County Airport.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding and flash flooding of smaller creeks in the western half of Somerset County during the evening of the 27th and affected Branchburg, Hillsborough and Montgomery Townships the most.  In Branchburg Township,  the Chambers Brook flooded.  In Bedmister Township, the Middle Brook also flooded. Event precipitation totals included 3.20 inches in Neshanic, 2.71 inches in Bridgewater Township, 2.45 inches in Hillsborough Township,  2.44 inches in Somerville and 2.12 inches in Montgomery Township.

Runoff from heavy rain that fell during the early evening of the 27th led to isolated flooding on area brooks and rivers into the afternoon of the 28th.  The Millstone River at Griggstown was above its 10 foot flood stage from 515 a.m. EDT through 5 p.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 10.15 feet at 730 a.m. EDT. The Middle Brook at Burnt Mills was above its 8 foot flood stage from 935 p.m. EDT on the 27th through 1225 a.m. EDT on the 29th. It crested at 9.23 feet at 1045 p.m. EDT on the 27th.

Runoff from heavy rain that fell during the early evening of the 27th led to isolated flooding along the Assunpink Creek early on the 28th.  The Assunpink Creek at Mercerville was briefly above its 9.5 foot flood stage from 255 a.m. EDT through 307 a.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 9.51 feet at 3 a.m. EDT.

A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a home on Lindsay Street in Ridley Park. Lightning struck and started a fire in the basement and also traveled along the electrical wiring within the house.  The furniture, electronics and clothing were all damaged within the home. The unharmed family was expected to be displaced for about six months.
A lightning strike damaged a home in Swarthmore.
A lightning strike damaged a home in Upper Providence Township.
A lightning strike damaged a home in Aston Township.

A man was injured by a lightning strike while working on the Glen Mills Reform School's baseball field in Concord Township.  From 2 p.m. EDT to 3 p.m. EDT there were over 1,000 cloud-to-ground lightning strikes in the local Philadelphia area.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees along Pennsylvania State Route 272 and Kirks Mill Road in West Nottingham Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a tree near Creek Road and Pennsylvania State Route 52 in Birmingham Township.

A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage across a couple of townships in Upper Bucks County.  In Springfield Township, trees and wires were knocked down on Old Bethlehem, Hickory, Slifer Valley and Blue Church Roads. In Durham Township, trees and wires were knocked down along Gallows Hill and Lehnenberg Roads. In Haycock Township, a sailboat was overturned on Lake Nockamixon, but no injuries were reported.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees, poles  and wires across a couple of roads in Nazareth. Trees were reported knocked down on Graceland Avenue and a downed tree damaged a vehicle (no injuries were reported) on Myers Street.

An EF0 tornado was confirmed near Newark at 447 p.m. EDT. The damage was focused from Ardmore Drive to Argyle Road, south of DE Route 4. Within this area, 10 to 20 homes sustained damage with several homes suffering significant damage due to large trees being blown into them. On Natalie Lane, a very large tree completely fell over and landed onto two homes with a car having significant damage. Other homes suffered siding and shingle damage. One house on Argyle Road had a tree limb through a side wall. On Havertown Road, several trees were uprooted, with some lying west and northwest, which appeared to be the western edge of the circulation. Several residents reported hearing a whooshing sound that lasted for about 10 to 15 seconds, along with some tree debris swirling into the air. Based on damage reports, the tornado briefly lifted with the main touchdown located from Ardmore Drive to Argyle Road. ||Additional damage was reported to the south of the tornado path, including siding and tree damage. One she was reportedly blown onto its side along McCormick Boulevard. The overall path length was nearly one mile. The maximum path width was 150 yards and the estimated maximum wind was 80 mph.

The East Branch of the Brandywine Creek at Downingtown was above its 7 foot flood stage from 834 a.m. EDT through 124 p.m. EDT on the 10th, and it crested at 8.67 feet at 1130 a.m. EDT. Several roads were closed in Chester County due to flooding, including PA Route 926 and Westtown Road in Westtown Township. Creek Road was also closed by PennDot for a time due to flooding. Event precipitation totals included 3.01 inches in Modena, 2.24 inches in West Chester, 2.14 inches in Valley Forge, and 2.12 inches in Northbrook.

The Christina River at Coochs Bridge had moderate flooding and was above its 10.5 foot flood stage from 614 p.m. EDT through 1016 p.m. EDT on the 10th. It crested at 11.54 feet at 815 p.m. EDT. Additional rainfall amounts include 1.70 inches in Prices Corner, 1.62 inches in Newark, 1.56 inches in Newport, 1.44 inches in Clayton and 1.06 inches in Middletown.

The Pompton River at Midwood was above its 7.5 foot flood stage from 150 p.m. EDT on the 14th through 335 a.m. EDT on the 16th. It crested at 8.04 feet at 1010 a.m. EDT on the 15th. The Pompton River at Ryerson Road was above its 12 foot flood stage from 225 a.m. EDT through 1210 p.m. EDT on the 15th. It crested at 12.03 feet at 740 a.m. EDT on the 15th.

Heavy rain that fell in the week leading up to the 14th caused the Millstone River to overflow its banks. The Millstone River at Griggstown was above its 10 foot flood stage from 530 a.m. EDT on the 14th through 515 a.m. EDT on the 15th. It crested at 10.35 feet at 430 p.m. EDT on the 14th.

Event precipitation totals included 1.81 inches in Bear, 1.73 inches in Newark, 1.21 inches in Middletown and 1.10 inches in Hockessin.

It crested at 8.50 feet at 1245 a.m. EDT on the 8th. ||Then, runoff from heavy rain that fell from the 7th into the 8th led to flooding on several gaged rivers and streams across Somerset County. The Raritan River at Bound Brook was above its 28 foot flood stage from 748 a.m. EDT through 745 p.m. EDT on the 8th, and it crested at 29.14 feet at 130 p.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 4.06 inches in Easton, 3.20 inches in Royal Oak, and 3.14 inches in Saint Michaels.

The Millstone River at Griggstown was above its 10 foot flood stage from 856 p.m. EDT on the 10th through 805 p.m. EDT on the 12th. It crested at 12.76 feet at 430 p.m. EDT on the 11th. The Millstone River at Millstone was above its 8.5 foot flood stage from 552 a.m. EDT on the 11th through 122 p.m. EDT on the 12th. It crested at 9.51 feet at 800 p.m. EDT on the 11th. The North Branch Raritan River at South Branch was above its 7 foot flood stage from 1040 p.m. EDT on the 10th through 508 a.m. EDT on the 11th. It crested at 7.67 feet at 230 a.m. EDT on the 11th. Event precipitation totals included 1.80 inches Hillsborough Township, 1.75 inches in Franklin Township, 1.67 inches in Warren Township, 1.62 inches in Montgomery Township, and 1.51 inches in Bridgewater Township.

Heavy rain led to flash flooding along some roadways and smaller rivers in Camden County. The Cooper River at Haddonfield was above its 2.8 foot flood stage from 1252 p.m. EDT through 451 p.m. EDT on the 10th, and it crested at 2.99 feet at 215 p.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 1.91 inches in Mount Ephraim, 1.88 inches in Collingswood, 1.69 inches in Merchantville, and 1.42 inches in Somerdale.

Runoff from heavy rain that fell during the 10th led to flooding along smaller creeks in Burlington County. The North Branch of the Rancocas Creek at Pemberton was above its 2.5 foot flood stage from 115 a.m. EDT on the 11th through 1100 a.m. EDT on the 12th. It crested at 2.54 feet at 1045 a.m. EDT on the 11th.
