Event precipitation totals included 3.00 inches in Hainesport Township, 2.31 inches in Mount Laurel Township, 2.06 inches in Wrightstown, 1.84 inches in Pemberton, and 1.74 inches in Tabernacle Township.

Runoff from heavy rain that fell during the 10th led to flooding along gaged rivers and creeks in Philadelphia County. The Wissahickon Creek at the mouth in Philadelphia was above its 5 foot flood stage from 1135 p.m. EDT on the 10th through 425 a.m. EDT on the 11th. It crested at 5.60 feet at 200 a.m. EDT on the 11th. The tidal Delaware River at Philadelphia was above its 8.2 foot flood stage from 306 a.m. EDT through 413 a.m. EDT on the 11th, and it crested at 8.40 feet. Event precipitation totals included 2.20 inches in Rockledge and 1.37 inches in Philadelphia.

Heavy rain that fell during the 10th led to flash flooding along roadways and gaged creeks and streams in Delaware County. The Chester Creek at Chester had moderate flooding and was above its 8 foot flood stage from 636 p.m. EDT through 1049 p.m. EDT on the 10th, and it crested at 10.93 feet at 845 p.m. EDT. The Crum Creek at Newtown Square was above its 6 foot flood stage from 518 p.m. EDT through 1022 p.m. EDT on the 10th, and it crested at 9.34 feet at 700 p.m. EDT. Several roads were closed due to high water in Delaware County; including Westtown Road, Westtown-Thornton Road, and Creek Road. Event precipitation totals included 3.22 inches in Wayne and 1.37 inches in Chester Heights.

Heavy rain that fell during the 10th led to flashing flooding of some roadways and gaged creeks and streams in Bucks County. The Neshaminy Creek at Langhorne was above its 9 foot flood stage from 1123 p.m. EDT on the 10th through 625 a.m. EDT on the 11th. It crested at 9.60 feet at 145 a.m. EDT on the 11th. The East Branch of the Perkiomen Creek at Dublin was above its 5 foot flood stage from 802 p.m. EDT through 845 p.m. EDT on the 10th. It crested at 5.18 feet at 815 p.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 2.21 inches in Langhorne, 1.99 inches in Penndel, 1.51 inches in Pennsburg, and 1.33 inches in Quakertown.

Heavy rain during the 10th led to flash flooding of some roadways and gaged steams and creeks in Montgomery County. The Wissahickon Creek at Fort Washington was above its 9 foot flood stage from 748 p.m. EDT through 1141 p.m. EDT on the 10th, and it crested at 10.20 feet at 1000 p.m. EDT. The East Branch of the Perkiomen Creek at Schwenksville was above its 7 foot flood stage from 1138 a.m. EDT through 145 p.m. EDT on the 10th. It crested at 7.58 feet at 130 p.m. EDT. The river rose above its flood stage a second time from 1142 p.m. EDT on the 10th through 423 a.m. EDT on the 11th. The second crest was 7.79 feet at 230 a.m. EDT on the 11th. Event precipitation totals included 3.61 inches in North Wales, 3.33 inches in Hatfield, 2.99 inches in Kulpsville, 2.63 inches in Blue Bell, 2.45 inches in Harleysville, and 2.36 inches in Collegeville.
Heavy rain through the morning to afternoon of the 10th led to flooding of some roadways in Southampton Township. County Road 530 was flooded in multiple locations.

Heavy rain through the morning to afternoon of the 10th led to flooding of some roadways in and around Wall Township. Flooding caused lane closures on the Garden State Parkway between mile-markers 91 and 93 and also between mile-markers 95 and 97.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Pittsgrove Township.

Heavy rain caused flooding along roadways and small creeks in Aberdeen Township. Roadway flooding occurred along NJ Route 35 near the intersection of County Road at milemarker 45 in Aberdeen Township. All lanes were closed and detoured due to flooding. Nearby event precipitation totals included 3.21 inches in Holmdel Township.

Heavy rain led to flooding of a few gaged creeks and streams in Mercer County. The Assunpink Creek at Mercerville was above its 9.5 foot flood stage from 1012 p.m. EDT on the 7th through 539 a.m. EDT on the 8th. It crested at 10.67 feet at 230 a.m. EDT on the 8th. The Assunpink Creek at Trenton was above its 8.5 foot flood stage from 1102 p.m. EDT on the 7th through 546 a.m. EDT on the 8th. It crested at 8.98 feet at 315 a.m. EDT on the 8th. The Stony Brook at Princeton was above its 9 foot flood stage from 1000 p.m. EDT on the 7th through 448 a.m. EDT on the 8th. It crested at 9.72 feet at 1230 a.m. on the 8th. Event precipitation totals included 4.44 inches in Lawrence Township, 4.33 inches in Ewing Township, 4.15 inches in Pennington, 4.06 inches in Princeton, 4.04 inches in Somerset, and 3.97 inches in Hamilton Township.

Torrential rains resulted in flash flooding in northeastern Northampton County.  Several home basements were flooded with two to five feet of water on Messinger Street in Bangor Borough as an underground creek rose and flooded. One family on Messenger Street was rescued. Two garages on the street were also damaged. Fuel oil leaked into the water. Flooding closed Messinger Road, Viaduct Road, South Main Street, and Rutt Road in the borough. No injuries were reported. Power was out to a number of homes for precautionary reasons also because water reached into the ground floor.  The flooding occurred because of an underground creek near the headwaters of Martins Creek.  Numerous streets were also flooded in Penn Argyl Borough.  Flooding waters also damaged a few homes in East Bangor Borough. The axis of heaviest rain extended from Penn Argyl and Washington Township northeastward through Upper Mount Bethel Township in Northampton County. Event precipitation totals included 3.54 inches in Nazareth and 2.07 inches in Bethlehem.  These municipalities were south of where the heaviest rain fell and Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached around 5 inches within the axis of heaviest rain.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding in eastern Monroe County in eastern sections of Smithfield and Middle Smithfield Townships. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 5 inches in the eastern parts of the townships.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding in northwest Warren County in Knowlton, Pahaquarry, and Hardwick Townships and affected the Worthington State Forest area the hardest.  Doppler Radar storm total estimates nearly reached 5 inches in the northwest part of the county. Event precipitation totals included 2.90 inches in Hope and 1.94 inches in Pequest.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding in central Hunterdon County from Kingwood and Alexandria Townships northeastward through Readington and Tewksbury Townships. U.S. Route 22 in Readington Township was flooded in both directions as was Interstate 78 in Clinton Township. In Readington Township, the approach to the Rockefellow Mills Bridge over the South Branch of the Raritan River was flooded. Flooding was reported along the South Branch of the Rockaway Creek in Whitehouse Station, the Neshanic River at Reaville (crested at 6.94 feet), the South Branch of the Raritan River near Stanton and the Mulhockaway Creek in Clinton. The Beaver Brook flooded into the parking lot of the municipal building in Clinton.  Widespread street flooding was reported in Kingwood Township. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached around 3 inches in this band and actual storm totals included 2.50 inches in Readington Township, 2.41 inches in Franklin Township, 2.40 inches in Lebanon Township, 2.34 inches in Frenchtown, 2.08 inches in Stockton, 1.95 inches in Pittstown and 1.71 inches in Kingwood.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding in Parsippany-Troy Hills Township. Eastbound Interstate 80 was flooded as was Interstate 287 in both directions. The ramp from Interstate 80 to Interstate 287 was also flooded. Ramps onto U.S. Route 46 and Interstate 80 were also flooded and closed. Several streets within the township were covered with rapidly flowing water. East of Morristown, the Columbia Turnpike exit east of New Jersey State Route 24 was flooded and closed. Event precipitation totals included 2.23 inches in Parsippany and 2.19 inches in Morristown.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding as well as field flooding in the northwest part of Somerset County centered in and around Bridgewater, Branchburg, Bedminster and Bernards Townships. The North Branch area was flooded in Branchburg Township. Burnt Mills Road was flooded and closed as was New Jersey State Route 28 (Easton Turnpike) at the North Branch Bridge. In Bridgewater Township, flooding along U.S. Route 22 blocked the eastbound entrance to Interstate 287. A few flooded roadways had rapidly moving water passing over them in Bernards Township. This included left lane flooding on Interstate 287 that necessitated a closure.  Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached around three inches in the township and street flooding was reported. Event precipitation totals included 2.34 inches in Bernards Township and 2.29 inches in Basking Ridge.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding across central and northern Montgomery County. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 2.0 to 2.5 inches across most of this area. In Towamencin Township, a motorist had to be rescued from flood waters. Event precipitation totals included 3.33 inches in Royersford and 2.53 inches in Hatfield.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Hillsborough Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several large trees, tree limbs and wires in Bridgewater Township. There were a few road closures. Downed trees and wires were reported on Old York as well as Foothill Road.

Heavy rain fell across southeast Carbon County and caused poor drainage flooding in Towamensing and Lower Towamensing Townships. Event precipitation totals included 2.56 inches in Weatherly and 1.22 inches in Beltzville.

Heavy rain fell across western Monroe County and caused poor drainage flooding in Polk, Jackson and Chestnuthill Townships. In Chestnuthill Township, flooding carried debris onto the intersection of Toll and Merwinsburg Roads.  Event precipitation totals included 2.66 in Kresgeville, 1.96 inches in Pocono Pines and 1.60 inches in Mount Pocono.
A funnel cloud formed during a thunderstorm over Greenwich Township. It did not touch down, there were no reports of wind damage.

A 48-year-old man was hospitalized after being struck by lightning on the Ocean Beach area of Island Beach State Park.  The man was fishing at the time and it was suspected that the lightning might have initially struck his fishing pole. The man complained about numbness in his legs and was taken to Jersey Shore University Medical Center in Neptune.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees and wires in Sadsbury Township.
Lightning struck and damaged a home in Valley Township.
Nickel size hail fell from a thunderstorm in Ledgewood (Roxbury Township).

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees, power lines, and power poles in Mine Hill Township at 8:13 p.m. EDT on the 7th.  One tree was reported to have fallen on a home.  The heaviest damage was reported in a wooded area between Route 10 and Canfield Avenue in Mine Hill Township, with a portion of Canfield Avenue being closed as a result.  Traffic lights were reported out along Route 10 and Route 467.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees, power lines, and transmission poles in Dover Township at 8:15 p.m. EDT on the 7th.  Several private residences and homes were damaged as a result.  Tree damage was also reported near St. Clare's Hospital.

Thunderstorms with torrential doownpours caused flash flooding on Kent Island during the morning of the 12th. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 7 inches south of Stevensville.  Flash flooding was reported on Maryland State Route 8 from Batts Neck Road southward.  Event precipitation totals included 5.64 inches in Stevensville and 3.60 inches in Centreville.

Thunderstorms with torrential doownpours caused flash flooding across central and northern Talbot County during the late morning and early afternoon on the 12th. Kingston Landing Road was closed after sections of it washed away. Four other roadways were flooded and closed including Maryland State Routes 309 and 328. There were several vehicular water rescues near Easton, but no injuries were reported.  Event precipitation totals were 3.36 inches in St. Michaels and 2.66 inches in Easton. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 4 inches in the heaviest band across the county.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding of creeks and roadways in southwestern Caroline County near the Tuckahoe River. Event precipitation totals included 3.42 inches in Henderson, 2.66 inches in Greensboro and 1.80 inches in Federalsburg.  Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 4 inches in the heaviest band in the county.
A severe thunderstorm caused roofing damage to several structures in Greenwich Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Spring Township.
A severe thunderstorm also knocked down a couple of trees in Cumru Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of large tree limbs and trees in Saint Lawrence Borough. One downed tree took down wires in the borough..
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Rockland Township..
Nickel size hail fell in the Kutztown area of Longswamp Township.
A Skywarn Spotter estimated wind gusts to severe levels during a thunderstorm in Brookhaven. Several large tree limbs were knocked down.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 66 mph at the Philadelphia International Airport.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in National Park.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in East Greenwich Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees and wires along Hessian Avenue in West Deptford Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees and wires in Woodbury.  A Skywarn spotter measured a wind gust of 52 mph withiin the city.
A lightning strike took down a couple of wires in Bordentown.

Nearly stationary thunderstorms dropped heavy rain and caused flash flooding in south central Delaware mainly to the southwest of Millsboro. There was widespread ponding of water on roadways, construction equipment was seen floating in the flood waters. Doppler Radar storm total estimates exceeded four inches southwest of Millsboro.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in Wilmington.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in the northeast part of Cecil County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down about eight trees in Pittstown (Alexandria Township).

A severe thunderstorm produced a 60 mph wind gust, measured at the Philadelphia International Airport at 141 a.m. EDT.  Radar imagery showed this thunderstorm wind gust to be the result of a wet microburst. The airport weather observer confirmed the occurrence of the wind gust. Elsewhere in the city, a downed tree forced the suspension of SEPTA commuter rail service between Center City and Thorndale in Chester County.  Service was restored later that day, but 30 minute delays along the line continued.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller streams and creeks in and around Upper Providence Township. Water rescues occurred within the township, but no serious injuries were reported. Event precipitation totals included 4.15 inches in Media.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain led to flash flooding in the Long Neck area of Indian River Hundred. Flood waters reached a foot deep on roadways. Event precipitation totals included 8.38 inches in Long Neck.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain led to flash flooding from Selbyville east in southern Sussex County. A few roads were closed and sections of Lighthouse and Sand Cove Roads collapsed.  Event precipitation totals included 5.50 inches in Selbyville.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding from Millville and Oceanview east to Bethany Beach. Water rescues were performed, but no serious injuries were reported. In Bethany Beach, Hollywood Street and Pennsylvania Avenuie were flooded as people resorted to kayaking to move around. Event precipitation totals included 6.62 inches in Bethany Beach.
Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding of roadways and small streams in and around Frankford. Event precipitation totals included 7.05 inches in Frankford.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding of roadways and small streams from Dagsboro east along the southern shore of the Indian River Bay.  High water was reported on Vines Creek Road, Warren Wingate Lane, Holts Landing Road and Waltersbluff Road.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding of roadways and small streams from Dagsboro northwestward toward Georgetown.  High water was reported on Hardscrabble Road (Delaware State Route 20), Shortly Road, Kendall Street and Laurel Road (Delaware State Route 24). Event precipitation totals included 4.20 inches in Stockley and 3.70 inches in Georgetown.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding of roadways and small streams and eventually flooding along the Saint Jones River in central Kent County. In Dover, several vehicles became stranded in flood waters as numerous roadways flooded. Several stranded motorists had to abandon their vehicles. The water was also several feet deep at the Kent General Hospital in Dover. The Little Creek in Port Mahon flooded and shut down Main Street and Delaware State Route 9. Numerous basements were flooded. Event precipitation totals included 5.46 inches in Dover, 3.49 inches in Sandtown, 3.45 inches at the Dover Air Force Base and 2.46 inches in Smyrna.

Showers and thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage flash flooding in the southern third of Cape May County. Event precipitation totals included 5.60 inches in Green Creek, 5.51 inches in Erma, 3.83 inches in Cape May,  3.71 inches in Cape May Harbor and 3.12 inches in Wildwood Crest.

A brief gustnado formed along a gust front from a severe thunderstorm at 510 p.m. EDT on the 22nd in the Cedar Glen West community along the Manchester and Jackson Township border in Ocean County. A gust front is the leading edge of winds that are produced from a downdraft in a severe thunderstorm. It is along this gust front that some rotation developed and a gustnado formed. A gustnado's rotation begins at the ground and spins up, and it does not connect with any cloud base rotation. The gustnado on the afternoon of the 22nd contained winds of up to 60 mph, and it brought down several trees and produced some minor roof damage in the Cedar Glen West community.  Two homes along Vath Street suffered minor roof damage.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused small stream, poor drainage and field flash flooding along the northern tier of Kent County affecting Duck Creek and Kenton Hundreds and Smyrna and Clayton the hardest. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 3 to 5 inches in this area.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused small stream, poor drainage and field flash flooding along the southern northern tier of New Castle County affecting Blackbird and Appoquinimink Hundreds the hardest.  Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 3 to 6 inches in this area. Actual rainfall amounts included 3.34 inches in Blackbird Hundred.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused urban, small stream and poor drainage flash flooding in northeastern New Castle County from around Bear northeast through Claymont.  Poor drainage flooding occurred on U.S. Route 13 north of Rogers Road in Wilmington. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 2 to 4 inches in this area. Actual rainfall amounts included 2.32 inches in Wilmington and 1.72 inches at the New Castle County Airport.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding in northeastern Lehigh County and affected Washington and Heidelberg Townships the most where Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 3 to 4 inches. Measured event precipitation totals included 2.09 inches in Slatington and 1.48 inches in Schnecksville.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding in southeastern Monroe County and affected Hamilton, Stroud, Smithfield and Middle Smithfield Townships as well as Stroudsburg and East Stroudsburg the hardest as Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 4 to 6 inches within parts of these municipalities. Measured event precipitation totals included 3.67 inches in East Stroudsburg, 2.92 inches in Middle Smithfield Township and 2.74 inches in Blakeslee.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused urban and poor drainage flash flooding in Philadelphia. Multiple ramps of Interstate 95 around Broad Street were closed. A 21-year-old woman drowned after she accidentally drove into the Schuylkill River near Boathouse Road in Philadelphia. A 31-year-old male passenger managed to swim to safety. The river was running higher than average, but was not flooding at the time of the drowning. SEPTA Regional rail lines reported flooding on tracks within Philadelphia. The flooding rains caused portions of Terminal A at Philadelphia International Airport to lose power. Departure and arrival delays reached 90 minutes and seventeen flights were cancelled. Event precipitation totals included 8.26 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport and 1.84 inches in Center City.  The precipitation gradient was tremendous over Philadelphia as only 0.64 inches fell at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport.||A total of 8.02 inches of rain fell at the Philadelphia International Airport on the 28th. The amount not only established a new record daily maximum rainfall for that date, but was also the most rainfall on record for any calendar day in Philadelphia. The previous record was set on September 16, 1999 during Tropical Storm Floyd and was 6.63 inches.  This torrential downpour also helped establish a new July monthly rainfall record of 13.24 inches in Philadelphia. The previous record was 10.42 inches set in 1994.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused urban and poor drainage flash flooding along all of the municipalities that border the Delaware River.  Event precipitation totals included 8.26 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport and 1.84 inches in Center City.  The precipitation gradient was tremendous over the county as only 0.80 inches fell in Swarthmore and 0.40 inches fell in Havertown.

Runoff from heavier rain caused minor flooding along the Valley Creek on the evening of the 28th. The Valley Creek at Valley Forge was above its 7 foot flood stage from 925 p.m. EDT through 956 p.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 7.11 feet at 945 p.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 2.32 inches in Kennett Square, 1.34 inches in Valley Forge and 1.19 inches in West Chester.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding mainly in the northeast part of Hunterdon County. Event precipitation totals included 3.18 inches in Readington Township, 2.51 inches in Lebanon, 2.10 inches in Flemington and 2.09 inches in Frenchtown.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding mainly in the southeast part of Morris County. Event precipitation totals included 3.33 inches in Chester, 3.32 inches in Randolph Township, 2.43 inches in Netcong and Parsippany-Troy Hills and 2.25 inches in Long Hill Township.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding mainly in the northwest part of Somerset County. Event precipitation totals included 3.15 inches in Pottersville, 3.04 inches in Bedminster Township, 2.99 inches in Basking Ridge, 2.96 inches in Bernards Township, 2.83 inches in Branchburg Township, 2.71 inches in Bridgewater Township, 2.53 inches in Far Hills and 1.84 inches in Hillsborough Township.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in western Salem County and affected Carneys Point and Pennsville Township the hardest. In Pennsville, two women were rescued from their vehicles on North Broadway. In Carneys Point, Ives Avenue, Hickory Avenue and U.S. Route 130 were all flooded and closed. A Cumberland Farms store within the township suffered flood damage. Field flash flooding damaged tomato crops in the county. Event precipitation totals included 5.93 inches in Pennsville Township.

A second wave of thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage, creek and field flash flooding in eastern Salem County. Event precipitation totals included 3.84 inches in Pittsgrove Township.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding in western Burlington County. The Southwest Branch of the Rancocas Creek flooded sections of the Golden Pheasant Golf Course in Lumberton. In Southampton. several apartment buildings flooded at the Sherwood Village Complex. Event precipitation totals included 2.91 inches in Mount Laurel, 2.76 inches in Mount Holly, 2.37 inches in Cinnaminson, 2.32 inches in Westampton, 2.08 inches in Palmyra and 2.05 inches in Moorestown.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding along the western tier of Gloucester County. In Paulsboro, numerous roads were flooded and closed. Some homes were flooded near the Mantua Creek. In Greenwich Township, one motorist had to be rescued from flood waters. A sewer main breakage exacerbated the ongoing flooding. Field flash flooding damaged tomato crops in the county. Event precipitation totals included 4.55 inches in East Greenwich Township, 4.25 inches in Mickleton, 4.15 inches in Westville, 3.78 inches in West Deptford, 3.77 inches in Mullica Hill, 2.75 inches in Woolwich Township, 2.30 inches in Wenonah and 1.91 inches in South Harrison Township.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in western Camden County that damaged vehicles and jammed traffic on major roadways for hours. People were trapped in vehicles for hours. Numerous vehicles were submerged to their tops with multiple rescues on the 42 Freeway, Interstate 76 and in Brooklawn, Camden and Gloucester City. In spite of all of the rescues, no serious injuries were reported. In Gloucester City, U.S. Route 130 was completely submerged. In Collingswood, U.S. Route 30 was closed. On the other side of the Cooper River, waves of water occurred on the Admiral Wilson Boulevard in Pennsauken and Camden. In Barrington, three feet of water accumulated on Clement Bridge Road (New Jersey State Route 41) and raw sewage backed up into apartment buildings. In Camden, the Ferry Avenue PATCO parking lot was flooded. Event precipitation totals included 5.37 inches in Audubon, 5.17 inches in Mount Ephraim, 5.05 inches in Haddonfield, 5.00 inches in Merchantville, 3.63 inches in Collingswood, 3.55 inches in Somerdale, 3.20 inches in Cherry Hill, 2.60 inches in Pennsauken and 2.50 inches in Voorhees Township.

A second wave of thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding in southeastern Camden County. Event precipitation totals included 3.22 inches in Winslow Township.

A second wave of thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused field, small stream and poor drainage flash flooding in southeastern Gloucester County. Event precipitation totals included 3.86 inches in Malaga in Franklin Township.

The runoff from the torrential downpours that fell earlier on the day on the 28th caused minor to moderate flooding on area creeks and rivers in northern Camden County.  The Cooper River at Haddonfield had moderate flooding and was above its 2.8 foot flood stage from 625 p.m. EDT on the 28th through 526 a.m. EDT on the 29th. It crested at 4.13 feet at 1115 p.m. EDT on the 28th.  The South Branch of the Pennsauken Creek at Cherry Hill was above its 9 foot flood stage from 1022 p.m. EDT on the 28th through 639 a.m. EDT on the 29th. It crested at 10.03 feet at 3 a.m. EDT on the 29th. Event precipitation totals included 3.20 inches in Cherry Hill, 2.60 inches in Pennsauken and 2.50 inches in Voorhees Township.

The runoff from the torrential downpours that fell earlier on the day on the 28th caused flooding on area creeks in southwestern Burlington County.  The South Branch of the Pennsauken Creek near Mill Road on New Jersey State Route 38 in Cherry Hill was above its 9 foot flood stage from 1022 p.m. EDT on the 28th through 639 a.m. EDT on the 29th. It crested at 10.03 feet at 3 a.m. EDT on the 29th. Event precipitation totals included 2.91 inches in Mount Laurel, 2.37 inches in Cinnaminson, 2.08 inches in Palmyra and 2.05 inches in Moorestown..

The runoff from the torrential downpours that fell overnight caused the Cohansey River at Seeley (Hopewell Township) to crest at its 6 foot flood stage from 715 a.m. EDT through 8 a.m. EDT on the 29th. Event precipitation totals included 2.79 inches in Upper Deerfield Township, 2.57 inches in Greenwich Township and 2.07 inches at Seabrook Farms.

The runoff from the heavy downpours that fell earlier on the 28th caused some minor flooding along rivers and brooks in northwest Somerset County centered around Bedminster and Branchburg Townships. The Lamington River at Burnt Mills (Bedminster Township) was above its 9.5 foot flood stage from 723 p.m. EDT on the 28th through 101 a.m. EDT on the 29th. It crested at 10.51 feet at 11 p.m. EDT on the 28th..The Middle Brook at Burnt Mills (Bedminster Township) was above its 8 foot flood stage from 559 p.m. EDT through 822 p.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 9.18 feet at 7 p.m. EDT. The North Branch of the Raritan River at South Branch was above its 7 foot flood stage from 1021 p.m. EDT on the 28th through 1248 a.m. EDT on the 29th. It crested at 7.42 feet at Midnight EDT. Event precipitation totals included 3.15 inches in Pottersville, 3.04 inches in Bedminster Township, 2.99 inches in Basking Ridge, 2.96 inches in Bernards Township, 2.83 inches in Branchburg Township, 2.71 inches in Bridgewater Township, 2.53 inches in Far Hills and 1.84 inches in Hillsborough Township.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding of smaller creeks and roadways in western Cumberland County.  Particularly hard hit by flooding was New Jersey State Route 77 in Upper Deerfield Township and Bridgeton City. Event precipitation totals included 2.79 inches in Upper Deerfield Township, 2.57 inches in Greenwich Township and 2.07 inches at Seabrook Farms.

Heavy rain fell the night of the 22nd and again in the early morning hours of the 23rd. The runoff from all of the rain caused the Rancocas Creek to exceed its flood stage. Flooding closed Mill and King Streets as well as Rancocas-Mount Holly Road along the creek. The North Branch of the Rancocas Creek at Iron Works Park was above its 11.7 foot flood stage from 922 a.m. EDT through 145 p.m. EDT on the 23rd. It crested at 11.74 feet at 1115 a.m. EDT.

Heavy rain fell through the night of the 22nd and caused urban and poor drainage flash flooding. Several areas of significant flooding were reported on the Schuylkill Expressway. Significant flooding was also reported on Broad Street in South Philadelphia under Interstate 95, with vehicles trapped. The water level was reported to be nearly up to the car windows. Deep standing water occurred on Interstate 95. The heavy rain flooded sections of the 8th and Market PATCO Commuter rail line stop. The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge was above its 7 foot flood stage from 242 a.m. EDT through 255 a.m. EDT on the 23rd. It crested at 7.25 feet at 245 a.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 1.50 inches in Northeast Philadelphia, 1.29 inches in Rockledge and 1.18 inches in Northwest Philadelphia.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding in Jackson Township in Ocean County. Several roads were reported to be flooded in Jackson. Event precipitation totals included 6.07 inches in Jackson.

Heavy rain fell through the night of the 22nd and caused urban and poor drainage flooding to occur during the early morning of the 23rd. The Admiral Wilson Boulevard in Camden was closed due to flooding with vehicles reported to be stuck in high waters. Route 130 in Pennsauken near Browning Road was closed due to significant flooding. Event precipitation totals included 1.97 inches in Merchantville.

Heavy rain fell through the night of the 22nd and caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding to occur during the early morning of the 23rd. Wyomissing Creek was quickly out of its banks. Flooding was reported at the Cambridge Commons Apartments Complex, with water reported in the maintenance building. Flooding was also reported on Pennsylvania State Route 12 approaching Reading. Event precipitation totals included 6.70 inches in Kutztown, 4.75 inches in Boyertown, 4.21 inches in Bernville, 2.29 inches in Fleetwood and 2.23 inches in Oley.

Heavy rain fell through the night of the 22nd and caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding to occur during the early morning of the 23rd. Several roads were reported to be flooded across Chester County. Event precipitation totals included 1.58 inches in West Grove.

Heavy rain fell through the night of the 22nd and caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding to occur during the early morning of the 23rd. Several roads reported flooding through the Mount Holly/Westampton/Mount Laurel area. In Mount Holly, two homes were damaged by flooding on Cherry Street as the Buttonwood Run flooded. Part of the foundation of one home was washed away and was uninhabitable.  The other home was severely damaged, but was unoccupied.  The intersection of Rancocas Road and the Mount Holly By-Pass (County Route 541) was flooded and closed. The basement of the First Presbyterian Church also flooded. In Mount Laurel, flash flooding along Parkers Creek shut down Hartford and Union Mill Rods. Event precipitation totals included 6.71 inches in Eastampton, 6.25 inches at the Mount Holly WFO, 4.00 inches in Florence, 3.43 inches in Hainesport and 3.36 inches in Mount Laurel.

Heavy rain fell through the night of the 22nd and caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding to occur during the early morning of the 23rd. Several roads around Schwenksville were reported to be flooded out. Cars were submerged within flood waters in Pottstown. No serious injuries were reported. Event precipitation totals included 3.32 inches in Gilbertsville, 2.90 inches in Blue Bell, 2.69 inches in North Wales, 2.57 inches in Kulpsville, 2.37 inches in Hatfield and 2.33 inches in Pottstown.

Heavy rain fell through the night of the 22nd and caused urban and poor drainage flash flooding to occur during the early morning of the 23rd. Water estimated to be a foot deep was reported on Hessian Avenue in West Deptford Township.

Slow moving showers and thunderstorms caused heavy rain to fall across western Monmouth County during the late afternoon and early evening on the 13th. Street flooding was reported in Freehold. Event totals included 1.56 inches in Freehold. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 1 to 2 inches in the western part of the county.

Slow moving showers and thunderstorms caused heavy rain to fall across extreme northwest Burlington County during the evening. Roadway flooding was reported in Florence and Roebling. Event totals included 1.65 inches in Florence Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 1 to 2 inches in the northwestern part of the county.

Slow moving showers and thunderstorms caused heavy rain to fall across the southern half of Mercer County. Roadway flooding was reported in and around Hamilton Township.  Event totals included 1.95 inches in Hamilton Township and 1.60 inches in Lawrence Township. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 1.5 to 2.5 inches in the southern part of the county.
Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused street and poor drainage flooding in North Wales. A CoCoRahs observer measured 0.97 inches of rain within a half hour and have an event total of 0.99 inches.

Showers and thunderstorms with heavy rain caused street and poor drainage flooding across extreme southern Bucks County. Street and poor drainage flooding were reported in both Morrisville and Bensalem.  Event precipitation totals included 1.60 inches in Bensalem and 1.08 inches in Penndel. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 1.5 to 2.5 inches across the extreme southern tier of Bucks County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down power transmission lines along the Morris-Essex New Jersey Commuter Transit Line.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Raritan Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Franklin Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Branchburg Township.
Lightning from early morning thunderstorms struck a house in Island Heights, Ocean County at 505 a.m. EDT on the 23rd.

Lightning from early morning thunderstorms struck a residential building along the 800 block of Blooming Glen Road in Hilltown Township at 215 a.m. EDT on the 23rd.  The lightning strike started a fire on the third floor and the roof.  All residents of the building escaped without injury.  The residents were expected to be displaced for about two to five months due to the damaged roof and third floor.
The combination of gusty thunderstorm winds and heavy rain brought down several trees along Red Bank Avenue in West Deptford Township at 145 a.m. EDT on the 23rd.
The combination of gusty thunderstorm winds and heavy rain brought down a few trees in West Goshen Township at 121 a.m. EDT on the 23rd.
The combination of gusty thunderstorm winds and heavy rain brought down a few trees in West Chester Township and caused some damage to yards and patio furniture around 120 a.m. EDT on the 23rd.
A gust front ahead of a line of strong thunderstorms knocked down a tree in Ridley Park, Delaware County at 7:39 p.m. EDT on the evening of the 7th.

A gust front and a line of strong thunderstorms knocked down several trees and caused numerous power outages in Abington, Glenside, and nearby areas at 7:47 p.m. EDT on the evening of the 7th.  PECO reported approximately 4,500 customers without power, with 4,463 of those outages being reported in Abington and Glenside.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and power lines in Wharton.
A severe thunderstorm dropped golfball size hail in Mine Hill Township, Morris County at 8:12 p.m. EDT on the 7th, resulting in cracked vehicle windshields and damaged porch furniture.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and power lines in Roxbury Township, Morris County at 8:06 p.m. EDT on the 7th.

Heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding in West Windsor Township. Several roads were flooded including the right lane flooding closure of County Route 571 within the township. Event precipitation totals included 1.82 inches in Lawrence Township and 1.72 inches in Ewing Township.

Flooding along the Big Elk Creek caused the closure of Delaware Avenue (Maryland State Route 7) into the 13th. While the flooding was over on the 13th, debris had to be cleared from the roadway. Event precipitation totals included 1.91 inches in Elkton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees across northern New Castle County. About 500 Delmarva Power homes and businesses lost power.
A severe thunderstorm dropped quarter size hail in Barnegat.

events.cz_name: MANASQUAN INLET TO LITTLE EGG INLET NJ OUT 20NM
events.event_narrative: A strong thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 45 knots (52 mph) at Barnegat Inlet.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Still Pond.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire caused minor damage and no personal injuries to a house on Brown Street.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in New Castle County north of the Chesapeake and Delaware Canal between Glasgow and Saint Georges. Several hundred Delmarva Power and Light customers lost power.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down dozens of large tree limbs and trees in and around the Honeybrook Golf Club and the Tel Hai development in Honey Brook.
Preceding the tornado touch down, the same parent thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in Glasgow.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees along U.S. Route 1 (Kennett-Oxford Bypass) near Oxford and blocked a couple of lanes on the roadway.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down or snapped several trees along Stateline Road in Bethel Township. Some of the trees were over 100 years old. One downed tree damaged a home on the road, but no injuries were reported.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees along and around Spring Valley Road in Glen Mills.  One woman had to be rescued from her minivan, when trees and wires were knocked down around her vehicle. Small hail also occurred during the severe thunderstorm.
A lightning strike and ensuing electrical surge started a couple of small basement fires in a home on Half Mile Post in Bethel Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding in southern Chester County. Event precipitation totals included 3.15 inches in West Grove, 2.86 inches in Landenburg, 2.55 inches in Nottingham and 2.36 inches in Unionville.

Runoff from the heavy rain caused flooding along the Saint Jones River twice on the 12th and 13th. The Saint Jones River in Dover was above its 6 foot flood stage from 542 p.m. EDT through 730 p.m. EDT on the 12th and again from 1254 a.m. EDT through 637 p.m. EDT on the 13th. Its highest crest was 6.80 feet at 715 a.m. EDT on the 13th.

An EF0 tornado touched down in Manahawkin (Stafford Township) on the morning of the 13th.  The estimated maximum wind speed was 85 mph and the maximum path width was 100 yards. The estimated path length was 3.2 miles. There were no reported injuries or fatalities and damage was estimated at $250,000.  The tornado initially touched down in the Cedar Run section near the intersection of U.S. Route 9 and Oak Avenue. The tornado lifted while it was moving through the Manahawkin Wildlife Management area. Numerous trees were blown down or snapped along the path of this tornado as were utility poles. There was roof and second floor wind damage to the Lighthouse Christian Academy and also the Manahawkin Baptist Church off of Hilliard Boulevard. One downed tree damaged a home, a trailer was flipped and wind damage occurred to the Moose Lodge off of New Jersey State Route 72. The worst reported wind damage occurred around Oak Avenue, East Bay Avenue and Hilliard Boulevard.  U.S. Route 9, New Jersey State Route 72, Hilliard Boulevard, Beach Avenue, Stafford Avenue and Parker Street were all closed.

A severe thunderstorm that moved through Newark sheared the bricks off of one building and also damaged shutters and windows at the Studio Green Apartments. Trees and power lines were also knocked down along Elkton Road.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Bear.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and power lines between North East and Elkton. Nearly three dozen trees were knocked down along Nottingham Road west of Elkton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in Schuylkill Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees along New Jersey State Route 45 in Mannington Township.
A Skywarn Spotter estimated wind gusts of 60 to 65 mph as a severe thunderstorm moved through Glassboro.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Franklin Township. Tree wind damage was concentrated along County Route 538 from Coles Mill to White Hall Road.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires in Clayton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires in Monroe Township. Approximately 7,600 homes and businesses lost power in Gloucester County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Hammonton.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires in Shamong Township with the wind damage centered around Indian Mills Road. A few homes were damaged by downed trees and a roof was blown off a barn.  One downed tree crashed through the bedroom roof of one home. Indian Mills Road remained closed for most of the day. No serious injuries were reported.

events.cz_name: MANASQUAN INLET TO LITTLE EGG INLET NJ OUT 20NM
events.event_narrative: A strong thunderstorm produced a wind gust to 34 knots (39 mph) at Barnegat Light.

Flash flooding in Cecil County closed Maryland State Route 222 near Maryland State Route 276 in Port Deposit and Maryland State Route 7 east of Ambleside Drive near Elkton. Flooding debris blocked lanes on U.S. Route 40 and on Elk Neck Road. Event precipitation totals included 3.04 inches in Childs, 2.50 inches in Fair Hill and 2.00 inches in Elkton.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused, creek, river as well as urban and poor drainage flash flooding in the northern half of New Castle County that started during the morning of the 13th. Hardest hit were Newark and New Castle. Delaware State Route 7 was covered with several feet of water in Pike Creek (Mill Creek Hundred) and also flooded in Newark. Flooding was also reported along South Chapel Street and Lovett Avenue in Newark, along Harmony Road east of Newark as well as on Delaware State Routes 72 and 896.  In New Castle, firefighters rescued stranded motorists on U.S. Route 13. Delaware State Route 273 and Ferry Cutoff Road were also flooded. U.S. Route 13 flooded in a couple of other locations including within Wilmington. Delaware State Route 141 flooded in Newport. The Nonsuch Creek flooded Airport Road near the New Castle County Airport. Flooding also occurred along the Christina River and White Clay Creek. The Christina River at Coochs Bridge flooded on the 13th, but the gage failed to report during the entire event. The river went below flood stage at 259 p.m. EDT on the 13th. The highest reported reading (at moderate flooding levels) was 12.15 feet at 130 p.m. EDT, but the actual crest may have been higher. The White Clay Creek east of Newark was above its 13 foot flood stage from 812 a.m. EDT through 1055 a.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 14.82 feet at 915 a.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 3.29 inches in Wilmington, 3.26 inches in Newport, 3.12 inches at Newark and 3.10 inches at the New Castle County Airport.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding of roadways and smaller streams in the southeastern part of Berks County.  Event precipitation totals included 2.82 inches in Reading, 2.66 inches in Wyomissing, 2.39 inches in Mohnton, 2.28 inches in Wernersville and 2.27 inches in Sinking Spring.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage and smaller creek flash flooding in Chester County and then led to flooding along the east branch and the main stem of the Brandywine Creek that lasted into the night of the 13th. The heaviest precipitation for this event fell in Chester County.  About 30 vehicles became stuck in flood waters and five water rescues were performed. A mudslide occurred on the Pennsylvania Turnpike near mile marker 318 near Chester Springs. The Valley Creek at Valley Forge had major flooding and was above its 7 foot flood stage from 705 a.m. EDT through 214 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 12.82 feet at 945 a.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 6.53 inches in Coatesville, 4.24 inches in Chesterbrook, 4.15 inches in Downingtown, 3.73 inches in Tredyfrrin, 3.14 inches in Unionville and 2.65 inches in West Chester.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage and creek flash flooding, particularly in the northern half of Delaware County. The Blue Route (Interstate 476) was flooded. The runoff from the heavy rain also led to flooding along the main stem of the Brandywine Creek.  The Crum Creek at Newtown Square had moderate flooding and was above its 6 foot flood stage from 906 a.m. EDT through 158 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 9.40 feet at 1115 a.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 3.10 inches in Wayne, 2.50 inches in Newtown Square and 1.72 inches in Aston.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding, particularly in the lower half of Montgomery County. Emergency personnel responded to around 30 calls for assistance from motorists trapped in their flooded vehicles. In Norristown, four roadways (including Trooper Road and Van Buren Avenue) and underpasses were flooded and closed. A construction barge broke free on Stony Creek at two workers were rescued. in Hatboro, flooding along the Pennypack Creek reached into the parking lot of the Robert Bruce Apartments. Gulph Road was flooded in King of Prussia. The Wissahickon Creek at Fort Washington had major flooding and was above its 9 foot flood stage from 830 a..m. EDT through 313 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 12.35 feet at 1230 p.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 3.98 inches in West Norriton, 3.81 inches in Blue Bell, 3.56 inches in Fort Washington and 3.48 inches in North Wales.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding in western Bucks County.  Vehicle rescues were performed in Southampton. The Little Neshaminy Creek at Neshaminy was above its 8 foot flood stage from 1029 a.m. EDT through 153 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 8.98 feet at Noon EDT. Event precipitation totals included 2.86 inches in Penndel, 2.17 inches in Warrington and 1.94 inches in Quakertown.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding of many roadways and streams in Salem County on the morning of the 13th.  Many roadways were closed and these included Broadway in Salem City and U.S. Route 40 in Pilesgrove and Pennsville Townships. A motorist was rescued from the U.S. Route 40 extension in Pennsville. Pittsgrove Township expected runoff problems to affect the municipality into the 14th.  Event precipitation totals included 3.75 inches in Upper Pittsgrove and 3.17 inches in Woodstown.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding of numerous roadways and creeks, especially in central and western Gloucester County.  Vehicles became trapped in flood waters and rescues were performed. Roadway closures included New Jersey State Route 55 and Delsea Drive in Deptford, Kings Highway in Woodbury, New Jersey State Route 44 in Paulsboro, Kings Highway in West Deptford, Main Street in Glassboro and New Jersey State Route 42 in Monroe Township. The Mantua Creek at Pitman was above its 5 foot flood stage from 1050 a..m. EDT through 338 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 5.80 feet at 1215 p.m. EDT.  The Raccoon Creek also flooded and crested at 14.69 feet at 2 p.m. EDT on the 13th. Event precipitation totals included 4.50 inches in Washington Township, 4.28 inches in Monroe Township, 4.14 inches in Clayton, 3.80 inches in Glassboro and 3.19 inches in Pitman.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding of numerous roadways and creeks, especially in central and western Camden County. Many vehicles became trapped in flood waters. Flooding also occurred along the Cooper River. Flooding forced the closure of Interstate 76 in Gloucester City, New Jersey State Route 42 near Interstate 295 and New Jersey State Route 70 in Cherry Hill. In Lindenwold, one vehicle was totally submerged in flood waters on the South White Horse Pike. Event precipitation totals included 4.68 inches in Winslow Township, 3.80 inches in Berlin Township, 2.94 inches in Lindenwold and 2.01 inches in Camden.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding of roadways and creeks, especially across the central third of Burlington County. In Evesham Township, a school bus became stuck in flood waters on Erindale Drive. Thirty-one children were rescued. Also within the township, a motorist was rescued from flood waters on New Jersey State Route 70 near Cropwell Road. Flooded and closed roadways also included Marlton Parkway in Evesham and Hartford Road in Medford. The flooding also affected the primary election as voting booths had to be moved after flooding occurred at some polling places. Event precipitation totals included 2.64 inches in Medford Township, 2.53 inches in Southampton Township, 2.35 inches in Pemberton Township and 2.30 inches in Tabernacle Township.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding of roadways and creeks, especially in the eastern half of Monmouth County.  Sections of New Jersey State Routes 35 and 71 were flooded and closed.  Roadway closures occurred in Ocean Township, Long Branch, Manasquan, Deal, Wall and Neptune. Several dozen vehicles became struck in flood waters. In Long Branch, a mother and her nine-month-old son were rescued from a vehicle on Long Branch Avenue. Three other roadways were flooded. In Ocean Township, secondary roadways took a big flooding hit. In Manasquan, basement flooding occurred along Marcellus Avenue. Event precipitation totals included 4.11 inches in Ocean Township, 2.85 inches in Fair Haven, 2.68 inches in Red Bank, 2.57 inches in Rumson and 2.16 inches in Long Branch.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding on Long Beach Island from Surf City south through Beach Haven. Some poor drainage flooding also occurred in Point Pleasant and Little Egg Harbor Township. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 2 to 3 inches.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding of small streams, fields as well as poor drainage flooding in southeastern Sussex County. Event precipitation totals included 4.13 inches in Bethany Beach, 3.80 inches in Selbyville and 3.50 inches in Gumboro.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding of small streams and fields as well as poor drainage flooding in and around Ellendale in central Sussex County. Event precipitation totals included 4.24 inches in Ellendale and 2.82 inches in Redden.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires near Burrisville. Delmarva Power and Light reported around 250 homes lost power.

Heavy rain caused some poor drainage flooding along Montgomery Avenue in West Chester. One vehicle became disabled in the flood waters.  Event precipitation totals in West Chester were 1.86 inches and 1.35 inches respectively. No serious injuries were reported.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage as well as small stream flash flooding in the western part of Sussex County. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 2.5 inches from Stillwater and Walpack Townships northeastward through Montague and Wantage Townships. Storm total estimates exceeded 5 inches in Sandyston Township. The Papakating Creek at Pellettown started exceeding its 4 foot flood stage at 737 a.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 4.81 inches at High Point, 4.09 inches in Montague, 2.85 inches in Wantage and 2.66 inches in Flatbrookville.

The runoff from the heavy rain during the morning of the 9th caused flooding on the Papakating Creek that lasted into the 10th. The Papakating Creek at Pellettown (Frankford Township) was above its 4 foot flood stage from 737 a.m. EDT on the 9th through 700 a.m. EDT on the 10th. It crested at 5.10 feet at 1015 p.m. EDT on the 9th.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage as well as small stream flash flooding in Monroe County. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 3.5 and 6.0 inches in an axis from Chestnuthill and Tunkhannock Townships northeastward through Price and Middle Smithfield Townships. Measured event precipitation totals included 3.29 inches in Stroudsburg, 3.02 inches in Reeders, 2.57 inches in McMichaels and 2.52 inches in East Stroudsburg.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours, over 2 inches fell within an hour, caused flash flooding of smaller creeks as well as field and poor drainage flooding in and to the south of Georgetown in central Sussex County. Event precipitation totals included 2.53 inches in Georgetown and 2.48 inches in Stockley.

The second straight day of thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused roadway and small creek flash flooding in Allentown and Whitehall Township. Numerous roadways were flooded with some water rescues from trapped vehicles. A child nearly was swept away in the flood waters before being rescued by an adult. Manhole covers popped. About 43 vehicles were badly damaged in the flooding in the West End of Allentown and several businesses were flooded. Flood damage in the area also occurred to homes, garages and basements. No serious injuries were reported. About 2200 people were sheltered in place at the Allentown Fair off of Liberty Street in the city because the entrances and exits to the fairground were flooded. The Zac Brown Band had to cut their concert short. Fair goers were able to leave later that evening.  Damage to the fair was limited to grass and gravel erosion. Elsewhere in the city, vehicles were trapped in flood waters on Sumner Avenue, 22nd and Allen Street, 13th and Liberty Street and 18th and Tilghman Street. About ten homes around 22nd and Allen Street had water in their basements and the electricity was turned off for precautionary reasons.  Event precipitation totals included 1.26 inches at the Lehigh Valley International Airport.

The runoff from the heavy rain and wet antecedent conditions caused minor flooding along the Christina River. The Christina River at Coochs Bridge was above its 10.5 foot flood stage from 1204 p.m. EDT through 303 p.m. EDT on the 1st. It crested at 11.34 feet at 115 p.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 1.90 inches in Newport, 1.31 inches in Newark, 1.17 inches at the New Castle County Airport and 1.03 inches in Hockessin.

The Frankford Creek at Castor Avenue was briefly above its 7 foot flood stage from 1245 p.m. EDT through 101 p.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 7.19 feet. Event precipitation totals included 1.80 inches in Wyndmoor and 1.04 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport.
Lightning struck a home on Springtown Road in Long Valley (Washington Township). No serious injuries were reported.
Lightning struck a home on Jane Terrace in Mendham Township. No serious injuries were reported.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees in East Greenwich Township along Cohawkin Road. One property owner lost eight trees. A gazebo was tossed and yard furniture was displaced by 50 yards. One downed tree rolled off the roof of one home. About 5,000 homes and businesses in Gloucester County lost power.

Heavy rain that coincided with the morning commute in Burlington County caused poor drainage flooding along Interstate 295 between Bordentown and Interstate 195. This caused traffic to back up for nearly ten miles. U.S. Route 130 was closed in Florence Township. Event precipitation totals included 2.00 inches in Bordentown and 1.75 inches in Florence Township.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding of roadways and streams in northwestern Somerset County and hit Bedminister, Peapack-Gladstone and Bernardsville the hardest. The flash flooding affected New Jersey Commuter Rail Service. Eastbound commuter rail service along the Morris and Essex Line was suspended for the day after flash flooding caused four to six washouts of stone supports along the Gladstone Branch tracks. Westbound service continued, but delays averaged 45 minutes.  Substitute eastbound bus service was provided. About ten people in Peapack-Gladstone self evacuated to the Municipal Building. The runoff from the heavy rain and also caused flooding along the Lamington River and Middle Brook.  Event precipitation totals included 5.85 inches in Peapack-Gladstone, 5.14 inches in Pottersville, 4.94 inches in Far Hills and 3.99 inches in Middlebush.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding of roadways and smaller streams in southern Morris County in Chester, Mendham and Washington Townships.  Event precipitation totals included 2.00 inches in New Vernon, 1.76 inches in Washington Township,  1.59 inches in Chester Township and 1.53 inches in Mendham Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding of roadways and smaller streams in northeastern Hunterdon County and affected Clinton, Tewksbury and Readington Townships the hardest.  In Tewksbury Township, a car became trapped in five feet of flood waters from the Lamington (Black) River on McCan Mill Road near the bridge at Black River Road. A front end loader was used to rescue the female driver. A vehicle was also stuck in flood waters on Rockaway Road. Flooding and road closures also occurred along U.S. Route 22 in Readington and Clinton Townships. Event precipitation totals included 3.15 inches in Lebanon Township, 3.06 inches in Califon and 1.62 inches in Clinton and Readington Townships.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding of roadways and smaller streams mainly in the northwestern and central sections of Mercer County.  The afternoon thunderstorms were most concentrated in Hopewell and Lawrence Townships. Roadway and creek flooding were reported in Hamilton, Princeton and Lawrence Townships.  Event precipitation totals included 2.62 inches in Hamilton Township, 2.23 inches in Pennington, 2.11 inches in Lawrence, 2.05 inches in Hopewell and 1.80 inches in Trenton.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding of roadways and smaller streams again in Somerset County, this time in the southern part of the county. The heaviest rain from this cluster of thunderstorms fell in Hillsborough and Franklin Townships.  In Hillsborough Township, U.S. Route 206 and Brooks Boulevard were flooded and closed. In Franklin Township, How Lane and New Jersey State Route 27 were flooded and closed. Event precipitation totals included 3.52 inches in Hillsborough, 3.50 inches in Manville, 2.90 inches in Franklin and 1.88 inches in Montgomery Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding of roadways and smaller streams in central and northern Middlesex County affecting North Brunswick and East Brunswick the hardest. In East Brunswick, numerous roadways were flooded (including New Jersey State Routes 18 and 27) and traffic was described as at a standstill. In New Brunswick, the basement of the Middlesex County Family Court was flooded and Family Court was closed for the rest of the day.  Joyce Kilmer Avenue, George Street, Johnson Drive and Livingston Avenue were all flooded. Buccleuch Park was closed. In Edison, New Jersey State Route 27 was flooded. Street flooding was also reported in Woodbridge. Event precipitation totals included 2.00 inches in Cranbury and 1.90 inches in New Brunswick.

The runoff from the heavy rain earlier in the day caused flooding to persist along sections of the Middle Brook, the Lamington River and the North Branch of the Raritan River.  The Lamington River at Burnt Mills was above its 9.5 foot flood stage from 147 p.m. EDT through 815 p.m. EDT on the 22nd. It crested at 12.00 feet at 5 p.m. EDT. It was its highest crest since 12.1 feet on April 15, 2007.  The Middle Brook at Burnt Mills was above its 8 foot flood stage from 1131 a.m. EDT through 428 p.m. EDT on the 22nd. It crested at 9.75 feet at 115 p.m. EDT.  The North Branch of the Raritan River at North Branch was above its 12.3 foot flood stage from 519 p.m. EDT through 933 p.m. EDT on the 22nd. It crested at 13.51 feet at 730 p.m. EDT.  Farther downstream, the North Branch of the Raritan River at the village of South Branch was above its 7 foot flood stage from 937 p.m. EDT through 1055 p.m. EDT on the 22nd. It crested at 7.07 feet at 1045 p.m. EDT.   Event precipitation totals included 5.85 inches in Peapack-Gladstone, 5.14 inches in Pottersville, 4.94 inches in Far Hills, 3.99 inches in Middlebush, 3.52 inches in Hillsborough, 3.50 inches in Manville, 3.02 inches in Bridgewater, 2.90 inches in Franklin and 1.88 inches in Montgomery Township.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage flash flooding as well as creek flooding within Philadelphia.  Flooding occurred along the Frankford, Pennypack and Wissahickon Creeks. A teenager was rescued from the Pennypack Creek in the Holmesburg section of the city. Extensive flooding snarled traffic along the Schuylkill Expressway. Lincoln Drive along the Wissahickon Creek was flooded in both directions and closed.  The Wissahickon Environmental Center Camp was cancelled because of flooding. The Frankford Creek at Castor Avenue had moderate flooding and was above its 7 foot flood stage twice from 820 a.m. EDT through 1011 a.m. EDT on the 13th. Its highest crest was 8.85 feet at 830 a.m. EDT. The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge crested at 8.87 feet at 345 p.m. EDT.  The Wissahickon Creek at its mouth crested at 7.23 feet at 415 p.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 2.20 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport and 1.93 inches in Northeast Philadelphia.

The runoff from the heavy rain that fell on the 13th led to minor flooding along the Great Egg River. The Great Egg River at Folsom was above its 6 foot flood stage from 1207 p.m. EDT through 1145 p.m. EDT on the 15th. It crested at 6.09 feet at 445 p.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 2.86 inches in Hammonton.

Runoff from the heavy rain on the morning of the 13th caused flooding along the Cooper River to persist into the early evening. The Cooper River at Haddonfield was above its 2.8 foot flood stage from 1103 a.m. EDT through 645 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 3.39 feet at 215 p.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 4.68 inches in Winslow Township, 3.80 inches in Berlin Township, 2.94 inches in Lindenwold and 2.01 inches in Camden.

The runoff from the heavy rain that fell during the morning of the 13th caused the Raccoon Creek to flood into the night of the 13th. The Raccoon Creek at Swedesboro was above its 13 foot flood stage from 1136 a..m. EDT on the 13th through 1238 a.m. EDT on the 14th. It crested at 14.69 feet at 2 p.m. EDT on the 13th. Flooding also continued along the Mantua Creek into the afternoon of the 13th. The Mantua Creek at Pitman was above its 5 foot flood stage from 1050 a..m. EDT through 338 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 5.80 feet at 1215 p.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 4.50 inches in Washington Township, 4.28 inches in Monroe Township, 4.14 inches in Clayton, 3.80 inches in Glassboro and 3.19 inches in Pitman.

The runoff from the morning heavy rain on the 13th continued flooding along some of the waterways in Philadelphia into the evening of the 13th. This was especially true of creeks whose sources are in Montgomery County as heavier rain fell in their headwater regions. The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge was above its 7 foot flood stage from 848 a.m. EDT through 511 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 8.87 feet at 345 p.m. EDT. The Wissahickon Creek at its mouth within Philadelphia had moderate flooding and was above its 5 foot flood stage from 956 a.m. EDT through 801 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 7.23 feet at 415 p.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 2.20 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport and 1.93 inches in Northeast Philadelphia.

The runoff from the morning heavy rain on the 13th continued flooding along the Brandywine Creek into the night of the 13th. Heavier rain fell in Chester County.  The Brandywine Creek at Chadds Ford had moderate flooding and was above its 9 foot flood stage from 2 p.m. EDT on the 13th through 237 a.m. EDT on the 14th. It crested at 11.72 feet at 815 p.m. EDT on the 13th. Event precipitation totals included 3.10 inches in Wayne, 2.50 inches in Newtown Square and 1.72 inches in Aston.

The runoff from the morning heavy rain on the 13th continued flooding along some of the creeks in eastern Chester County into the afternoon and night, especially in the Brandywine Basin. The East Branch of the Brandywine Creek below Downingtown had moderate flooding and was above its 7 foot flood stage from 725 a.m. EDT through 413 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 10.78 feet at 1045 a.m. EDT.  The main stem of the Brandywine Creek at Chadds Ford also had moderate flooding and was above its 9 foot flood stage from 2 p.m. EDT on the 13th through 237 a.m. EDT on the 14th. It crested at 11.72 feet at 815 p.m. EDT on the 13th.  The Valley Creek at Valley Forge had major flooding and was above its 7 foot flood stage from 705 a.m. EDT through 214 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 12.82 feet at 945 a.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 6.53 inches in Coatesville, 4.24 inches in Chesterbrook, 4.15 inches in Downingtown, 3.73 inches in Tredyfrrin, 3.14 inches in Unionville and 2.65 inches in West Chester.

A severe thunderstorm in Jefferson Township tossed a utility shed upside down on a property on School House Road as well as knocked down a tree across the roadway. The severe thunderstorm also knocked down about four trees on a property on Ridge Road and knocked down another tree and overturned another utility shed on another property in the area. No serious injuries were reported.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in and around Radnor Township in northern Delaware County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in and around Warminster Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in and around 10th and Pine Street in Philadelphia.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees along U.S. Route 40 in Glasgow. The westbound lanes of the roadway were closed at LaGrange Avenue and large trees were knocked down in Glasgow Park.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous large tree limbs, trees and wires in Salem County. About 3,300 homes and businesses lost power.
A lightning strike struck the 911 center in Mannington Township and damaged some equipment.
A lightning strike at the Borough Hall in Manasquan caused damage and disrupted the communication systems in the borough. They were transferred to other facilities.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller creeks as well as roadway flooding in upper Bucks County in and around Quakertown. Flooding was reported along Pennsylvania State Route 309. Event precipitation totals included 1.60 inches in Quakertown.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller creeks as well as poor drainage and roadway flooding from Allentown southward in Lehigh County. The heavy rain fell so quickly that manhole covers were popping. Roadway flooding, stranded vehicles and water rescues in Allentown were reported on Mack Boulevard, Basin and Auburn Streets, Elmo Street, Mohawk Street and South 4th, 8th and 12th Streets.  Farther to the south, Pennsylvania State Route 309 was flooded and closed in Upper Saucon Township. Event precipitation totals included 2.91 inches at the Lehigh Valley International Airport and 1.64 inches in Orefield.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller creeks as well as poor drainage and roadway flooding in Bethlehem. Flash flooding isolated forty homes around Pennsylvania State Route 412 in the city. Event precipitation totals included 2.91 inches at the Lehigh Valley International Airport.
Lightning struck a home on Schweitzer Place in North Brunswick. No serious injuries were reported.
A lightning strike damaged the communication center of the Sayreville Police department. Phone and radio communication lines were damaged.

A thunderstorm produced a funnel cloud that was seen by several eyewitnesses over a corn field near Railway Road and Delaware State Route 26 in Millville.  While eyewitness accounts stated that the funnel came close to the ground, no damage was reported.

A severe thunderstorm produced damaging wind gusts in western New Castle County along with some small hail (around half an inch in diameter). In Hockessin, large tree limbs were knocked down along Brackenville Road. In Lindell, several large trees were knocked down along the Mill Creek from Limestone Road south to Kirkwood Highway. While the thunderstorm weakened as it moved into eastern New Castle County, it still produced some pea size hail and a wind gust to 45 mph at the New Castle County Airport.
Lightning strikes damaged three homes in Forks Township. The damage was from the lightning strikes themselves as there were no ensuing fires reported.  No serious injuries were also reported.
Lightning struck a home and caused a fire in the Frankford section of Philadelphia. No serious injuries were reported.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down five trees in central Philadelphia.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees and large tree limbs along County Route 541 in lower Medford Township.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding in eastern and southeastern parts of Philadelphia. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 1 to 2 inches within the city.  Event precipitation totals included 1.89 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding across central Delaware County with Springfield and Upper Darby Townships affected the hardest.  In Springfield Township, flash flooding along the Stony Creek backed into storm drains in the parking lot of BJ's Wholesalers on Woodland Avenue. The water reached up to five feet high and completely submerged some vehicles. About twenty water rescues were performed as fifty vehicles were affected in the parking lot.  Seven fire companies responded to the flooding. Specialized rescue boat water units were used to rescue people from their vehicles. Numerous roadways were flooded in the township and neighboring Upper Darby Township. One vehicle was swept into a flooded creek. The intersections of Normandy and Marshall Roads, Copley and Marshall Roads and Lansdowne Avenue and State Road were all flooded and closed for several hours. In Middletown Township, several water rescues occurred in the Lima area.  A Skywarn spotter also reported flooding along Cobbs Creek bordering Philadelphia.   Event precipitation totals included 3.59 inches in Swarthmore, 2.85 inches in Havertown, 2.00 inches in Drexel Hill and 1.89 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport.

A Skywarn spotter reported that thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding along sections of Cobbs Creek bordering Delaware County.  While there are no established flood stages for gages along Cobbs Creek, it crested at 7.67 feet at Noon EDT on the 2nd at Lincoln Highway/City Avenue (U.S. Route 1) and at 13.72 feet at the Mount Moriah Cemetery at 215 p.m. EDT on the 2nd. Event precipitation totals included 1.89 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused creek and poor drainage flash flooding in central Bucks County affecting Bedminster, Plumstead and Tinicum Townships  Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 2 and 4 inches in sections of those townships.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused creek and poor drainage flooding in central Gloucester County, affecting Glassboro Borough and Elk, Harrison and South Harrison Townships the most. In Glassboro,  significant roadway flooding was reported. At Rowan University, several parking lots quickly flooded and roadways leading into and through the university were also flooded. Event precipitation totals included 4.30 inches in Glassboro, 2.78 inches in Malaga, 2.58 inches in Franklin Township and 2.01 inches in Sewell.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused creek and poor drainage flooding in west central Camden County in and around Somerdale Borough and Gloucester Township. In Somerdale, significant street flooding was reported with several vehicles stuck in flood waters.  Event precipitation totals included 4.26 inches in Stratford, 4.10 inches in Clementon, 4.09 inches in Gloucester Township, 4.00 inches in Glendora and 3.50 inches in Blenheim.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused creek and poor drainage flooding in east central Camden County centered in and around Voorhees Township. Flooding along the Millard Creek and Kirkwood Lake reached some properties. Roadway flash flooding also occurred and some vehicles were trapped in flood waters. Event precipitation totals included 4.26 inches in Stratford, 4.10 inches in Clementon, 4.09 inches in Gloucester Township, 4.00 inches in Glendora and 3.50 inches in Blenheim.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused creek and poor drainage flooding in west central Hunterdon County centered in and around Alexandria, Franklin, Holland and Union Townships.  Event precipitation totals included 3.22 inches in Pittstown, 2.58 inches in Franklin Township and 2.38 inches in Spruce Run.
A lightning strike damaged a tree in a housing development in Fork Township.
Lightning struck a home in Bern Township and ignited a fire. No serious injuries were reported.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Tulpehocken Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Oley Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Muhlenberg Township. One downed tree fell onto and damaged a home. An elderly woman was injured and trapped within her house. She had to be extricated and was transported to Reading Hospital. A wind gust to 46 mph occurred at the Reading Regional Airport.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires in Rockland Township. One downed wire started an appliance fire in a home in the township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and caused low hanging wires in Whitehall Township. Pennsylvania Power and Light reported about 500 of its customers lost power in Lehigh County.

A severe thunderstorm generated a wind gust of 61 mph in Bushkill Township and tore down utility poles as well as a large pine tree. The same line of thunderstorms produced a wind gust to 47 mph in Forks Township. Pennsylvania Power and Light reported about 3,500 of its customers lost power in Northampton County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and power lines in Mansfield Township. Some brush fires were started by the downed wires.
A severe thunderstorm produced an estimated wind gust of 60 mph in Chester.
A severe thunderstorm downed several trees in Hope and also caused property damage to one farm. Pea size hail also fell from the thunderstorm.
A severe thunderstorm downed  trees and wires along and around Johnsonburg Road in Allamuchy Township. Some roadways were blocked. A small farm stand was also damaged.
A severe thunderstorm downed  trees and wires along and around Kennedy Road in Green Township. Some roadways were blocked.
A severe thunderstorm knocked over a tree onto a van in Belvidere. No serious injuries were reported.

A severe thunderstorm knocked numerous large tree limbs, wires and several trees in the Shongum Lake area as well as along New Jersey State Route 10 in Randolph Township.  Downed wires also started small fires. Power was not fully restored in the township until later in the day on the 13th.

A severe thunderstorm knocked several trees in Sparta that caused road closures and this included Alpine and South Shore Trails. Siding was also torn off some homes. About 5,000 homes and businesses lost power.
A severe thunderstorm knocked several trees across County Route 517 in Ogdensburg.

A severe thunderstorm knocked a couple of trees in Jefferson Township. A motorcycle rider was injured when a tree fell onto the motorcycle near the intersection of Berkshire Valley and Dover-Milton Roads.
