Repeating thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in western Hunterdon County in Alexandria, Holland and Union Townships. Flash flooding inundated Sweet Hollow Road in Alexandria Township, one of several roads impacted in the township. Several roads were also flooded in Holland Township and included Rummel Road. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached around 3 inches along the heaviest rain axis in the county.

The runoff from the thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flooding along the Raccoon Creek that lasted into the night of the 2nd. The Raccoon Creek near Swedesboro was above its 13 foot flood stage from 347 p.m. EDT on the 2nd through 506 a.m. EDT on the 3rd. It crested at 15.25 feet at 8 p.m. EDT on the 2nd. It was historically the 5th highest crest on record for the creek and the highest crest since August 28, 2011 associated with Tropical Storm Irene. Event precipitation totals included 4.30 inches in Glassboro, 2.78 inches in Malaga, 2.58 inches in Franklin Township and 2.01 inches in Sewell.

The runoff from the thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused minor flooding along the Cooper River the lasted into the night of the 2nd.  The Cooper River at Haddonfield was above its 2.8 foot flood stage from 235 p.m. EDT on the 2nd through 1209 a.m. EDT on the 3rd. It crested at 3.65 feet at 530 p.m. EDT on the 2nd. Event precipitation totals included 4.26 inches in Stratford, 4.10 inches in Clementon, 4.09 inches in Gloucester Township, 4.00 inches in Glendora and 3.50 inches in Blenheim.

The runoff from the heavy rain that fell during the evening of the 21st and overnight caused minor flooding along the Cooper River.  The Cooper River at Haddonfield was above its 2.8 foot flood stage from 234 a.m. EDT through 317 a.m. EDT on the 22nd. It crested at 3.08 feet at 245 a.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 1.95 inches in Stratford, 1.68 inches in Lindenwold, 1.55 inches in Collingswood, 1.50 inches in Mount Ephraim and 1.39 inches in Cherry Hill.
A lightning strike started a small barn fire in Northampton.
A squall line of severe thunderstorms knocked down a few trees in the western part of Berks County centered around Upper Bern Township.
A squall line of severe thunderstorms knocked down a few trees in and around Reading.
A squall line of severe thunderstorms knocked down a few trees in and around Earl Township.
A  squall line of strong to severe thunderstorms knocked down a couple of trees in East Allen Township.
A  squall line of strong to severe thunderstorms knocked down a couple of large tree limbs and wires in Lower Nazareth Township.
A squall line of strong to severe thunderstorms uprooted whole trees in Solebury Township and a couple of downed trees damaged homes. No serious injuries were reported.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 59 mph within the city of Allentown.
A severe thunderstorm snapped the tops off of several trees along Hillcrest Lane in Northeast.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Bernards Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Chatham Borough.

A severe thunderstorm snapped five utility poles along U.S. Route 46 in Parsippany. Downed power lines fell onto parked cars. Nearby workers were escorted out of buildings, away from the downed poles. The roadway was closed to all traffic between Baldwin Road and North Beverwyck Road.

The runoff from the heavy rain that fell early on the 11th caused minor flooding along sections of the East Branch and Main Stem of the Brandywine Creek that persisted into the night of the 11th.  The heavy rain also caused poor drainage flooding. The East Branch of the Brandywine Creek at Downingtown was above its 7 foot flood stage from 843 a.m. EDT through 228 p.m. EDT on the 11th. It crested at 8.87 feet at 1215 p.m. EDT on the 11th. The Main Stem of the Brandywine Creek at Chadds Ford was above its 9 foot flood stage from 138 p.m. EDT on the 11th through 130 a.m. EDT on the 12th. It crested at 9.47 feet at 637 p.m. EDT on the 11th. Event precipitation totals included 4.35 inches in Modena, 4.29 inches in Longwood, 3.76 inches in Northbrook and 3.59 inches in Downingtown.

The runoff from the heavy rain that fell earlier on the 11th caused minor flooding along sections of the Main Stem of the Brandywine Creek that persisted into the night of the 11th. The heavy rain also caused poor drainage flooding. The Main Stem of the Brandywine Creek at Chadds Ford was above its 9 foot flood stage from 138 p.m. EDT on the 11th through 130 a.m. EDT on the 12th. It crested at 9.47 feet at 637 p.m. EDT on the 11th. Event precipitation totals included 3.50 inches in Chadds Ford and 2.03 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport.

The runoff from the heavy rain that fell early on the 11th caused minor flooding along the Red Clay Creek Basin on the morning and afternoon of the 11th. The heavy rain also caused poor drainage flooding in and around Newark and Middletown.  The Red Clay Creek at Wooddale was above its 7 foot flood stage from 832 a.m. EDT through 1023 a.m. EDT on the 11th. It crested at 7.15 feet at 915 a.m. EDT on the 11th. Farther downstream, the Red Clay Creek at Stanton was above its 15 foot flood stage from 916 a.m. EDT through 1239 p.m. EDT on the 11th. It crested at 15.30 feet at 1030 a.m. EDT on the 11th. Event precipitation totals included 2.90 inches in Blackbird, 1.98 inches in Newark and 1.50 inches at the New Castle County Airport.
A line of showers and isolated thunderstorms with damaging winds knocked down numerous trees and wires across Carbon County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and power lines in Bartonsville. The same line of showers and thunderstorms produced a wind gust of 54 mph in Stroudsburg.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Mertztown (Longswamp Township).

A severe thunderstorm knocked down three telephone poles in Fogelsville in Upper Macungie Township. Pennsylvania Power and Light reported about 2,700 of its customers lost power with the greatest concentration of outages in South Whitehall and Upper Macungie Townships.  A wind gust of 53 mph was measured at the nearby Lehigh Valley International Airport.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Pen Argyl. At least one damaged a home.
A line of showers and severe thunderstorms knocked down several trees and wires in southeast Northampton County.

A line of showers and severe thunderstorms also knocked down several trees and wires along the southwest tier of Montgomery County.  PECO Energy reported about 10,000 of its customers lost power in Montgomery County.
A line of showers and severe thunderstorms knocked down several trees and wires along the northeast tier of Montgomery County.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in East Whiteland Township. One fell on and damaged the roof of a home. PECO Energy reported about 1,700 of its customers lost power in Chester County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in and around Oxford.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Pittstown (Franklin Township).
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Bedminster Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in and around Boonton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees and wires in Camden.
A line of severe showers and thunderstorms knocked down several trees and wires in central and eastern Gloucester County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several large tree limbs and wires in Haverford Township.
A convective line knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Newark.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in White Township. Downed trees closed U.S. Route 46 in both directions in the township east of Pequest Furnace Road.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Clinton. Downed wires blocked a southbound lane of New Jersey State Route 31 near Old Clinton Road.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Harding Township.  Downed trees and wires blocked Baileys Mill Road between Lees Hill and Young Roads.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Hamilton Township. Metropolitan Edison reported about 1,300 of its customers lost power in Monroe County. All power was restored by Noon EDT that day.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a transformer along Gerald Avenue in Cumru Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Robeson Township. Wires fell onto the garage of one home on Old River Road. No damage to the garage was reported.  Pennsylvania Power and Light and Metropolitan Edison reported about 2,000 of their customers lost power in Berks County. Power was restored by Noon EDT that day.

The Christina River at Coochs Bridge had moderate flooding and was above its 10.5 foot flood stage from 505 a.m. EST through 936 a.m. EST on the 27th. It crested at 11.54 feet at 715 a.m. EST. Event precipitation totals included 3.12 inches in Newport, 3.01 inches in Hockessin, 3.00 inches in Prices Corner, 2.56 inches in Newark and 2.51 inches at the New Castle County Airport.

The Chester Creek at Chester was above its 8 foot flood stage from 518 a.m. EST through 621 a.m. EST on the 27th. It crested at 8.14 feet at 600 a.m. EST.  Event precipitation totals included 2.50 inches in Upper Chichester Township.

The heavy rain contributed to a fatal accident on the Schuylkill Expressway (Interstate 76) in Philadelphia. About 430 a.m. EST on the 27th, a westbound Audi automobile hit a pool of water and spun out and hit the barrier and stopped. A minivan following stopped in time. But, a tractor-trailer behind it could not stop in time and struck a minivan.  A 47-year-old male passenger was killed and six other people were injured. The westbound lanes of the Schuylkill remained closed between Exit 341 (Montgomery Drive/West River Drive) and Exit 339 (U.S. Route 1 South - City Avenue) due to the accident.  The westbound side of the expressway completely reopened at 3 p.m. EST that afternoon.  On the eastbound side of the Schuylkill Expressway in nearly the same area, poor drainage flooding closed the expressway between Exit 340B (U.S. Route 1 North - Roosevelt Boulevard) and Exit 341 (Montgomery Drive/West River Drive). Cleanup included removing debris from the roadway. Three of the four lanes were reopened that afternoon.  Additional flooding forced the closure of Interstate 76 within Philadelphia at the 26th Street Tunnel after a cab became stuck in flood waters. The rain also contributed to accidents along Interstate 95 and the Pennsylvania Turnpike. | |The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge was above its 7 foot flood stage from 543 a.m. EST through 1032 a.m. EST on the 27th. It crested at 7.52 feet at 715 a.m. EST. Event precipitation totals included 2.32 inches at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport and 2.28 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport.

The Christina River at Coochs Bridge was above its 10.5 foot flood stage from 510 p.m. EST through 750 p.m. EST on the 29th. It crested at 11.03 feet at 645 p.m. EST. Event precipitation totals included 1.37 inches at the New Castle County Airport, 1.32 inches in Newark, 1.25 inches in Prices Corner and 1.20 inches in Odessa.

The unseasonably cold arctic air mass resulted in ice jam flooding north of the jam in Trenton on January 8th and 9th. The ice jam started to form near the U.S. Route 1 Bridge on the night of the 7th and extended for one mile north of it. Flooding began on the 8th. The ice jam rose water levels on the Delaware River for three miles behind the jam. In Trenton,  flooding of parking areas north of the Trenton-Morrisville Bridge included the lower level of the Capitol Complex's garage.  Both Market Street and Memorial Drive off of New Jersey State Route 29 in Trenton were also closed because of flooding.  Southbound New Jersey State Route 29 was also closed in Trenton. The flooding caused a dual problem because of the low temperatures. As roadways flooded, they also became icy. Residents in the Glen Afton and Island sections of Trenton were alerted about possible flooding. Some voluntary evacuations occurred. Islands in the middle of the Delaware River were completely submerged. The Delaware River in Trenton was sporadically above its 20 foot flood stage from 550 p.m. EST on the 8th through 800 a.m. EST on the 9th. It crested at 20.76 feet at 730 p.m. EST on the 8th.

The unseasonably cold arctic air mass resulted in ice jam flooding along the Delaware River north of the jam in Bucks County on January 8th and 9th. The ice jam started to form near the U.S. Route 1 Bridge on the night of the 7th and flooding began on the 8th. The flooding caused the closure of River Road (State Route 32) from Black Rock Road in Lower Makefield Township south through to East Trenton Avenue/Calhoun Street Bridge in Morrisville Borough. The road was re-opened at Noon EST on January 9th. The flooding caused a dual problem because of the low temperatures. As roadways flooded, they also became icy. Islands in the middle of the Delaware River were completely submerged. The Delaware River in Trenton was above its 20 foot flood stage at times from 550 p.m. EST on the 8th through 800 a.m. EST on the 9th. It crested at 20.76 feet at 730 p.m. EST on the 8th.

An ice jam along the Lehigh River caused flooding along Lehigh Drive (State Route 2026) from the Old Glendon Bridge to its confluence with the Delaware River. In West Easton Borough from the afternoon of the 8th into the morning of the 9th. A vehicle became stuck in four feet of icy water on Lehigh Drive after driving around a barricade. Temperatures that rose above freezing on the 9th and 10th helped ease the ice jam.

The combination of snow melt and heavy rain caused flooding along The Bushkill Creek  in Bushkill Township. The creek flooded West Douglassville and Clearfield Roads. Event precipitation totals included 1.51 inches at the Lehigh Valley International Airport and 1.27 inches in Forks Township.

The combination of melting snow and freezing rain on the 5th and rain on the 6th caused minor flooding along the Millstone River at Griggstown. The Millstone River at Griggstown was above its 10 foot flood stage from 930 p.m. EST on the 6th through 1137 a.m. EST on the 7th. It crested at 10.21 feet at 6 a.m. EST on the 7th. While the flooding was occurring, temperatures were below freezing and plummeting toward zero. Any leftover, untreated standing water froze.  Two day event precipitation totals included 0.72 inches in Basking Ridge (Somerset County), 0.64 inches in Trenton (Mercer County) and 0.63 inches in Hillsborough (Somerset County).

The Manatawny Creek near Spangsville was above its 6 foot flood stage from 718 p.m. EST through 949 p.m. EST on the 11th. It crested at 6.18 feet at 830 p.m. EST. Event precipitation totals included 1.67 inches in Reading, 1.66 inches in Sinking Spring, 1.63 inches in Boyertown and 1.14 inches in Kutztown.

The combination of snow melt and rain caused poor drainage and some creek flooding in southern Monroe County. In Stroudsburg, flooding was reported along McMichael's Creek in the vicinity of the 7th Street Bridge. In Hamilton Township, flooding was reported along Metzgar Road in the vicinity of the Lake Creek and Mackes Street. Event precipitation totals included 2.50 inches in East Stroudsburg, 2.32 inches in Saylorsburg and 1.69 inches in Mount Pocono.

A single cloud-to-ground lightning strike struck and caused a transformer explosion on Hermit Street in the Manayunk section of Philadelphia. The concussive force of the transformer explosion damaged the windows of at least six homes in the area. One home suffered damage to a dozen windows. The vibrations from the explosion were felt up to one mile away. No serious injuries were reported.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs in Dover, one of which punctured the roof of the Central Delaware Habitat for Humanity ReStore building. Rain water leaked into the building and damaged the rear of the store. No injuries were reported. A wind gust to 47 mph occurred at the Dover Air Force Base.

A severe thunderstorm badly damaged a home in Preston. The winds lifted the house's front porch over the back of it. A window air-conditioning unit was blown into the house. Two sliding glass doors were torn away and the effects of the wind badly damaged the home's kitchen and living room.  The American Red Cross provided a hotel room for the home owner.  No injuries occurred.

The runoff from waves of heavy precipitation caused minor to moderate flooding along the Millstone River that lasted through the night of the 31st and into the late afternoon of April 1st. The flooding forced the closure of the Griggstown Causeway and Blackwells Mills Road across the Millstone River as well as sections of Millstone River Road in Franklin and Montgomery Townships. Minor flooding occurred along the Millstone River at Blackwells Mills, and it was above its 9 foot flood stage from 710 p.m. EDT on the 30th through 900 p.m. EDT on the 31st. It crested at 9.94 feet at 845 a.m. EDT on the 31st. Moderate flooding occurred along the Millstone River at Griggstown, and it was above its 10 foot flood stage from 145 a.m. EDT on the 30th through 435 p.m. EDT on April 1st. It crested at 13.78 feet at 1145 p.m. EDT on the 30th. Minor flooding occurred along the Millstone River at Millstone, and it was above its 10 foot flood stage from 127 p.m. EDT on the 30th through 548 p.m. EDT on the 31st. It crested at 10.96 feet at 315 a.m. EDT on the 31st. Minor flooding also occurred along the Green Brook at Plainfield, and it was briefly above its 8 foot flood stage from 220 a.m. EDT through 318 a.m. EDT on the 30th. It crested at 8.05 feet at 245 a.m. EDT on the 30th. Finally, the North Branch Raritan River at South Branch was above its 7 foot flood stage from 109 a.m. EDT through 1104 a.m. EDT on the 30th, and it crested at 8.80 feet at 645 a.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 3.48 inches in Franklin Township, 3.30 inches in Blackwells Mills, 3.28 inches in Hillsborough Township, 2.99 inches in Montgomery Township, 2.78 inches in Bridgewater Township, and 2.43 inches at the Somerville Airport.

The runoff from waves of heavy precipitation caused flooding along the Manasquan River during the afternoon of the 30th. The Manasquan River at Squankum was above its 7.5 foot flood stage from 1200 p.m. EDT through 451 p.m. EDT on the 30th, and it crested at 7.70 feet at 200 p.m. EDT. In addition, flooding occurred twice along Watson Creek due to runoff from the heavy rain, first during the evening of the 30th and again during the morning of the 31st. Watson Creek at Manasquan was first above its 6 foot flood stage from 644 p.m. EDT through 951 p.m. EDT on the 30th, cresting at 6.77 feet at 812 p.m. EDT. Watson Creek at Manasquan again rose above its 6 foot flood stage from 706 a.m. EDT through 1030 a.m. EDT on the 31st, with a higher crest of 6.95 feet at 854 a.m. EDT on the 31st. Event precipitation totals included 4.00 inches in Colts Neck Township, 3.75 inches in Millstone Township, 2.90 inches in Eatontown, 2.85 inches in Rumson, 2.78 inches in Long Branch, and 2.76 inches in Red Bank.

Buses were made available to shuttle passengers between Montclair State University and Denville. An EF1 tornado with an estimated maximum wind speed of 105 mph touched down in West Dover Hundred.  It touched down just west of Darling Drive and lifted just east of Darling Farm Road.  Two people were injured as the worst wind damage occurred on Darling Drive.  A 58-year-old man and his wife were injured after the tornado elevated, spun and then leveled their mobile home. The man had a bureau, a file cabinet and a mattress over him. The tornado damaged about seventeen homes in the area, leaving four condemned and uninhabitable. The tornado also snapped five poles. A couple of  thousand homes and businesses were also without power. The tornado was embedded within a swath of other damaging winds. The estimated path length was 0.35 miles and the estimated maximum path width was 50 yards.

Very heavy rain caused widespread poor drainage, creek and river flooding throughout the county. More than forty major roadways were closed. There were twenty water rescues and over one hundred stranded vehicles. Numerous roads were closed. Creek and river flooding reached major category. Flooding along the Schuylkill River was the worst since Tropical Storm Floyd on September 16,1999 and flooding along the Perkiomen Creek was the worst since Tropical Storm Irene on August 28, 2011. Hardest hit municipalities included Bridgeport, Conshohocken, Springfield and Whitemarsh. ||In West Norriton Township, flooding along the Schuylkill River surrounded several apartment buildings at Rivercrest and The Lofts. All the residents were sheltered in place. In Lower Providence Township (Eagleville), along the Schuylkill River, the garages of the Riverview Landing Apartments were flooded. In Conshohocken Borough, flooding from the Schuylkill River flooded apartments and a hotel on Washington Street. Residents were asked to voluntarily evacuate. In Skippack Township, vehicles were stuck on Pennsylvania State Route 73. The Skippack Creek also flooded. For about an hour during the evening rush on April 30th in Lower Merion Township, Interstate 76 (Schuylkill Expressway) eastbound was closed due to flooding between State Route 3050 (exit 337) and U.S. Route 1 southbound (exit 339).  Sections of U.S. Route 422 were also closed. SEPTA Regional rail service was suspended through May 1st on the Manayunk-Norristown line. Roadways were flooded and closed in many other townships. Townships reporting multiple roadway closures included Upper Moreland, Perkiomen, Whitemarsh, Horsham, Limerick, Norristown (U.S. Route 202) and Bridgeport.||The West Branch of the Perkiomen Creek at Hillegass rose above its 5 foot flood stage from 330 p.m. EDT on April 30th through 115 a.m. EDT on May 1st. It crested at 5.23 feet at 5 p.m. EDT on April 30th. It crested at 11.76 feet at 1230 a.m. EDT on May 1st.  ||The main stem of the Perkiomen Creek at East Greenville had minor flooding and was above its 4 foot flood stage from 202 p.m. EDT on April 30th through 924 a.m. EDT on May 1st. It crested at 6.02 feet at 730 p.m. EDT on April 30th. This was historically the 8th highest crest on record for the creek and the highest crest since August 28, 2011, associated with Tropical Storm Irene. ||The Schuylkill River at Pottstown had minor flooding and was above its 12.5 foot flood stage from Midnight EDT through 131 p.m. EDT on May 1st. It crested at 12.90 feet at 830 a.m. EDT on May 1st.  Farther downstream, the Schuylkill River at Norristown had major flooding and was above its 13 foot flood stage from 331 p.m. EDT on April 30th through 1115 p.m. EDT on May 1st. It crested at 20.83 feet at 245 a.m. EDT on May 1st. This was historically the 4th highest crest on record for the river and the highest crest since September 16, 1999, associated with Tropical Storm Floyd. The Wissahickon Creek at Fort Washington had major flooding and was above its 10 foot flood stage from 413 p.m. EDT on April 30th through 205 a.m. EDT on May 1st. Very heavy rain caused widespread poor drainage, moderate to major creek and river flooding in Philadelphia. Flooding along the Schuylkill River was the worst since Tropical Storm Floyd on September 16, 1999.  Even moderate tidal flooding occurred on the night of April 30th. The flooding also affected regional rail lines as SEPTA service was suspended through May 1st between Manayunk and Norristown. Air travel was no better at Philadelphia International Airport as flight delays reached around two hours at the height of the storm and one third of all arriving and departing flights were cancelled on April 30th. In Manayunk, three people were rescued from the top of a SEPTA bus as Main Street was severely flooded. Residents were evacuated from an apartment complex on the river. Road closures included Martin Luther King, Kelly and Lincoln Drives.   ||The worst damage to city structures occurred at the Water Works facility and to the Gorgas Bridge on Forbidden Drive. About thirty residents on Venice Island Lofts suffered heavy apartment flooding and about thirty vehicles were towed. The paper factory on Venice Island was also damaged. The Manayunk Brewery suffered significant damage and was closed for several weeks as were some of its neighboring businesses. The Green Towne Montessori School was also heavily flooded. The water department responded to over 100 reports of residential basement flooding.| |The Frankford Creek at Castor Avenue had moderate flooding and twice rose above its 7 foot flood stage, first from 257 p.m. EDT through 323 p.m. EDT on April 30th with a crest of 7.28 feet at 315 p.m. EDT. The Frankford Creek at Castor Avenue again rose above its flood stage from 453 p.m. EDT through 837 p.m. EDT on April 30th, with moderate flooding occurring and a higher crest of 9.50 feet at 615 p.m. EDT. The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge had major flooding and was above its 7 foot flood stage from 307 p.m. EDT on April 30th through 530 a.m. EDT on May 1st. It crested at 12.03 feet at Midnight EDT on May 1st. It was the 6th highest crest on record and the highest since Tropical Storm Irene on August 28, 2011.  |  |The Wissahickon Creek at its mouth had moderate flooding and was above its 5 foot flood stage from 405 p.m. EDT on April 30th through 837 a.m. EDT on May 1st. It crested at 8.30 feet at 1200 a.m. EDT on May 1st. This was the highest crest recorded since September 8, 2011.  The Schuylkill River at Philadelphia had moderate flooding and was above its 11 foot flood stage from 624 p.m. EDT on April 30th through 626 p.m. EDT on May 1st. It crested at 13.91 feet at 400 a.m. EDT on May 1st. This was historically the 7th highest crest on record for the river and the highest crest since September 17, 1999 associated with Tropical Storm Floyd.  | |The onshore flow that started on April 29th caused minor tidal flooding in Philadelphia with both high tide cycles on April 30th.  But, the combination of the residual onshore flow and the freshwater runoff caused moderate tidal flooding with the high tide cycle early on May 1st. The high tide in Philadelphia reached 9.94 feet above mean lower low water. Moderate tidal flooding starts at 9.2 feet above mean lower low water. This was the 7th highest tide on record in Philadelphia.||Event precipitation totals included 5.45 inches in Rockledge, 4.91 inches at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport, 4.87 inches in Somerton and Philadelphia and 4.81 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport.

Flooding along the main stem of the Brandywine Creek was the worst since Tropical Storm Floyd on September 16, 1999. Other flooding was the worst since Tropical Storm Irene on August 28, 2011. | |In Avondale Borough, flooding along the East Branch of the White Clay Creek forced the evacuation of 300 residents in the Avondale Apartments on First Street late on the afternoon of April 30th. They were permitted to return on the morning of May 1st. Shelters were opened for the evacuees. In East Coventry Township, the Pigeon Creek overflowed and forced the closure of Halteman and Kolp Roads. It crested at 13.50 feet at 915 p.m. EDT on April 30th. This was historically the 5th highest crest on record for the creek and the highest crest since August 28, 2011, associated with Tropical Storm Irene. ||The main stem of the Brandywine Creek at Chadds Ford had major flooding and was above its 9 foot flood stage from 505 p.m. EDT on April 30th through 1123 p.m. EDT on May 1st. It crested at 16.05 feet at 245 a.m. EDT on May 1st. This was historically the 3rd highest crest on record for the creek and the highest crest since September 16, 1999, associated with Tropical Storm Floyd.   ||The Red Clay Creek at Kennett Square was above its 7.5 foot flood stage from 535 p.m. EDT through 1108 p.m. EDT on April 30th. It crested at 8.55 feet at 7 p.m. EDT on April 30th, the 7th highest crest on record.  The White Clay Creek at Strickersville was above its 9.5 foot flood stage from 505 p.m. EDT on April 30th through 208 a.m. EDT on May 1st. It crested at 12.11 feet at 915 p.m. EDT on April 30th, the 5th highest crest on record and the highest since Tropical Storm Irene on August 28th.  The French Creek at Phoenixville was above its 8 foot flood stage from 1258 p.m. EDT on April 30th through 147 p.m. EDT on the 1st.  It crested at 9.40 feet at 345 p.m. EDT on April 30th. Very heavy rain caused widespread poor drainage and moderate to major creek flooding throughout Delaware County. States of Emergency were declared in Chester City, Darby Borough and Marple Township. Flooding along the main stem of the Brandywine Creek was the worst since Tropical Storm Floyd on September 16, 1999.  Even moderate tidal flooding occurred along the Delaware River on the night of April 30th.||Flooding along Chester Creek forced the evacuation of around 60 homes and 250 residents in the Parker Manor Section of Chester City. The American Red Cross assisted with opening shelters. Farther upstream, Brookhaven Borough recommended evacuations along Chester Creek Road. At the Kerlin Street Bridge, the creek was almost completely blocked by debris. The borough opened a welcome, warming center at the Borough Hall. Darby Borough declared an emergency as the Darby Creek flooded. Road closures included McDade, Springfield, New Walnut, Pine, 9th, Chestnut, 12th, 13th and 14th streets. A shelter was opened at the Darby Borough Recreation Center. Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused two water rescues involving occupied vehicles in Norristown. One vehicle was stuck on U.S. Route 202/Markley Street. Three persons were rescued from that vehicle unharmed. A second vehicle was trapped in flood waters at the intersection of East Lafayette Street and Walnut Street. One person was rescued unharmed. The precipitation event total in Norristown was 2.13 inches.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused a water rescue from a trapped vehicle along the Mill Creek at the intersection of Old Gulph and Williamson Roads in Lower Merion Township.  The single occupant was safely rescued by fire department personnel. The precipitation event total in Lower Merion Township was 2.13 inches.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding along the Tannery Run along East Butler Avenue in Ambler Borough. The borough police station was also flooded. The precipitation event total in Ambler Borough was 2.84 inches.
Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding along the Wissahickon Creek which resulted in the closure of Locust Street.  The precipitation event total in Ambler Borough was 2.84 inches.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding along the Tacony Creek. The Tookany Creek Parkway was closed in Cheltenham Township between Jenkintown Road and Central Avenue. Roadways were also flooded in Elkins Park and Abington. Event precipitation totals included 2.51 inches in Blue Bell.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding along the Wissahickon Creek. The Wissahickon Creek at Fort Washington (Upper Dublin Township) crested at 10.23 feet at 815 p.m. EDT on the 9th. Event precipitation totals included 2.84 inches in Ambler, 2.51 inches in Blue Bell and 1.73 inches in Fort Washington.

Residual flooding along the Wissahickon Creek at Fort Washington (Upper Dublin Township) continued until 835 p.m. EDT on the 9th. Overall, the Wissahickon Creek at Fort Washington was above its 10 foot flood stage from 701 p.m. EDT on the 9th through 835 p.m. EDT on the 9th. It crested at 10.23 feet at 815 p.m. EDT on the 9th. Event precipitation totals included 2.84 inches in Ambler, 2.51 inches in Blue Bell and 1.73 inches in Fort Washington.

Heavy rain led to flash flooding of roadways around the intersection of Interstate 95 and Churchmans Road in the northeast part of White Clay Hundred.  The left lanes of Interstate 95 in both directions were flooded. Southbound Interstate 95 was down to one lane open. Southbound Delaware State Route 1 was closed at Interstate 95 due to flooding. The ramps from Churchmans Road were also flooded.  Sand and mud runoff spilled onto the Delaware State Route 1 ramp from the Christina Mall. The heavy rain also caused a gas station's canopy collapse at University Plaza in Christina.  Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 3 and 4 inches in the area.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding of the Scotland Run and the closure of U.S. Route 322 at Fries Mill Road in Williamstown (Monroe Township). Event precipitation totals 2.69 in the township, most of which fell within an hour.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in and around Glassboro. The flooding also affected a shopping center where water accumulated around one foot.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller creeks and roadways in and around Pitman. Event precipitation totals included 4.11 inches within the borough.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding along the Mantua Creek near Pitman. The creek crested at 5.32 feet (flood stage is 5 feet). Event precipitation totals included 4.11 inches in Pitman.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding along and around U.S. Route 130 in Pennsauken Township. Lanes were closed on the major roadway.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller creeks and roadways in Pilesgrove Township just to the northwest of Woodstown. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 3.0 and 3.5 inches.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage flash flooding in southern Philadelphia. Water was waist high in both directions on Interstate 95 at the Broad Street Tunnel. Numerous vehicles were stranded. Precipitation total was 2.56 inches at the Philadelphia International, most of which fell within one hour.

The heavy rain caused flooding along the Mantua Creek near Pitman that continued into the middle of the evening on the 10th.  The Mantua Creek near Pitman was above its 5 foot flood stage from 627 p.m. EDT through 854 p.m. EDT on the 10th. It crested at 5.32 feet at 730 p.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals in Gloucester County included 4.11 inches in Pitman, 2.69 in Monroe Township, 2.59 inches in Washington Township, 2.20 inches in Sewell and 2.04 inches in Sewell.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding within Dover.  Lockerman Street was flooded and closed. A water rescue saved one person from a trapped vehicle. A few buses were also surrounded by flood waters within the city.  Event precipitation totals included 1.78 inches in Dover.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding in the Millsboro and Long Neck areas of Sussex County around Indian River Bay. The flash flooding was enhanced because the heavy rain and run-off coincided with the high tide.  Event precipitation totals included 1.90 inches in Millsboro.

The runoff from the heavy rain that fell during the late afternoon and early evening of the 9th in Montgomery County caused minor flooding along the Wissahickon Creek overnight on the 9th in Philadelphia. The Wissahickon Creek at its mouth in Philadelphia was above its 5 foot flood stage from 1030 p.m. EDT on the 9th through 216 a.m. EDT on the 10th. It crested at 5.43 feet at 1215 a.m. EDT on the 10th.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage and small stream flooding in East Hanover Township. New Jersey State Route 10 was closed within the township with some underpasses totally submerged. Entire event precipitation totals included 2.41 inches in Denville, 2.28 inches in Mendham Township and 2.11 inches in Mine Hill Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding in Metuchen. Flooding was reported along Main Street and New Jersey State Route 27 in Metuchen.  Entire event precipitation totals included 2.00 inches in Woodbridge.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding in southwest Warren County centered in and around Phillipsburg as well as Mansfield and Franklin Townships. Road closures were reported in both municipalities. Entire event precipitation totals included 3.52 inches in Mansfield Township, 3.29 inches in Greenwich Township, 3.11 inches in Stewartsville, 2.88 inches in Washington Township and 2.57 inches in Hope.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding of roadways and smaller creeks in and around Wyomissing. At least one vehicle was stranded in flood waters on State Hill Road near Bern Road in Wyomissing. Event precipitation total was 2.20 inches in Wyomissing.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding of roadways and smaller creeks in Muhlenberg Township. Two vehicles were trapped in flood waters on North Fifth Street Highway near the Plaza 222 Shopping Center.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding of roadways and small creeks in Reading.  Several motorists were stranded within the flood waters. Spring Street was flooded and closed. The subway was submerged. Other roadways that were flooded included the Warren Street Bypass (Pennsylvania State Route 12). Event precipitation totals included 2.07 inches within Reading and 2.05 inches at the Reading Regional Airport.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding of roadways and small creeks in Upper Pottsgrove Township. Flooding was reported along Pine Ford Road at Pennsylvania State Route 100 near the headwaters of Sprogels Run and a tributary of the Manatawny Creek. Event precipitation totals included 3.65 inches in Pottstown, 3.19 inches in Gilbertsville and 2.34 inches at the Pottstown Airport.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours also caused flash flooding of roadways and small creeks in New Hanover Township. Flooding was reported along North Charlotte Street and Kleman Road near the Minister Creek. Event precipitation totals included 3.65 inches in Pottstown, 3.19 inches in Gilbertsville and 2.34 inches at the Pottstown Airport.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding of small creeks and poor drainage flooding in Lehigh County. In Allentown, heavy flooding was reported on Lehigh Street and around the intersection of U.S. Route 22 and MacArthur Road. In Emmaus, flood waters from the Leibert Creek inundated Indian Creek Road.  Event precipitation totals included 3.31 inches at the Lehigh Valley International Airport and 1.80 inches in Schnecksville.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused poor drain flash flooding in eastern Northampton County. A water rescue was performed in Palmer Township on South 25th Street at the Easton High School.  Event precipitation totals included 3.62 inches in Forks Township, 3.34 inches in Martins Creek, 3.31 inches at the Lehigh Valley International Airport and 2.55 inches in Glendon.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused flash flooding along the Perkiomen Creek at East Greenville. The creek crested at 4.33 feet at 645 p.m. EDT on the 13th. Event precipitation totals included 2.95 inches in East Greenville.

Residual flooding from the heavy rain persisted into the evening of the 13th along the far northern Perkiomen Creek. The Perkiomen Creek at East Greenville was above its 4 foot flood stage from 421 p.m. EDT through 756 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 4.33 feet at 645 p.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 2.95 inches in East Greenville.
A severe thunderstorm tore down trees and wires in eastern Bern Township.
A severe thunderstorm tore down a few trees and wires in Spring Township.
A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees and wires in Reading. Nearby Reading Regional Airport reported a wind gust of 53 mph.
A severe thunderstorm tore down a few trees and wires in Alsace Township.
A few trees and wires were torn down by a severe thunderstorm in District Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires within Allentown. A trained Skywarn spotter measured a wind gust of 54 mph in the south side of the city. The greatest number of power outages within Lehigh County was in Salisbury Township, just south of Allentown.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs in Bethlehem as well as a tree at the intersection of West Elizabeth Avenue and Main Street. The greatest number of power outages in Northampton County was concentrated within Bethlehem.

A lightning strike caused a townhouse fire at the Stonegate Village townhouse development in Richland Township. It took firefighters about half an hour to extinguish the blaze. No serious injuries were reported.
A lightning strike caused a house fire in Forks Township. The same thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 57 mph within the township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs in Franklin Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and large tree limbs in Mansfield Township. Jersey Central Power and Light reported about 1,500 homes and businesses lost power in Warren County, mainly in Mansfield Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Randolph Township.
A Skywarn spotter estimated wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Chester Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Easton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Ridgely.
A severe thunderstorm dropped quarter size hail in Orefield (Along the North and South Whitehall Township line).
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in eastern Lynn Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Heidelberg Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Lowhill Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in North Whitehall Township.
A lightning strike started a house fire in Hockessin (Mill Creek Hundred). No injuries were reported.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees along Maryland State Route 18 in Queenstown.

A lightning bolt damaged the chimney of a home at Wisteria Lane and Fox Glove Court in Doylestown. The lightning strike caused the brick chimney to explode. Bricks and mortar were left strewn across the home's roof, front yard and were even thrown into the street. No injuries were reported.
The Pennsylvania State Police Barracks in Avondale were struck by lightning and damaged radio transmitters at the site.
A house was struck by lightning off of North Main Street in Trumbauersville. No serious injuries were reported.

A lightning strike and subsequent fire totally consumed an abandoned home along Martin Road in Highland Township. The house was fully consumed by flames when fire crews arrived and it took two companies more than an hour to get the fire under control.
Lightning struck a garage on Allentown Road in Milford Township and caught fire.

An attic lightning strike and subsequent fire forced residents of a two-story home on Summer Ridge Circle in Warrington Township to flee their home. When firefighters arrived, smoke and flames were spreading through the attic of the home and forced them to cut holes in the roof to battle the blaze.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several large trees in Trumbauresville Borough.  The downed trees made it difficult for firefighters to get to blazes started by lightning strikes in the area. A pair of downed trees damaged the roof of a garage within the borough.
A severe thunderstorm also dropped quarter size hail in Trumbauersville.
A lightning strike to a chimney caused an attic fire in a home along Lynn Drive in West Deptford Township. Fire fighters were able to bring the fire under control within 30 minutes.
A lightning strike caused another house fire in Gloucester County on Hickory Lane in Harrison Township. No serious injuries were reported.
A lightning strike caused smokey conditions in the basement of a home on Birch Street in Vineland. This was one of two homes that were struck by lightning in the city.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees along Tasker and Mifflin Streets in South Philadelphia.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees along South 59th Street in South Philadelphia.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees along Pennsylvania State Route 313 in Bedminster Township. Wind damage extended south into Doylestown. The intersection of East State Street and Cedar Lane was closed because of a downed tree. Many intersection lights were not functioning within Doylestown.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a whole tree on Wheaton Avenue near State Route 55 in Millville. A wind gust of 49 mph was measured at Millville Municipal Airport.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 62 mph near Tuckerton on the Great Bay Boulevard.

Event precipitation totals included 1.75 inches at East Nantmeal, 1.39 inches in Unionville and 1.30 inches in Spring City.

A thunderstorm dropped nickel size hail in Piscataway.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees along Interstate 295 in Mansfield Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires were knocked down in Lumberton Township.
A severe thunderstorm damaged sail boats in the Delaware River off of Cinnaminson Township. No injuries were reported.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires in Marydel.  One downed tree badly damaged an outdoor grill.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Lehighton.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Mountainhome within Barrett Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Glen Mills.
A severe thunderstorm uprooted trees in Media.  PECO Energy reported about 15,000 of its customers lost power in Delaware County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in North Coventry Township. One fell onto and damaged a home.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees across northeastern Montgomery County in Upper Frederick and  Upper Salford Townships; the Harleysville section of Lower Salford Township and in Pennsburg and East Greenville. PECO Energy reported about15,000 of its customers lost power in Montgomery County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in lower sections of Northeast Philadelphia.

Earlier the same thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 54 mph at Philadelphia International Airport at 659 p.m. EDT. PECO Energy reported about 30,000 of its customers lost power in Philadelphia.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees across lower Buck County from Upper Southampton east through Lower Makefield Township. PECO Energy reported about 25,000 of its customers lost power in Bucks County.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused poor drainage, field and small creek flash flooding in parts of Wantage and Montague Townships. Event precipitation totals included 3.69 inches in Wantage Township. Three inches of rain also fell in Sussex Borough.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding of roadways and smaller streams in central Somerset County. The flash flooding resulted in a rescue of a stranded motorist on Somerset Street in Somerville. Event precipitation totals included 2.35 inches in Montgomery Township and 1.72 inches in Hillsborough Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in the Lake Hopatcong area of Jefferson Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused roadway and creek flash flooding in western Reading and Wyomissing around the Wyomissing Creek. Vehicles were stranded in flood waters near the Spring Street subway in Reading. Event precipitation totals included 2.69 inches in Wyomissing and 2.62 inches in Reading.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding along New Jersey State Route 12 in Kingwood Township around where it crosses the Lockatong Creek. Event precipitation totals included 2.64 inches in Kingwood Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain also caused flash flooding along New Jersey State Route 12 in Raritan Township near the Plum Brook. One vehicle was trapped in the flood waters. Event precipitation totals included 2.64 inches in Kingwood Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage flash flooding along U.S. Route 9 in Woodbridge Township. Multiple water rescues occurred, but no serious injuries were reported. Event precipitation totals included 2.03 inches in Woodbridge Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage flash flooding in Perth Amboy with significant flooding reported along New Brunswick Avenue (County Route 616). Event precipitation totals included 2.03 inches in Woodbridge Township.

Event precipitation totals included 2.03 inches in Woodbridge Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees along Red Mill Road in Newark.  Farther east, the squall line produced a wind gust of 51 mph at the New Castle County Airport.

A severe thunderstorm tore down a few trees, tree limbs and power lines in Doylestown Township. The combination of the wind and lightning caused about 3,500 homes and businesses to lose power in Doylestown Township and Borough.
A lightning strike knocked down a pole in Doylestown. The combination of the damaging winds and lightning caused about 3,500 homes and businesses to lose power in the local area.
A severe thunderstorm tore down a large oak tree as well as several large tree limbs in Westampton Township.
A squall line severe thunderstorm knocked down a large tree and several large tree limbs in Wernersville Borough.
A squall line severe thunderstorm knocked down several large tree limbs in Wyomissing.

A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees in Robeson Township. A 10-year-old boy was injured when a tree toppled onto a building at the camp behind High Point Baptist Church on Chapel Road. The  boy was outside and was hit by one of the branches when the tree came down. He was taken to Reading Hospital with a cut to his head and a possible shoulder injury. About 7,000 Berks County residents lost power.
A 39-year-old man was struck and injured by lightning. He required hospitalization.

A squall line of severe thunderstorms knocked down several trees and tree limbs as it moved across Monroe County.  About 140 homes lost power. Hardest hit were Eldred Township, Stroudsburg and East Stroudsburg. In Stroudsburg, a 60 foot tall tree damaged two gravestones in the Stroudsburg Cemetery.

A squall line of severe thunderstorms knocked down numerous trees as it moved through Chester County. Approximately 80,000 homes and businesses lost power with thirty roadways closed because of downed trees. Chester County had about a third (17,000) of the remaining southeast Pennsylvania outages on the afternoon of the 9th.  West Caln Township still had 5,000 homes and businesses without power that night.  Overall, the southern half of the county was hardest hit.  Downed trees damaged homes in West Fallowfield, West Caln, Penn and Easttown Townships.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous large tree limbs in Chadds Ford Township.
A squall line of severe thunderstorm knocked down trees in Glen Mills.
A Skywarn spotter measured a wind gust of 60 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Norwood.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Upper Darby Township.

A squall line of severe thunderstorms knocked down numerous trees and wires mainly across the northern half of Lehigh County. In North Whitehall Township, a back-up generator started a house fire. Wind gusts of 56 mph and 47 mph were measured within Allentown and at the Lehigh Valley International Airport respectively. The combination of damaging winds and lightning caused about 6,500 homes and businesses to lose power in the Lehigh Valley. It took until the night of the 10th to have power fully restored.
A severe thunderstorm snapped a large tree which fell onto and damaged a vehicle in the Mount Airy section of Philadelphia.

A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 59 mph at the Philadelphia International Airport at 836 p.m. EDT. The same squall line produced a wind gust of 56 mph at Northeast Philadelphia Airport at 846 p.m. EDT.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Washington Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Levittown (Middletown Township). The downed trees caused some transformers to pop.  A wind gust of 57 mph was measured at nearby Newbold Island.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 58 mph in Maple Shade Township.
A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees and tree limbs in Riverside Township. Power lines were also knocked down.
A Skywarn Spotter measured a wind gust of 62 mph in Runnemede Borough during a severe thunderstorm.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees, poles and wires in Pennsauken Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down many trees and wires in Cherry Hill Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and caused power outages in Stratford Village.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a tree across Creek Road in Moorestown and partially blocked the roadway.

A National Weather Service employee measured a wind gust of 58 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Burlington Township. Nearby Florence Township had over one-third of the remaining power outages in Burlington County the ensuing morning.
A severe thunderstorm split a large tree in half in Lumberton Township.
A Skywarn Spotter measured a wind gust of 60 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Southampton Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees, some of which blocked roadways in the Groveville area of Hamilton Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down several large tree limbs and wires, mainly over the southern half of Chester County.

A severe thunderstorm produced a strong microburst in Voorhees Township in the Green Ridge Development. Numerous trees and wires were knocked down. The wind itself and/or the downed trees caused siding, roofing and fencing damage to several homes. Downed trees also damaged some vehicles. Trees as tall as 70 feet were toppled. A few families were evacuated. The microburst affected homes from Great Oak and North Pelham Roads east through Green Ridge, Blue Ridge and Saddle Ridge Roads.  The estimated peak wind gust was 80 mph. Nearly 7,000 homes and businesses lost power in Camden County.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused widespread street flooding with several impassable roadways within the township.  Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 6 inches in the township and in nearby Howell (Monmouth County), 5.91 inches of rain fell.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage and small creek flash flooding in southeastern Monmouth County in Wall and Howell Townships. New Jersey State Route 35 was flooded in Wall Township between New Jersey State 138 and the Shark River Bridge. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 6 inches and 5.91 inches of rain was measured in Howell.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage flash flooding within Metuchen. Main Street was under three feet of water, near the Amtrak tracks. Event precipitation totals in Middlesex County included 3.13 inches in Matawan, 3.11 inches in New Brunswick, 2.98 inches in East Brunswick and 2.92 inches in Old Bridge.
Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused the closure of Interstate 295 in Bordentown Township near Blacks Creek.  Event precipitation total included 2.62 inches in Burlington Township.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage flash flooding within Sayreville. Motorists were stranded in high water. Event precipitation totals in Middlesex County included 3.13 inches in Matawan, 3.11 inches in New Brunswick, 2.98 inches in East Brunswick and 2.92 inches in Old Bridge.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage flash flooding within Perth Amboy. Market Street, Maple Street, Fayette Street and New Brunswick Avenue were all flooded and closed. Residents were using kayaks and at least one vehicle was stranded in flood waters. The flash flooding forced the suspension of New Jersey Transit Service between Woodbridge and South Amboy. Event precipitation totals in Middlesex County included 3.13 inches in Matawan, 3.11 inches in New Brunswick, 2.98 inches in East Brunswick and 2.92 inches in Old Bridge.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused the evacuation of residents along Ellisdale Road near the Crosswicks Creek in Chesterfield Township. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 2.5 and 3.0 inches in the area. Event precipitation totals included 2.62 inches in Burlington Township.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage and small creek flash flooding in Hazlet near its border with Keyport. New Jersey State Route 36 and Florence Avenue near the Chingarora Creek were flooded and closed.  Event precipitation totals included 3.62 in Millstone Township, 3.42 inches in Holmdel, 3.30 inches in Middletown and 3.13 inches in Matawan.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding in Salisbury Township. This caused numerous flooded roads as well as a couple of road washouts. Sections of the Trout Creek and Black River flooded. Event precipitation totals included 1.57 inches in Breinigsville, 1.39 inches in Macungie and 1.31 inches at the Allentown Queen City Airport. Most of this rain fell within an hour.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding in south central Lehigh County. Several roadways were flooded in Allentown, South Whitehall Township, Emmaus and Upper Saucon Township.  Vehicles stalled trying to cross the flood waters.  In Allentown, this included one vehicle that became stuck in flood waters under a railroad bridge on South 8th Street. Flooded roadways included Walbert Avenue and Cedar Crest Boulevard in South Whitehall Township and Lehigh Street in Emmaus.  Event precipitation totals included 1.57 inches in Breinigsville, 1.39 inches in Macungie and 1.31 inches at the Allentown Queen City Airport. Most of this rain fell within an hour.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused poor drainage flash flooding in Center City Philadelphia.  Storm drains could not keep up with the run-off near Thomas Jefferson University Hospital at the intersection of 12th and Chestnut Streets. Event precipitation totals included 2.16 inches at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport and 1.86 inches in Philadelphia.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding along the Frankford Creek. The Frankford Creek at Castor Avenue was above its 7 foot flood stage from 845 p.m. EDT through 925 p.m. EDT on the 14th. It crested at 8.71 feet at 9 p.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 2.16 inches at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport and 1.86 inches in Philadelphia.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding along the Pennypack Creek. The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge was above its 7 foot flood stage from 852 p.m. EDT through 910 p.m. EDT on the 14th. It crested at 7.43 feet at 9 p.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals included 2.16 inches at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport and 1.86 inches in Philadelphia.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused poor drainage flash flooding in Bristol Township. Numerous roadways were flooded near the Delaware River and included Radcliffe Street, Farragut Street and Wilson Street.  Event precipitation totals included 2.16 inches at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport, 2.01 inches in Warrington, 1.96 inches in Newtown and 1.92 inches in Jamison.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused poor drainage flash flooding on the campus of the Lower Bucks Hospital in Bristol Township. Flood waters started to cascade from the parking lots into the hospital's staircases. No patients had to be evacuated. Event precipitation totals included 2.16 inches at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport, 2.01 inches in Warrington, 1.96 inches in Newtown and 1.92 inches in Jamison.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees and tree limbs in Cecilton, one of which fell onto power lines.

Slow moving thunderstorms caused flash flooding in eastern Chester County centered on East and West Whiteland Townships. In the Exton section of West Whiteland Township, flash flooding along the Valley Creek spilled onto parts of South Whitford Road and Commerce Drive. Dopper Radar storm total estimates reached between 1 and 2 inches in the county, most of which fell within an hour.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Trenton. A wind gust of 51 mph was recorded at Mercer County Airport and a wind gust of 50 mph was recorded within the city of Trenton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires around the intersection of Taunton Boulevard and Tomlinson Mill Road in Medford Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Tabernacle Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires around New Jersey State Route 70 in from Friendship Road east to Big Hill Road in Southampton Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires around the intersection of Tuckerton and Old Indian Mills Road in Shamong Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Camden County centered in and around Winslow Township.
Penny size hail fell in the West Trenton section of Ewing Township.
A severe thunderstorm also dropped quarter size hail in Tabernacle Township.
Lightning struck the Shawnee Baptist Church on Oakshade Road in Shamong Township.
A lightning strike caused power outages and disrupted 911 communications in Long Hill Township.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused poor drainage flash flooding in Spotswood Borough around Mundy Lane and the Matchaponix Brook. Mundy Lane was closed due to the flooding. Event precipitation totals included 2.98 inches in East Brunswick, 2.00 inches in New Brunswick and 1.72 inches in Old Bridge.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused poor drainage flash flooding in and around Main Street near the Sqankum Branch  Williamstown (Monroe Township).  Event precipitation totals included 1.92 inches in Piney Hollow.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused poor drainage flash flooding in South Amboy.  Event precipitation totals included 2.98 inches in East Brunswick, 2.00 inches in New Brunswick and 1.72 inches in Old Bridge.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused poor drainage and small creek flash flooding in Brick Township. Flash flooding closed the northbound exit to Brick Township off of the Garden State Parkway near the Cedar Bridge Branch.  Event precipitation totals included 3.73 inches in Brick Township, one of the highest amounts to fall in New Jersey on the 15th.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused poor drainage flash flooding in southeastern Monmouth County from Wall and Howell Townships northeast through Long Branch.  In Howell Township, Blake Drive was flooded. Event precipitation totals included 4.55 inches in Belmar, 3.07 inches in Wall Township, 2.94 inches in South Howell, 2.52 inches in Howell, 2.09 inches in Brielle, 1.95 inches in West Belmar and 1.85 inches in Ocean Township.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused poor drainage, small creek and field flash flooding in Salem County from Lower Alloway Township northeast through Upper Pittsgrove Township. Event precipitation totals included 2.80 inches in Woodstown.

Thunderstorms with very heavy downpours caused poor drainage, small creek and field flash flooding in Winslow Township. A few roadways were flooded.  Event precipitation totals included 3.89 inches in Ancora and 2.19 inches in Winslow Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down poles and wires along Pennsylvania Route 10 at Wawassan Drive in Honey Brook Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs in Graterford (Perkiomen Township).

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Lower Salford Township. Trees were knocked down along Cressman Road, Shadynook Road, Old Skippack Road, Main Street, Maple Avenue, Clemens Road and Astor Drive.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few large tree limbs and a tree in Franconia Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and large tree limbs in Concord Township. Some roadways were blocked by downed trees.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and large tree limbs in Middletown Township. Some roadways were blocked by downed trees.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Collingdale Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Glenolden Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Folcroft Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Upper Darby Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down three trees in Philadelphia.
A thunderstorm dropped nickel size hail in Media.

A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees and caused wind damage in the Hoot Owl subdivision of Medford Township. Two homes suffered major damage and were uninhabitable. A tree fell onto a home on Christopher Mills Road. About four or five other homes suffered shingle or siding damage. Three vehicles were also damaged by fallen trees.
A thunderstorm dropped dime to nickel size hail in Riegelsville.
A home was struck by lightning in Malvern Borough.
A home was struck by lightning in East Nottingham Township. Another lightning strike took down wires in the township.
Lightning struck and damaged wires and a pole in West Brandywine Township.
Lightning struck a home in West Bradford Township.
Lightning struck a propane tank in Paoli (Tredyffrin Township). No serious damage or injuries were reported.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in and around Elverson. A tributary to the North Branch of the French Creek flooded South Brick Lane. Flooding likely also occurred near the headwaters of the East Branch of the Conestoga River. A Skywarn spotter measured 2.6 inches in one hour in Elverson. Other event totals included 3.11 inches in Honey Brook, 2.56 inches in Warwick and 2.39 inches in Glenmoore.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in and around Pottstown. A water rescue occurred on College Drive near the Manatawny Creek.  Event precipitation totals included 2.28 inches in Perkiomen, 1.95 inches in Collegeville, 1.87 inches in Harlesville and 1.55 inches in Pottstown.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in Upper Providence Township in the Mingo Creek Basin. Roboda Boulevard and Springer Town Road were flooded and closed. Event precipitation totals included 2.28 inches in Perkiomen, 1.95 inches in Collegeville, 1.87 inches in Harlesville and 1.55 inches in Pottstown.

Runoff from the heavy rain caused flash flooding along the Frankford Creek. The Frankford Creek at Castor Avenue was above its 7 foot flood stage from 1225 a.m. EDT through 1239 a.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 8.27 feet at 1230 a.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 1.43 inches at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport and 1.37 inches in Wyndmoor.
A strong thunderstorm dropped penny size hail in Springtown.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain also caused flash flooding along Reaville Road in Flemington along tributaries to the Neshanic River. One vehicle was stuck in flood waters. Event precipitation totals included 1.51 inches in Flemington, most of which fell within an hour.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in West and East Amwell Townships. New Jersey State Route 31 was closed south of Ringoes.  Downed trees and wires fell onto a tractor-trailer in the Rocktown area. In West Amwell Township, a downed tree blocked Jefferson Road.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees and wires along Hancock Street in Lambertville. The adverse weather in Hunterdon County forced the county's Tricentennial Concert indoors into Hunterdon Central High School and Independence Day fireworks were postponed until August 7th.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires along Sergeantsville Road in Delaware Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires along Zion Road in the Neshanic section of Hillsborough Township. Downed wires surrounded a truck on Castle Hill Lane. No injuries were reported.

A lightning strike and ensuing fire gutted a Wyckoff Mill Condominium building on Powell Court in Hightstown Borough. The lightning struck the roof of the building and started a fire. Seven families were displaced. The fire reached three alarms and fifteen fire companies from seven townships battled the blaze. It took about two hours to get the fire under control. One firefighter hurt his back.

A lightning strike and ensuing fire heavily damaged a two story home on Tremain Road in Bensalem Township. Flames were already emanating from the roof when firefighters arrived. One firefighter suffered minor burns.

A lightning strike and ensuing fire heavily damaged four units of the Orangewood Apartments off of Mill Creek Road in the Violetwood section of Levittown in Bristol Township.  The fire spread along the roof and attic portions of the two story apartment building. Four families were displaced. Approximately 500 cloud-to-ground lightning strikes in Bucks County between 8 p.m. and 9 p.m. EDT.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Medford.

Runoff from thunderstorms with heavy rain caused minor flooding along the Christina River early on the 28th. The Christina River at Coochs Bridge was above its 10.5 foot flood stage from 207 a.m. EDT through 436 a.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 11.33 feet at 345 a.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 1.96 inches at the New Castle County Airport, 1.82 inches in Newport and 1.74 inches in Newark.

The runoff from the thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused minor flooding along the West Branch of the Brandywine Creek during the early morning of the 28th.  The West Branch of the Brandywine Creek near Honey Brook was above its 7 foot flood stage from 211 a.m. EDT through 625 a.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 7.71 feet at 415 a.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 3.11 inches in Honey Brook, 2.56 inches in Warwick and 2.39 inches in Glenmoore.

The runoff from the thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused minor flooding along the North Branch of the Metedeconk River during the early morning of the 15th. The North Branch of the Metedeconk River near Lakewood was above its 8 foot flood stage from 305 a.m. EDT through 645 a.m. EDT on the 15th. It crested at 8.08 feet at 415 a.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 3.42 inches in Jackson Township and 2.95 inches in Brick Township.

The runoff from the thunderstorms with very heavy rain on the 15th caused minor flooding along parts of the Millstone River on the 16th and 17th. The Griggstown Causeway was flooded and closed. The Millstone River at Griggstown was above its 10 foot flood stage from 611 a.m. EDT on the 16th through 410 a.m. EDT on the 17th. It crested at 10.55 feet at 345 p.m. EDT on the 16th. Event precipitation totals from the 15th included 2.63 inches in Raritan, 2.51 inches in Somerville, 2.31 inches in Bridgewater Township and 1.79 inches in Hillsborough Township.

The runoff from the thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused minor flooding along the East Branch of the Brandywine Creek during the early morning of the 11th.  The East Branch of the Brandywine Creek below Downingtown was above its 7 foot flood stage from 1250 a.m. EDT through 249 a.m. EDT on the 11th. It crested at 7.24 feet at 200 a.m. EDT. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached around 3.5 inches in central Chester County.
