A lightning strike started a house fire on Sycamore Street. No serious injuries were reported.
A lightning strike started a house fire in William Township on Morgan Hill Road. No serious injuries were reported.
A lightning strike started a second house fire in William Township on Raubsville Road. No serious injuries were reported with this fire either.
A severe thunderstorm caused significant tree damage in Lehigh Township.

A severe thunderstorm caused significant tree damage in Upper Mount Bethel Township. The combination of damaging winds and lightning caused about 6,500 homes and businesses to lose power in the Lehigh Valley. It took until the night of the 10th to have power fully restored.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 65 mph in the Port Richmond section of Philadelphia.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees in Bensalem Township, one of which damaged a vehicle. Nearby Falls Township still had over 2,700 homes and businesses without power on the night of the 9th.

A squall line of severe thunderstorm knocked down dozens of trees in Radnor Township. The downed trees tore down wires and fences. The township still had over 1,200 homes and businesses without power on the night of the 9th.

A severe thunderstorm snapped a large pine tree along Lansdowne Avenue onto an idling vehicle in Yeadon Borough. No one in the vehicle was injured. PECO Energy reported about 40,000 of its customers lost power in Delaware County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Media Borough. The downed wires caused shuttle buses to be used on the SEPTA 101 trolley line between Media and Scenic Road.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees along Riverton Road in Cinnaminson Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees along East Main Street in Moorestown Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs in Berkeley Township. In addition, three people were injured at the Ocean County Fairgrounds when a tent collapsed on them during the severe thunderstorm. Two of them required hospitalization.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous large tree limbs and trees in Frankford Township.  Frankford, Green and Sparta Townships were hardest hit by power outages in Sussex County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees along the southbound lanes of Brenford Road in Smyrna.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees along Delaware State Route 100 in Christina Hundred and blocked the roadway. Wooden fences and construction signs were also knocked down.  A few other roadways in the hundred were also blocked by downed trees including Hillside and Montchanin Roads as well as Kennett Pike in the Greenville area.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees along three roadways in the Yorklyn area in Mill Creek Hundred. Trees were reported down along Old Kennett Pike and Snuff Mill and Creek Roads.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees on Barley Mill Road near Wilmington.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires along Silverside Road in Brandywine Hundred.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs in the West Trenton section of Ewing Township. One downed limb damaged a vehicle. A wind gust of 51 mph was recorded at Mercer County Airport and a wind gust of 50 mph was recorded within Trenton.
A severe thunderstorm toppled several trees and started a couple of small fires because of downed wires in Glassboro Borough.

A severe thunderstorm tore down trees, large tree limbs and wires mainly across the central third of New Castle County. Nearly 3,000 homes and businesses lost power and power was not completely restored until the morning of the 15th.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire destroyed a shed and its contents on Ridge Road in Southampton Township.
Lightning struck for separate homes in Neptune. No serious injuries or significant damage occurred.
A severe thunderstorm also knocked down a couple of trees in central Philadelphia. One downed tree damaged a vehicle on Palmetto Street.

A severe thunderstorm lastly knocked down a couple of trees in northeastern Philadelphia along Roosevelt Boulevard (U.S. Route 1) between Cottman and Ryan Avenues. The combination of lightning and wind caused about 10,000 PECO Energy customers to lose power in Philadelphia.
A Lightning strike started a shed fire in Lakewood.
A lightning struck damaged three poles, a traffic light system and the intersection itself (from the arcing wires) at Whitehorse and Klockner Roads in Hamilton Township.

Lightning struck three homes in Washington Township and caused electrical damage in all of them. No serious injuries were reported. The combination of damaging winds and lightning caused about 3,000 homes and businesses to lose power in Gloucester County.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused creek and poor drainage flash flooding in Pennsauken in and around the Airport Circle and the Cooper River. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached between 2.0 and 2.5 inches in the township.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding in southern Warren County. Road closures were reported in Phillipsburg (Route 22) and Washington (Route 31 and Highway 57). Entire event precipitation totals included 3.80 inches in Phillipsburg, 3.37 inches in Stewartsville, 1.93 inches in Riegelsville, 1.90 inches in Blairstown, 1.88 inches in Hackettstown, and  1.54 inches in Washington.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage and small stream flash flooding in Northampton County. Road closures were reported in Forks Township and Belfast. A sinkhole developed at the intersection of Freemansburg Avenue and Emrick Boulevard in Bethlehem Township. Entire event precipitation totals included 4.12 inches in Nazareth, 3.56 inches in Palmer Township, 3.22 inches in Plainfield Township, 2.47 inches in Martins Creek, and 2.05 inches in Bethlehem.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller creeks in northeastern Kent County east of Smyrna in the Mill Creek and Smyrna River basins in Duck Creek Hundred.  Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached nearly four inches in the area.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees onto power lines in Middletown.
A mesonet site measured a wind gust of 61 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Saint Georges Hundred near the Appoquinimink River.  Another wind gust of 53 mph was measured in Odessa.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down some trees as tall as 60 feet as well as tree limbs along Barbara Drive in Clarksboro (East Greenwich Township).

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding at the southern end of Kent Island. Kent Point Road was closed due to flash flooding.  Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 4 inches on Kent Island.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in and around Chestertown. One vehicle water rescue occurred on Quaker Neck Road. Many roadways were flooded and included Maryland State Routes 213, 514 and 20, Garland Way, Trafford Drive, High Street, Cross Street and East Campus Avenue. The flooding heavy rains saturated the soil and caused a few weak trees to be knocked over.  The Chester River was also reported to be running very high, but within bankful. Event precipitation totals included 5.75 inches in Kennedyville, 4.60 inches in Rock Hall and 3.64 inches in Galena.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in and around Rock Hall. Many roadways were flooded and closed and included Chesapeake Avenue, Walnut Street, Crosby Road and Eastern Neck Island Road.  Event precipitation totals included 5.75 inches in Kennedyville, 4.60 inches in Rock Hall and 3.64 inches in Galena.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in and to the west of Kennedyville. A few roadways were flooded and included Still Pond Road, Urieville Lane, Kennedyville Road and Morgnec Road.  Event precipitation totals included 5.75 inches in Kennedyville, 4.60 inches in Rock Hall and 3.64 inches in Galena.
Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in the northern part of Tilghman Island in western Talbot County. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached seven inches.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in western Queen Anne's County from Centreville westward through Queenstown and Grasonville.  The hardest hit locations were Grasonville and Queenstown where nearly 10 inches of rain fell. This caused flooded roads and multiple water rescues.  In Grasonville, the hardest hit area was Prospect Bay. Six families were evacuated from an apartment surrounded by water on Main Street at Gravel Run Road. About 15 motorists were rescued from trapped vehicles.  In Queenstown, a water rescue occurred on Del Rhodes Avenue near Friel Road. The vehicle was swept off the roadway.  A section of Hibernia Road near Centreville was washed out and much of Maryland State Route 18 from Kent Narrows to Queenstown was flooded.  A number of farm fields in the Church Hill area were also flooded. The flooding rains also knocked over a few shallow rooted trees in the area.  Event precipitation totals included 9.92 inches in Queenstown, 8.47 inches in Romancoke, 7.60 inches in Centreville and 3.57 inches in Stevensville.

Bands of heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding in northern New Castle County during the evening of the 12th. The heavy rain also saturated the soil and knocked over a few shallow rooted trees. About 1,000 homes and businesses lost power in the county. Vehicles became stuck in flood waters at the Christiana Mall. Twaddell Mill Road was flooded and closed between Montchanin Road and Kennett Pike.  Event precipitation totals included 4.10 inches in Odessa, 3.48 inches in Glasgow, 3.23 inches in Middletown, 3.10 inches in Townsend, 3.08 inches in Blackbird, 2.65 inches in New Castle, 2.51 inches at the New Castle County Airport, 2.22 inches in Pike Creek, 2.17 inches in Newport and 2.02 inches in Claymont.

The heaviest rain within New Castle County called small stream and poor drainage flash flooding during the evening of the 12th. The heaviest rain in the county fell in Saint Georges and Appoquinimink Hundreds.  Delaware State Route 9 had high water on it east of Odessa.  Event precipitation totals included 4.10 inches in Odessa, 3.48 inches in Glasgow, 3.23 inches in Middletown, 3.10 inches in Townsend, 3.08 inches in Blackbird, 2.65 inches in New Castle, 2.51 inches at the New Castle County Airport, 2.22 inches in Pike Creek, 2.17 inches in Newport and 2.02 inches in Claymont.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down the framing of  a house under construction on West Central Avenue in Seaside Heights.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Millville. About 1,000 homes and businesses lost power in Cumberland County.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused creek and poor drainage flash flooding in Millville. Hardest hit were homes along Rhonda Drive near the White Marsh Run. Three homes suffered collapsed basement walls. One woman was injured when the basement walls collapsed and she became trapped. The high water mark on some homes reached two feet above their ground level and evacuations occurred. Elsewhere in Millville, numerous vehicles were stranded along New Jersey State Route 47.||Event precipitation totals included 8.94 inches in Millville, 8.60 inches in Newport, 6.51 inches in Vineland, 5.43 inches in Fairfield Township, 4.62 inches in Upper Deerfield and 4.51 inches in Bridgeton.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding within Vineland. Flooded roadways included New Jersey State Route 47. There were several vehicle rescues from flooded roadways. Event precipitation totals included 8.94 inches in Millville, 8.60 inches in Newport, 6.51 inches in Vineland, 5.43 inches in Fairfield Township, 4.62 inches in Upper Deerfield and 4.51 inches in Bridgeton.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding in Downe and Commercial Townships. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 7 inches. Actual event precipitation totals included 8.94 inches in Millville, 8.60 inches in Newport, 6.51 inches in Vineland, 5.43 inches in Fairfield Township, 4.62 inches in Upper Deerfield and 4.51 inches in Bridgeton.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in Deal. Numerous roadways were flooded. Both Norwood Avenue (New Jersey State Route 71) were flooded and impassable near the Poplar Brook. Heavy rain did cause additional poor drainage flooding in eastern Monmouth County. Event precipitation totals included 5.91 inches in Manasquan, 4.94 inches in Wall Township, 4.76 inches in Neptune City, 4.59 inches in Belmar, 4.56 inches in Sea Girt, 4.25 inches in Long Branch, 3.98 inches in Eatontown, 3.84 inches in Ocean Township and 3.12 inches in Howell Township.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in Egg Harbor Township. Franklin Avenue near the headwaters of the Cedar Branch was flooded and closed.  Event precipitation totals in Atlantic County included 6.79 inches in Buena Vista Township, 6.17 inches in Estell Manor, 5.58 inches at the Atlantic City International Airport, 5.55 inches in Egg Harbor City, 4.78 inches in Mays Landing, 4.14 inches in Mullica Township, 3.89 inches in Egg Harbor Township, 3.47 inches in Hammonton and 2.54 inches in Margate City.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in Hamilton Township. Both the Black Horse Pike (U.S Route 322) and Cologne Avenue were closed due to high water. Event precipitation totals in Atlantic County included 6.79 inches in Buena Vista Township, 6.17 inches in Estell Manor, 5.58 inches at the Atlantic City International Airport, 5.55 inches in Egg Harbor City, 4.78 inches in Mays Landing, 4.14 inches in Mullica Township, 3.89 inches in Egg Harbor Township, 3.47 inches in Hammonton and 2.54 inches in Margate City.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in Buena Vista and nearby parts of Hamilton Township. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached around 6.5 inches. Actual event precipitation totals in Atlantic County included 6.79 inches in Buena Vista Township, 6.17 inches in Estell Manor, 5.58 inches at the Atlantic City International Airport, 5.55 inches in Egg Harbor City, 4.78 inches in Mays Landing, 4.14 inches in Mullica Township, 3.89 inches in Egg Harbor Township, 3.47 inches in Hammonton and 2.54 inches in Margate City.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in Galloway Township. Doppler Radar storm total estimates nearly reached 6.5 inches. Actual event precipitation totals in Atlantic County included 6.79 inches in Buena Vista Township, 6.17 inches in Estell Manor, 5.58 inches at the Atlantic City International Airport, 5.55 inches in Egg Harbor City, 4.78 inches in Mays Landing, 4.14 inches in Mullica Township, 3.89 inches in Egg Harbor Township, 3.47 inches in Hammonton and 2.54 inches in Margate City.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in eastern Ocean County. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached 9 inches. In Stafford Township, several vehicles were stranded in high water on New Jersey State Route 72.  Also in the township, an oil tanker was stuck on a washed out section of New Jersey State Route 72 in the bridge construction area.  In Seaside Park, New Jersey State Route 35 was closed north of 5th Avenue. In Point Pleasant, many roadways were flooded, up to two feet deep. Flooding affected the New Jersey Transit Commuter Coast Line Depot in Bay Head. Crews could not access the trains. Buses honored train tickets along the line on the 13th.||Actual precipitation event totals included 8.35 inches in Lacey Township, 7.50 inches in Little Egg Harbor Township, 7.24 inches in Stafford Township, 6.55 inches in Lavallette, 6.02 inches in Point Pleasant, 5.87 inches in Brick Township, 5.43 inches in Berkeley Township,  4.59 inches in Seaside Heights, 4.39 inches in Toms River, 4.02 inches in Lakewood and 2.51 inches in Jackson Township.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused small stream and poor drainage flash flooding in northern Somerset County mainly in Bernards, Bridgewater and Warren Townships. An intersection in Somerville was closed due to flooding. Event precipitation totals included 2.96 inches in Bridgewater Township and 2.30 inches in Bedminster Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and as well as a tree along Leesbridge Road in West Nottingham Township.
A lightning strike damaged a home in East Nottingham Township.  No serious injuries were reported.
Lightning struck a retirement home in Pocopson Township.  No serious damage or injuries were reported.
Lightning struck a home in Havertown (Haverford Township).  No serious damage or injuries were reported.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees across Elkton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few large tree limbs and wires in Christiana Hundred.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a tree as well as several large tree limbs along New Jersey State Route 70 in Cherry Hill Township east of the Ellisburg Circle (New Jersey State Routes 41 and 154).

Stop signs and a traffic light were also knocked down along 29th Street.

The Christina River at Coochs Bridge had minor flooding and was above its 10.5 foot flood stage from 257 p.m. EST through 648 p.m. EST on the 18th. It crested at 11.41 feet at 5 p.m. EST.  Event precipitation totals included 1.85 inches in Port Penn, 1.67 inches at the New Castle County Airport, 1.54 inches in Newark, 1.49 inches in Glasgow and 1.40 inches in Hockessin.

The Crum Creek at Newtown Square had minor flooding and was above its 6 foot flood stage from 256 p.m. EST through 427 p.m. EST on the 18th. It crested at 6.15 feet at 330 p.m. EST. Event precipitation totals included 1.84 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport and 1.40 inches at Garnet Valley.

The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge had minor flooding and was above its 7 foot flood stage from 240 p.m. EST through 742 p.m. EST on the 18th. It crested at 7.71 feet at 430 p.m. EST. Event precipitation totals included 1.95 inches in Rhawnhurst, 1.84 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport and 1.71 inches in Wyndmoor.

Heavy rain caused flooding along Parkers Creek and closed both Union Mill and Hartford Roads in the vicinity of the creek in Mount Laurel Township.  Event precipitation totals included 1.99 inches in Mount Laurel, 1.96 inches in Medford and 1.95 inches in Moorestown.

Heavy rain caused flooding along the Stony Brook and closed Quaker Road (County Route 533) in Princeton. In addition, poor drainage flooding closed Terhune Road between Walnut Lane and Jefferson Road in Princeton Township.  Event precipitation totals included 2.08 inches in Ewing, 1.96 inches in Hamilton and Trenton, 1.94 inches in Princeton and 1.84 inches in East Windsor.

Heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding as well as flooding along waterways in Somerset County.  In Hillsborough Township, high water advisories were in effect on Millstone River Road between Manville and Franklin Drives. Elsewhere in the township, Riverside Drive was closed between Mill Lane and Clawson Avenue along the South Branch of the Raritan River.  In Branchburg Township, the Black Point Road Bridge was closed over the South Branch of the Raritan River.  | |The Millstone River at Griggstown had moderate flooding and was above its 10 foot flood stage from 627 p.m. EST on the 18th through 405 p.m. EST on the 20th. It crested at 12.91 feet at 915 a.m. EST on the 19th. Farther downstream, the Millstone River at Blackwells Mills had minor flooding and was above its 9 foot flood stage from 11 a.m. EST through 430 p.m. EST on the 19th. It crested at 9.05 feet at 100 p.m. EST.  The North Branch of the Raritan River at the village of South Branch had minor flooding and was above its 8 foot flood stage (the established flood stage was raised at this site) from 724 p.m. EST through 1130 p.m. EST on the 18th. It crested at 8.18 feet at 830 p.m. EST. ||Event precipitation totals included 2.29 inches in Franklin Township, 2.05 inches in Bound Brook, 1.92 inches in Montgomery Township, 1.90 inches in Hillsborough Township, 1.88 inches in Raritan and Somerville and 1.78 inches in Branchburg.

The Neshanic River at Reaville had minor flooding and was above its 6.5 foot flood stage from 404 p.m. EST through 846 p.m. EST on the 18th. It crested at 7.39 feet at 6 p.m. EST.  Event precipitation totals included 1.64 inches in Readington Township, 1.63 inches in Flemington and 1.31 inches in Clinton.

Heavy rain caused some poor drainage flooding in Middlesex County. In East Brunswick Township,  Dunhams Corner Road and Church Lane were closed. In Old Bridge Township, Cantrell Road was closed. Event precipitation totals included 2.24 inches in Cranbury Township, 1.90 inches in Old Bridge Township and New Brunswick, 1.88 inches in South River and Woodbridge and 1.86 inches in East Brunswick Township.
A strong thunderstorm knocked down patio furniture and rolled a chair approximately 200 feet of home in Doylestown.

The combination of rain and snowmelt caused moderate flooding along the Millstone River from the morning of the 11th through the afternoon of the 13th. Moderate flooding occurred along the Millstone River at Griggstown, and it was above its 10 foot flood stage from 725 a.m. EDT on the 11th through 452 p.m. EDT on the 13th. It crested at 12.45 feet at 1230 a.m. EDT on the 12th. Event precipitation totals included 0.34 inches in Franklin Township and Montgomery Township, 0.32 inches in Somerville, and 0.31 inches in Bridgewater Township.

Runoff from additional rainfall combined with snowmelt caused minor flooding along the Millstone River from the afternoon of the 14th through the morning of the 16th. Minor flooding occurred along the Millstone River at Griggstown, and it was above its 10 foot flood stage from 242 p.m. EDT on the 14th through 926 a.m. EDT on the 16th. It crested at 11.80 feet at 645 a.m. EDT on the 15th. Event precipitation totals included 0.94 inches in Franklin Township, 0.93 inches in Montgomery Township, 0.90 inches in Somerville, 0.88 inches in Bridgewater Township, and 0.87 inches in Manville.

The combination of rain and snowmelt caused minor flooding along the West Branch Brandywine Creek from the late evening of the 10th through the early morning of the 11th. The West Branch Brandywine Creek at Honey Brook was above its 7.0 foot flood stage from 1125 p.m. EDT on the 10th through 320 a.m. EDT on the 11th, and it crested at 7.23 feet at 115 a.m. EDT on the 11th. Event precipitation totals included 0.73 inches in West Grove, 0.68 inches in Nottingham, and 0.66 inches in Chadds Ford and Unionville.

The combination of rain and snowmelt briefly caused flooding along the Neshanic River during the evening of the 11th. The Neshanic River at Reaville briefly touched its 6.50 foot flood stage at 715 p.m. EDT on the 11th, before then falling below flood stage at 730 p.m. EDT on the 11th. Event precipitation totals included 0.38 inches in Stockton, 0.37 inches in Flemington, and 0.35 inches in Frenchtown.
A lightning strike damaged the Manor House in the Londonderry Retirement Community in Easton. The ensuing fire was limited to the roof and 2nd floor of the 150-year-old building.
A thunderstorm dropped penny size hail in North East.
A thunderstorm dropped nickel size hail in Lincroft (Middletown Township).

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding along 12th Street near the Brandywine Creek in Wilmington. Vehicles were stuck in flood waters on that roadway. No serious injuries were reported. Event precipitation totals since the morning of the 20th included 2.83 inches at the New Castle County Airport, 2.81 inches in Newport, 2.52 inches in Newark and 2.40 inches in Hockessin.

Poor drainage flooding was reported along Governor Printz Boulevard in Wilmington. In addition, minor flooding occurred along the Christina River.  The Christina River at Coochs Bridge was above its 10.5 foot flood stage from 908 a.m. EDT through 1143 a.m. EDT on the 20th. It crested at 11.22 feet at 1045 a.m. EDT.  Event precipitation totals through the morning of the 20th included 2.20 inches in Talley Brook, 2.11 inches in Greenville, 1.88 inches in Newark and 1.77 inches at the New Castle County Airport.

Heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding in eastern Delaware County and resulted in a couple of water rescues in Lansdowne and Darby Township. Event precipitation totals included 2.04 inches in Saint Davids, 1.95 inches in Wallingford, 1.88 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport and 1.75 inches in Swarthmore.

Heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding as well as creek flooding within Philadelphia. Street flooding was reported in Chestnut Hill. The Frankford Creek at Castor Avenue was above its 7 foot flood stage from 844 a.m. EDT through 925 a.m. EDT on the 20th. It crested at 7.53 feet at 915 a.m. EDT. The Pennypack Creek at the Rhawn Street Bridge was briefly above its 7 foot flood stage from 913 a.m. EDT through 919 a.m. EDT on the 20th. It crested at 7.08 feet.  Event precipitation totals through the morning of the 20th included 2.22 inches at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport and 1.88 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport.

A line of severe showers and thunderstorms produced wind damage within Philadelphia. Several trees were knocked down. Peak wind gusts included 71 mph at the Philadelphia International Airport and 62 mph at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport. The severe thunderstorm knocked down trees on Ridge Avenue in the Andorra section of the city as well as in the Fishtown neighborhood. Roadways in Fishtown were blocked by downed trees.
A line of severe showers and thunderstorms knocked down trees along Gulph Road in Upper Merion Township.
A line of severe showers and thunderstorms knocked down trees in Bethlehem.
A severe thunderstorm produced a measured wind gust of 61 mph in Florence.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a large tree onto a house on West Olive Street in Westville.  The tree crashed through the top floor and the home was deemed unsafe to continue to be occupied. No injuries were reported. A wind gust of 71 mph was measured with the same storm at the Philadelphia International Airport.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees on Perryville Road in East Windsor Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and tree limbs near the intersection of U.S. Route 1 and Whispering Woods Boulevard in South Brunswick Township.
A Skywarn Spotter estimated 60 mph as a severe thunderstorm moved through Williamstown.

A severe thunderstorm uprooted a large tree in Glassboro. It took down wires and also damaged a sidewalk. The severe thunderstorm also took down another tree that blocked access to a homeowner's driveway.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down severeal trees on Perrineville Road in Monroe Township.
A Skywarn Spotter estimated wind gusts to 60 mph as a severe thunderstorm moved through Pitman.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a tree that damaged the roof of a home in Wrightstown.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down about a half dozen trees in Newport.

Slow moving thunderstorms caused flash flooding in Toms River Township. New Jersey State Route 37 was flooded from Vaughn Avenue to the Thomas A. Mathis Bridge. Multiple vehicles were trapped in the flood waters with water up to their windows. No serious injuries were reported. Between 20 and 30 water rescues occurred. Flooding was also reported along Adams Avenue and Bash Road near New Jersey State Route 37 in Toms River.  Event precipitation totals within Toms River included 5.24 inches and 4.60 inches.

Thunderstorms with heavy downpours caused flash flooding in Bethlehem Township.  One water rescue was performed. Through the early morning, Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached around 2.5 inches in central Northampton County.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in and around Sayreville. Several roadways were flooded.  Doppler Radar storm total estimates exceeded three inches, most of which fell within 90 minutes.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in and around South Amboy.  The flash flooding also affected New Jersey State Route 35. A storm total amount of 4.50 inches was measured in the city, most of which fell within 90 minutes.

Five people were trapped in those vehicles, but no serious injuries were reported.  Event precipitation totals within Somerset County included 2.52 inches in Bernards Township and 2.20 inches in Branchburg Township.

No serious injuries were reported.  Event precipitation totals within Hunterdon County included 3.56 inches in Lebanon, 2.95 inches in Stockton, 2.93 inches in Clinton and 2.75 inches in Franklin Township.

A severe thunderstorm generated a wind gust of 59 mph in Smyrna. Widely scattered power outages also occurred.

Large hail fell in New Castle from a severe thunderstorm. Half dollar, nickel and dime size hail occurred.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Massey, one of which damaged a fence.

Lightning struck a transformer on Burchard Sawmill Road and started a fire.

Lightning struck the roof of a Brookside Park house on Marlin Drive. It sparked a fire that caused about $30,000 in damage to the home and rendered it uninhabitable.  The family of four were not injured and were assisted by the Red Cross in finding emergency shelter.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in Buena Vista Township and Folsom Borough in Atlantic County.  While flash flooding started with the first wave of thunderstorms during the late afternoon,  a second wave of thunderstorms continued it into the evening. In the Collings Lake area of Buena Vista Township as well as in Folsom, several roadways were flooded and closed. The fire department rescued some stranded motorists in Collings Lake.  Event precipitation totals included 6.37 inches in Folsom, 4.60 inches in Hammonton, 4.40 inches in Mullica Township, 4.24 inches in Buena Vista Township, 3.20 inches in Estell Manor and 2.99 inches in Mays Landing.

The second wave of thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in Vineland. Several roadways were severely flooded within the city.  Event precipitation totals included 4.65 inches in Fairfield Township, 4.60 inches in Vineland, 3.83 inches in Millville, 3.56 inches in Greenwich, 3.10 inches in Newport, 2.98 inches in Upper Deerfield Township and 2.71 inches in Bivalve.

The second wave of thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller creeks and roadways in Franklin and Monroe Townships near the border with Atlantic County.  Event precipitation totals included 4.91 inches in Piney Hollow (Franklin Township) and 3.12 inches in South Harrison Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused flash flooding in and around Newark. Vehicles became stuck in flood waters in Newark.  The afternoon and evening event precipitation totals included 2.55 inches in Newark.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain also caused flash flooding in and around Christiana Hundred. Vehicles also became stuck in flood waters. The afternoon and evening event precipitation totals included 2.27 inches at the New Castle County Airport.
Heavy rain caused some street flooding to occur in Ocean City.  Event precipitation total from Ocean City was 2.58 inches.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few large tree limbs and wires in Upper Township.

A line of severe thunderstorms tore down large tree limbs and wires across the northern tier of Berks County.
A severe thunderstorm tore down poles and wires in Topton.
A severe thunderstorm also tore down poles and wires in Mertztown. A mesonet site measured a wind gust of 60 mph in Mertztown.
A severe thunderstorm tore down numerous trees and wires in Alburtis. Several roadways were closed. Three poles were snapped just outside of the borough line. Power outages lasted for several hours.
The same severe thunderstorm tore down numerous trees and wires in Macungie. Several additional roadways were closed.
The severe thunderstorm continued to knock down trees and wires in Lower Macungie Township.  About 1,600 homes and businesses lost power.
A thunderstorm dropped penny size hail in Skippack.

The same severe thunderstorm knocked down multiple trees in Fredon Township.
A severe thunderstorm also knocked down trees and wires in Newton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Frelinghuysen Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Spring Township on Bainbridge Circle as well as on Avon Avenue and Shakespeare Drive.  One home was damaged as downed trees punctured a hole in the roof.  Another downed tree damaged a vehicle.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires in Whitehall Township and caused power outages. A wind gust of 56 mph was measured at nearby Lehigh Valley International Airport.

A severe thunderstorm toppled about a dozen tractor tailers at the Osram Sylvania Warehouse on Brodhead Road in Bethlehem.  A couple of snapped trees also rolled into vehicles. The roof of a Crayola warehouse was also damaged.  Numerous trees were knocked down in Bethlehem City and Bethlehem Township. A wind gust of 56 mph was measured at nearby Lehigh Valley International Airport.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused some poor drainage flooding in Middlesex County.  A couple of low lying area and underpasses on roadways were closed.  Event precipitation totals included 1.33 inches in North Brunswick, 1.29 inches in South Brunswick and 1.24 inches in South River.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused some poor drainage flooding in Monmouth County, especially on the eastern side of the county.  A couple of low lying area and underpasses on roadways were closed.  Event precipitation totals included 1.44 inches in Wall Township, 1.23 inches in Aberdeen,  1.16 inches in Red Bank and 1.00 in Holmdel.

Poor drainage flooding followed the passage of thunderstorms through Monroe County on the evening of the 14th. The heaviest rain fell in the central and western part of the county.  Event precipitation totals included 2.56 inches in McMichaels, 2.47 inches in Pocono Pines, 2.17 inches in Syndersville and 1.78 inches in Pocono Summit.
A lightning strike knocked a tree down onto wires in Lower Saucon Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Franconia Township, knocked down a mailbox and blew it into a neighboring house's driveway.
A lightning strike started a house fire in Seaville. No injuries were reported.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage flooding as well as flash flooding of smaller creeks in Durham and Nockamixon Townships.  Doppler Radar storm totals reached 3 to 4 inches near the Northampton County border.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding along the Monocacy Creek in Bethlehem. Parts of the Illick's Mill and locations behind the Hotel Bethlehem were flooded. Flood waters also reached into the bottom of the historic Tannery and Waterworks. Other parts of the historic downtown and northern neighborhoods also suffered from poor drainage flooding. The Monocacy Creek at the Illicks Mill Road gage reached its 4.5 foot flood stage at 837 p.m. EDT on the 15th and crested at 5.99 feet at 1045 p.m. EDT on the 15th.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused poor drainage flooding as well as flash flooding of smaller creeks in central and southern Northampton County. The heaviest rain fell in a northwest to southeast axis across the county from eastern East Allen Township through Lower Nazareth Township, Bethlehem Township, Lower Saucon Township and Williams Township. In Bethlehem, flash flooding forced the closure of Easton Avenue at Willow Park Road.  Flash flooding along the Nancy Run also washed out sections of Willow Park Road south through Walnut Street.  A large sink hole near a Pennsylvania Power and Light transmission tower on Clermont Street forced the evacuation of 25 to 30 families for a day. A home on Garrison Street had damage to its foundation and sidewalk. Wilson Avenue, near the Lehigh River became a river itself. Other roadways near the Lehigh River were washed away.  In Easton, parts of Hope Road washed away. Event precipitation totals included 2.89 inches in Glendon and 2.21 inches in Easton.

Residual flooding along the Monocacy Creek in Bethlehem continued into the overnight of the 15th. The Monocacy Creek at the Illicks Mill Road gage was above its 4.5 foot flood stage from 837 p.m. EDT on the 15th through 107 a.m. EDT on the 16th. It crested at 5.99 feet at 1045 p.m. EDT on the 15th.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires along Bridgeville Road (Delaware State Route 18) in Georgetown.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a tree and large tree limbs along Morris Mill Road in Millsboro.
A Skywarn spotter measured a wind gust of 63 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Frankford.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Cecil County including within Elkton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Chestertown.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in and around Collegeville. Roadways were flooded and some flood waters went into the basements of homes. A mesonet site in Collegeville had an event total of 3.81 inches of rain. A mesonet site in nearby Eagleville had an event total of 2.04 inches.

Thunderstorms with torrential downpours also caused flash flooding in southern Montgomery County mainly in Upper Merion Township. In Upper Merion Township, a mud slide caused the closure of Balligomingo Road between Front Street and Portland Road. In the King of Prussia area of the township, numerous roadways were flooded. The Schuylkill Expressway (Interstate 76) was badly flooded with traffic either halted or barely able to get through as the heaviest rain occurred. Event precipitation totals included 2.61 inches in King Of Prussia and 1.98 inches in Bala Cynwyd.
Thunderstorms with torrential downpours caused flash flooding in and around Pheonixville.  A mesonet site within Phoenixville had an event total of 3.50 inches of rain.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees in Rock Hall.
A severe thunderstorm also knocked down trees in Worton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Crumpton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees just south of Millington.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in Middletown.

The Christina River at Coochs Bridge had moderate flooding and was above its 10.5 foot flood stage from 826 p.m. EDT on the 27th through 202 a.m. EDT on the 28th. It crested at 12.16 feet at 1130 p.m. EDT. Event precipitation totals included 2.86 inches in Townsend, 2.81 inches in Middletown, 2.51 inches in Glasgow and Newark, 2.26 inches at the New Castle County Airport and 1.98 inches in Hockessin.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding and poor drainage flooding in southern Cecil County. Flash flooding occurred along creeks feeding into the Sassafras River, particularly Dowdel and Hall Creeks. The intersection of Sandy Bottom and Knights Island Roads was flooded. Event precipitation totals included 2.79 inches in Earleville, 2.78 inches in Sassafras and 1.99 inches in Elkton.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in northern Queen Anne's County. Several roadways had high water on them. In Sudlersville, a part of John Powell Road was washed away near tributaries to the Southeast Creek. Event precipitation totals included 1.97 inches in Centreville and 1.95 inches in Carville.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in central Cumberland County affecting Millville and Vineland the hardest. In Vineland, vehicles were submerged on Butler and Sherman Avenues. Flooding also occurred along New Jersey State Route 47. Event precipitation totals included 4.20 inches in Vineland, 4.07 inches in Millville and 2.94 inches in South Vineland.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in Buena Borough. U.S. Route 40 was flooded and closed near the Deep Run. Event precipitation totals included 3.27 inches in Buena Vista Township.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller streams as well as poor drainage flooding in northern Atlantic County, mainly in and around Hammonton and Folsom.  In Hammonton Township, Packard Street and Bellevue Avenue were closed due to flash flooding. Flooding was also reported along New Jersey State Route 54.  Event precipitation totals included 3.49 inches in Hammonton, 3.22 inches in Folsom and 2.69 inches at the Atlantic City International Airport.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller streams as well as poor drainage flooding in southern Camden County in Winslow Township.  Flooding was reported along New Jersey State Route 73 as well as on U.S. Route 30 (White Horse Pike). Event precipitation totals included 2.86 inches in Winslow Township, 2.67 inches in Berlin Township and 1.93 inches in Haddonfield.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller streams as well as poor drainage flooding in southeastern Burlington County.  Event precipitation totals included 4.46 inches in Chatsworth, 3.39 inches in Oswego Lake, 2.53 inches in Shamong Township and 2.23 inches in Westampton Township.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller streams as well as poor drainage flooding in eastern Ocean County from Toms River Township south through Little Egg Harbor Township.  Event precipitation totals included 4.71 inches in Brick Township, 4.49 inches in Berkeley Township, 4.41 inches at Robert J. Miller Airport, 4.26 inches in Toms River, 3.73 inches in Little Egg Harbor Township, 3.70 inches in Pine Beach, 3.51 inches in Stafford Township, 2.90 inches in Tuckerton and 2.25 inches in Lacey Township.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused poor drainage flash flooding on Long Beach Island. Roadways near Barnegat Inlet were impassable. Surf City also closed Barnegat Avenue Event precipitation totals included 2.26 inches in Point Pleasant Beach, 1.70 inches in Surf City and 1.63 inches in Seaside Heights.

An EF-1 tornado touched down in Honey Brook Township.  No injuries were reported, although several homes as well as numerous trees were damaged.  The tornado touched down near Given Road and moved northeast lifting near Talbotville Road.  Roof panels were torn from one home. A mobile home was unseated from its moorings. Two uninjured people were trapped within the mobile home and had to be rescued by the local fire department. A barn along Talbotville Road had its roof torn off and wall damaged during the storm. Farmstands were damaged along Talbotville Road. Numerous trees were uprooted or snapped along the damage path.  Debris was scattered across roadways and farm fields and included pieces of tin roofs as well as insulation.  Several roads were impassable because of downed trees and power lines.  The path length was approximately 0.7 of a mile, the maximum path width was estimated to be 100 yards and the estimated peak wind gust was 95 mph.

A strong microburst caused wind damage in Whitehall Township in and near the Stiles section of the township. Because of the wind damage, a township state of emergency was declared.  Numerous trees were knocked down and many roads were impassable due to the downed trees. The downed trees damaged twenty-nine homes and buildings. One building sustained major damage. The township advised residents to stay off the roads. Around 600 Pennsylvania, Power and Light customers within the township were still without power late in the evening on the 30th.  Some of the most significant crop damage occurred along Columbia Street where large sections of corn fields were flattened.

A microburst from a severe thunderstorm also affected northern parts of Catasauqua Borough. Numerous trees were knocked down. Several roadways even remained closed the next day as workers continued to remove trees and restore electric service. Hardest hit in the borough were locations from Strawberry Street northeast through Walnut and 14th Streets.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Coplay Borough.
A funnel cloud sighted over Whitehall Township did not reach the ground, however a microburst still caused wind damage in the township.
A trained Skywarn spotter saw a funnel cloud over Fogelsville.  The funnel cloud did not touch down and cause any wind damage.
Another Skywarn spotter saw a funnel cloud over Trexletown.  The funnel cloud did not touch down and cause any wind damage.
A funnel cloud was photographed near Pennsylvania State Route 30 in West Goshen Township. While wind damage did occur in the township, the funnel cloud itself did not reach the ground.
A severe thunderstorm dropped golf ball size hail in Orefield.
Nickel size hail fell in Coplay.
A severe thunderstorm dropped quarter size hail in North Catasauqua Borough.

In addition to the wind damage, a severe thunderstorm dropped golf ball size hail in Whitehall Township. Quarter size hail also fell in the Fullerton section of the township. Siding of homes was dented by the large hail.
A severe thunderstorm damaged a home as well as downed numerous trees in Northampton Borough.  Two people were uninjured, but trapped inside one building.
A severe thunderstorm damaged four to five homes as well as downed numerous trees in North Catasauqua Borough.  No serious injuries were reported.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires in Hanover Township. Airport Road (Pennsylvania State Route 987) was closed because of downed trees between Schoenersville Road and Orchard Lane. The township suffered the most tree damage of any municipality within the county.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires and caused power outages in Allen Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires and caused power outages in East Allen Township. The southbound lanes of Airport Road (Pennsylvania State Route 987) were closed near Hanoverville Road.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires and caused power outages in Upper Nazareth Township.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 61 mph at the Lehigh Valley International Airport.
A Skywarn spotter measured a wind gust of 64 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Pottstown. Hail also fell.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in West Goshen Township.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 63 mph in West Chester.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in Phoenixville.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees onto wires in Hamilton Township. Over 1,000 homes and businesses lost power in Monroe County.
A severe thunderstorm dropped half dollar size hail in Oxford Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Oxford Township.
A severe thunderstorm uprooted whole trees in Liberty Township. About 1,500 homes and businesses lost power in Liberty and Hackettstown.

A severe thunderstorm uprooted more than a dozen whole trees and knocked poles to the ground in Hackettstown. One vehicle was totaled by a downed tree. About 1,500 homes and businesses lost power in Hackettstown and Liberty.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees across the northern tier of New Castle County.
A severe thunderstorm tore down large tree limbs and wires in Grasonville.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Newark.

A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage along the east side of the Northeast River from the McDaniel Yacht Basin northeast to near Maryland State Route 7.  At the McDaniel Yacht Basin, metal siding was peeled from buildings, boats were tossed and a wooden shed was destroyed. Farther to the northeast, trees and poles were knocked down along both Maryland State Routes 272 and 7. Trees were also knocked down between Granview Avenue and Hillcrest Lane, Irishtown Road and Saddler Avenue. Nearly 2,000 homes and businesses lost power in Cecil County.

The Brodhead Creek near Anamolink was above its 8 foot flood stage from 858 p.m. EDT through 1030 p.m. EDT on the 30th. It crested at 8.13 feet at 930 p.m. Pennsylvania State Route 447 which is located along the creek was flooded and remained closed into the overnight.

A series of thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in central Monroe County that lasted into the overnight of the 30th. Hardest hit were Chestnuthill and Pocono Townships. The Monroe County Office of Emergency Management urged motorists to stay off the road. In Chestnuthill Township, the Pohopoco Creek flooded near Camp Jaycee. Merwinesburg Road was closed from Pennsylvania State Route 115 to Jonas Road.  Ziegler Road was also closed near Jonas Road. In Pocono Township, southbound Pennsylvania State Route 611 along the Pocono Creek and near the intersection with Pennsylvania State Route 715 in Tannersville was flooded. There were mud slides in the area also. Farther south along the same creek, Warner Road (a partial wash-out) and Pennsylvania State Route 611 were also closed because of flooding. In Polk Township, Dotters Corner Road (near Dotters Creek) near Pennsylvania State Route 534 was flooded and closed.  Event precipitation totals included 4.63 inches in Pocono Pines, 3.84 inches in Pocono Summit, 2.78 inches in Saylorsburg and 2.71 inches in McMichaels.

In addition to the severe weather, torrential downpours caused flash flooding in Coplay Borough. Several roadways were flooded with vehicles trapped in flood waters. A water rescue occurred on Catherine Street.  Doppler radar storm total estimates reached around two inches.

In addition to the severe weather, torrential downpours caused flash flooding in Northampton Borough as the Dry Run flooded.  On Banks Street, about 12 to 14 homes were flooded. Gasoline was also released into the flood waters. Flash flooding extended to East 8th Street where one home suffered structural damage and two people were trapped inside. The family was displaced and assisted by the Red Cross. Doppler radar storm total estimates reached around two inches.

A series of thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding of smaller streams and poor drainage locations in central Carbon County from around Lehighton northeast through parts of Penn Forest and Towamensing Townships to the Monroe County border. Event precipitation totals include 3.57 inches in Lehighton and 3.19 inches in Jim Thorpe and 2.28 inches in Albrightsville. Doppler Radar storm total estimates reached nearly 5 inches along the Monroe County border in the Pohopoco Creek drainage basin.
A severe thunderstorm snapped a pole northeast of Delmar.
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 67 mph at Royal Oak.  Trees fell onto and knocked down power lines in Talbot County and caused outages. All power was restored by the 24th.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees and wires in Paradise Crossing within Paradise Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Price Township. One tree fell across and blocked Pennsylvania State Route 447 near the Alpine Mountain Resort.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Upper Tulpehocken Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires in Strausstown and caused multiple outages in the downtown area.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Centre Township.
A few trees were knocked down by a severe thunderstorm in Brecknock Township.

A second severe thunderstorm knocked down more trees in Brecknock Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees in Oxford Borough.
A lightning strike destroyed the chimney of a Lower Providence Township home.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires in Lower Providence Township.
A Skywarn Spotter estimated wind gusts of 70 mph as a severe thunderstorm moved through King of Prussia (Upper Merion Township).  Numerous trees were knocked down within the township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees and wires in the Roxborough section of Philadelphia.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Stroud Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Concord Township. One large downed tree damaged a home in the Glen Mills section of the township.

An extremely powerful macroburst associated with a severe thunderstorm cut a swath of wind damage across the eastern side of Aston Township to the east of Concord Road. Peak wind gusts were estimated to reach 85 mph. Shingles and siding was ripped from homes as well as numerous homes that were struck by fallen trees. About fifteen homes were condemned in the township. Wind damage from the macroburst continued southeast through Chester City.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Drexel Hill (Upper Darby Township). One fell across School Lane.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down over 100 trees across Upland Borough and numerous roadways were closed and blocked by fallen trees.
The Borough of Brookhaven was also hit very hard by the squall line of severe thunderstorms. Dozens and dozens of trees were knocked down across the borough and the entire borough lost power.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Chadds Ford Township. Numerous roadways were closed.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires in Middletown Township. It was described as one of the harder hit locations within Delaware County.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires in Chester Heights Borough. Both houses and vehicles were damaged by the fallen trees.

A severe thunderstorm forced the closure Southbound U.S. Route 1 between the Interstate 476 exit in Marple Township and the State Road exit in Upper Providence Township because of downed trees. The roadway remained closed into the 24th.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees and wires in the Feltonville section of Philadelphia. One woman suffered a foot injury.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a couple of trees along Adams Avenue in Philadelphia. One downed tree damaged a gas main. No injuries or additional damage was reported.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees onto homes along Sylvester Street in Philadelphia.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a house under construction on East Allen Street and injured four workers.
A 72 mph wind gust was measured during a severe thunderstorm at the Philadelphia International Airport. It was the fourth highest wind gust ever recorded in Philadelphia.
A Skywarn Spotter measured a wind gust of 71 mph in Norwood Borough during a severe thunderstorm.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Rising Sun.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in Hockessin (Mill Creek Hundred).
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in the southern part of Mill Creek Hundred in Pike Creek.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires in Newark (White Clay Hundred).
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Greenville (Christina Hundred).
A mesonet site recorded a 59 mph wind gust during a severe thunderstorm in Glasgow (Pencader Hundred).  A trained Skywarn Spotter also reported downed trees in Glasgow.
A severe thunderstorm generated a 66 mph wind gust at the New Castle County Airport.
A severe thunderstorm tore off the roof of a third story building within Wilmington.  Wind damage occurred along Elm and Madison Streets within the city.
A trained Skywarn Spotter measured a wind gust of 62 mph in Talleyville (Brandywine Hundred) during a severe thunderstorm.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Bear (New Castle Hundred).
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in New Castle.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in the Minquadale section of New Castle Hundred. A couple of homes were damaged by the fallen trees.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees and wires in Middletown (Saint George's Hundred).
A mesonet site measured a wind gust of 58 mph during a severe thunderstorm at Saint George's Heights (Red Lion Hundred).

Chester City was also hard hit by the powerful macroburst associated with the line of severe thunderstorms. About twenty homes and buildings were condemned because of wind damage including fallen trees.  Buildings along the Avenue Of The States as well as trees within city parks were particularly hard hit. A tractor-trailer along Interstate 95 was overturned by the severe thunderstorm. the driver was not injured. Wind damage in the city was estimated at 2.5 million dollars.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees along Central School Road in Wantage Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Vernon Township.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires in Salem County, especially across the northern tier of the county.  At Noon EDT the next day, about 10,000 homes and businesses were still without power in the county.

The combination of damaging winds and lightning from a line of severe thunderstorms caused slightly more than  half of Cape May County to lose power during the evening of the 23rd. Outages were concentrated from Middle Township north through Ocean City. Power restoration was easier in the county than other places and by noon EDT the next day (24th), the number of customers without power was down to 70.

The macroburst wind damage clipped western Deptford Township and included the Deptford Mall. A vehicle was flipped by the damaging winds in the mall parking lot. Mall and store signs along Clements Bridge Road were damaged.

A severe thunderstorm caused pockets of wind damage throughout Gloucester Township. Downed trees and wires were reported in Blackwood, Grenloch and Lakeland. In the Grenloch neighborhood, 100-year-old trees were knocked over and telephone poles were snapped.  One downed tree damaged a home and two vehicles in Blackwood.

The wind damage from a powerful macroburst maximized across eastern sections of East Greenwich Township. A survey estimated peak wind gusts of 85 mph. Power poles were snapped in the area of East Chawkin Road and Paul Mills Road along Kings Highway (County Route 551) in the Clarksboro section. Shingle damage occurred to numerous homes and sheds were blown over. Many roads were impassable because of downed trees and wires. Wind damage extended to the Mantua Township border through Windsor Way and Carriage Court where one building's roof was completely destroyed. The township estimated 2,800 trees and 100 poles were knocked down.

The macroburst wind damage continued into Mantua Township. There were multiple reports of trees and wires knocked down. In addition, the roof of the township fire department building was badly damaged. Wind damage continued through the Sewell section of the township.
The macroburst wind damage continued through Wenonah Borough where numerous and massive trees including oaks were knocked down.
A severe thunderstorm knocked over a few trees in Westville Borough. One tree fell onto and damaged a pool.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Pitman Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees including one along Greentree Road in Glassboro Borough.
A Skywarn Spotter measured a wind gust of 66 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Merchantville Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Palmyra Borough.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Turnersville as well as other locations within Washington Township. At least one home was damaged by fallen trees. A Kohl's Department store sign was left dangling in a shopping center.

A severe thunderstorm caused considerable tree damage within Cherry Hill Township. Downed trees damages homes, fences and vehicles. The male driver was trapped and injured in his vehicle for forty-five minutes after trees and live wires fell around him.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in Maple Shade Township. One downed tree damaged a home.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Williamstown within Monroe Township. The squall line of severe thunderstorms caused agricultural damage in Gloucester County. Within Monroe Township, one farmer lost all of his cage free hens.
A severe thunderstorm knocked over dozens of trees in Mount Laurel Township, especially on the western side of the township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Clementon Borough.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Winslow Township, especially in the Sicklerville area. At least one downed tree damaged a home.  Poles were snapped and street lamps and and fences were knocked down. One motorist was trapped in his vehicle by downed trees.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down severeal trees in Waterford Township. A downed tree damaged a home in the Atco section of the township.
A severe thunderstorm caused considerable wind damage in Evesham Township in the Marlton area. Trees were snapped, siding ripped from some homes and sheds and fences destroyed.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and wires in Lindenwold Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down dozens of trees in Woodbury Heights. Downed trees also caused the closure of the southbound lanes of the New Jersey Turnpike in the Borough.

A severe thunderstorm hit Hammonton Township very hard and caused approximately one million dollars in property damage along with additional damage to the blueberry crop. There were dozens upon dozens of downed and uprooted trees. Trees fell on homes on Bellevue Avenue and French Street. Two buildings at the municipal airport were damaged.  The Hammonton High School roof suffered approximately 100 thousand dollars in wind damage.  The township's overland drip irrigation system that disperses its treated wastewater near the Boyer Avenue Recreational Center was damaged by downed trees. It was estimated that it would take three weeks to clear all of the fallen trees. A mesonet site measured a wind gust of 71 mph in the township.

A severe thunderstorm hit Medford Township very hard and caused approximately eight million dollars in property damage. Hundreds upon hundreds of trees were either uprooted or snapped. Three people were injured after a tree fell onto their vehicle. Another person was injured after a tree fell on their home on Mississippi Trail.  Several other people were trapped in their homes.  Some gas lines were ruptured. A firefighter suffered cardiac arrest the next day after assisting people through the night.  There were approximately 350 calls for assistance because of wind damage from the thunderstorms within the township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees in Medford Lakes Borough.  Tree damage also occurred at the Medford Lakes Country Club.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and large tree limbs in Bridgeton.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees throughout Southampton Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees throughout  Tabernacle Township. One downed tree fell onto and damaged a truck. The thunderstorm winds also damaged the roof of Seneca High School.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees in multiple locations throughout Washington Township.

The wind damage from a powerful macroburst started to cause considerable wind damage in eastern parts of Greenwich Township. This then continued farther to the southeast in Gloucester County. There were multiple reports of hundreds of trees and wires down in the Gibbstown area of the township. The roof of Saint Michael's Convent was damaged after it was lifted 10 to 15 feet into the air from the rest of the convent. The roof of a pet store also collapsed.  A tree fell through a home on Cucinotta Road. Telephone poles fell across Harmony Road.
A Skywarn Spotter estimated a wind gust of 60 mph as a severe thunderstorm moved through Swedesboro Borough.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down multiple trees in Haddonfield Township. Some trees fell across and blocked roadways.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees across Voorhees Township. Wind damage also affected the Kresson Golf Course where large trees were knocked down between the 11th and 12th holes.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees across Berlin Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Mays Landing (Hamilton Township).
A severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 69 mph in Mullica Township. Numerous trees were knocked down in the township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down numerous trees and wires in Tuckerton including along South Green Street.  The roof was also blown off the Tuckerton Beach Grille on South Green Street.
A severe thunderstorm generated a wind gust of 70 mph in Long Beach Township.
A severe thunderstorm damaged a couple of businesses in Brant Beach. Some windows were damaged. No injuries were reported.
A mesonet site reported a wind gust of 68 mph during a severe thunderstorm in Harvey Cedars. Minor wind damage occurred.

A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and caused fencing and siding damage as it moved through Little Egg Harbor Township.  The wind damage was concentrated around the intersection of Radio Road and Oak Lane.
A Weatherflow mesonet site reported a wind gust of 73 mph in Tuckerton during a severe thunderstorm.
A second different Weatherflow mesonet site reported a wind gust of 65 mph at 652 p.m. EDT in Tuckerton during the same severe thunderstorm.
A Skywarn Spotter saw a funnel cloud over Chester Township, but the circulation did not make it to the ground.
A funnel cloud was spotted near Philadelphia International Airport, but the circulation did not make it to the ground.
A Skywarn Spotter saw a funnel cloud over Jenkintown Borough, but the circulation did not make it to the ground.
A severe thunderstorm tore down power lines in Wantage Township.
A funnel cloud was sighted over West Berlin by a Skywarn Spotter. The circulation did not make it to the ground.

The combination of heavier rain and especially blocked and clogged storm drains led to a roadway closure on the Blue Route (Interstate 476) during the morning commute on the 1st. All the northbound lanes of the interstate were closed from 530 a.m. EDT to 645 a.m. EDT between exit 9 for Broomall and exit 13 for Villanova.  Heavier rain fell at the Philadelphia International Airport between 2 a.m. and 630 a.m. that morning and the event total was 1.09 inches.

A severe thunderstorm also knocked down numerous trees and wires in South Whitehall Township and caused power outages. A wind gust of 56 mph was measured at nearby Lehigh Valley International Airport.
A funnel cloud was seen over West Chester. While wind damage did occur, the funnel cloud itself did not reach the ground.
A funnel cloud was spotted over Morgantown. The funnel cloud did not touch down and cause any wind damage.
Half dollar size hail fell over Thorndale during a severe thunderstorm.
A lightning strike damaged a home's chimney on Orchard Avenue in Folsom Borough. The bricks fell to the ground, but there were no injuries.

A severe thunderstorm uprooted several trees in Mansfield Township. Janes Chapel Road was closed because of downed trees between the Mount Bethel firehouse and Pequest Road. Valley Road was also closed in the township because of downed trees, poles and transformers.
A funnel cloud was sighted over Newark.  While there was thunderstorm wind damage across the northern tier of Delaware, the circulation did not reach downward to the ground.
Heavy rain caused poor drainage flooding at the Prospect Park SEPTA commuter rail line station.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several very large trees along Willow Street in North Whitehall Township.
A funnel cloud was sighted over Upper Dublin Township. The circulation did not reach the ground and no wind damage was reported from this phenomenon.
In Tatamy Borough, Bushkill Street was closed because of downed trees caused by a severe thunderstorm. The severe thunderstorm knocked also knocked down poles along Newlins Mill Road.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down several trees and poles on the western side of Forks Township. Downed poles were reported along Bushkill Drive and Kesslerville Road.

Heavy rain during the late afternoon and early evening of the 27th forced the closure of Kelly Drive within Philadelphia. Event precipitation totals included 1.79 inches at the Northeast Philadelphia Airport and 1.34 inches at the Philadelphia International Airport.

Heavy rain during the late afternoon and early evening of the 27th forced the closure of Colwell Road in Conshohocken. Event precipitation totals included 1.90 inches in Blue Bell, 1.80 inches in Fort Washington and 1.74 inches in Bala Cynwyd.
A Paulsboro refinery was struck by lightning which caused a loss of power. The refinery then off gassed. No evacuations were needed.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a few trees in Oxford.

A series of thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in central Monroe County lasted into the early morning of July 1st. Hardest hit were Chestnuthill and Pocono Townships. The Monroe County Office of Emergency Management urged motorists to stay off the road. In Chestnuthill Township, the Pohopoco Creek flooded near Camp Jaycee. Merwinesburg Road was closed from Pennsylvania State Route 115 to Jonas Road. Ziegler Road was also closed near Jonas Road. In Pocono Township, southbound Pennsylvania State Route 611 along the Pocono Creek and near the intersection with Pennsylvania State Route 715 in Tannersville was flooded. There were mud slides in the area also. Farther south along the same creek, Warner Road (a partial wash-out) and Pennsylvania State Route 611 were also closed because of flooding. In Polk Township, Dotters Corner Road (near Dotters Creek) near Pennsylvania State Route 534 was flooded and closed. Event precipitation totals included 4.63 inches in Pocono Pines, 3.84 inches in Pocono Summit, 2.78 inches in Saylorsburg and 2.71 inches in McMichaels.

Two New Jersey state troopers avoided serious injury after their cruiser was struck by lightning in Middle Township on the afternoon of the 21st on the Garden State Parkway near mile-marker 10.9 at a construction site. One officer was taken to the Atlantic City Medical Center. The other officer did not need additional medical attention.

An EF1 tornado occurred in Tilden Township in Berks County and injured one person.  The tornado touched down near Stone Road and moved eastnortheast, passing through the Blue Mountain Academy before crossing Mountain Road into a campground area before lifting.  The most significant damage occurred to the Blue Mountain Elementary School. The roof of the school was completely removed by the tornado. The building is a total loss.  The 52-year-old principal inside the school at the time of the tornado was injured and was found covered by ceiling tiles.  Pieces of the roof were found hundreds of yards away in trees.  Hardwood trees were snapped along the tornado's path with a soybean field having debris dragged through it with visible arcing marks.  ||The estimated path length of the EF-1 tornado was three-quarters of a mile with a maximum path width of 75 yards.  The estimated maximum wind speed was 105 mph.

An EF-0 tornado occurred in eastern New Castle County in Minquadale (Brandywine Hundred).  | |The tornado touched down near a trailer park off of New Castle Avenue.  Eight units of the mobile home village and apartments on New Castle Avenue were damaged. A downed transformer went through one bedroom. Shingles and gutters were ripped from other homes. Six families were displaced and the Red Cross opened an emergency shelter at William Penn High School. The tornado damage extended eastward with a telephone pole sheered off and a tree down on Revis Avenue. Farther east, additional damage occurred on Harbor View Drive where roof damage and a wall collapse occurred at an industrial park.  Several trees were also knocked down on Dock View Drive. ||The EF-0 tornado path length was about half a mile with a maximum path width of 75 yards. The estimated maximum wind speeds were 65 mph.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down trees and wires that damaged five homes in Rehrersburg (Tulpehocken Township).
A line of severe thunderstorms tore down numerous trees and wires across the northern tier of Chester County.
Another segment of a line of severe thunderstorms tore down numerous trees and wires across the southern tier of Chester County.
A line of strong to severe thunderstorms tore down trees and wires across the northeast half of Montgomery County.
A severe thunderstorms tore down large tree limbs at the intersection of DeKalb and Germantown Pikes in Norristown.
A line of severe thunderstorms tore down trees and wires in several locations throughout Delaware County. This included one downed tree that snapped a utility pole in Media.
The gust front of a severe thunderstorm damaged the gym roof and scoreboards at DeSales University in Upper Saucon Township.
In addition to the tornado wind damage in the area, the parent severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires along Delaware State Route 9 between Lambson Lane and Terminal Avenue.
A Skywarn spotter detected a funnel cloud over Rising Sun.  It did not extend to the ground and no wind damage from it was reported.
A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees in Port Deposit.
A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees in Colora.
A severe thunderstorm tore down several trees in Centreville.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down a very large tree within Washington Square Park.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Pitman Borough.
A funnel cloud was detected over extreme southern Evesham Township.  The funnel cloud did not extend to the ground and no wind damage was reported.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires along U.S. Route 30 in Waterford Township.
A severe thunderstorm knocked down large tree limbs and wires in Washington Township.
A line of severe thunderstorms knocked down numerous trees and tree limbs in central and southern Kent County along the U.S. Route 13 corridor from Woodside to Greenwood.
A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a home in Milford. No injuries were reported.
